## File: .cursor/rules/astro-client-directives.mdc
`````
  1: ---
  2: description: Guidelines for using Astro client directives and interactive components
  3: glob_patterns:
  4:   - "src/**/*.astro"
  5:   - "src/components/**/*.tsx"
  6:   - "src/components/**/*.jsx"
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Astro 5.5
 10: 
 11: ## Client Directives
 12: 
 13: When using interactive components in Astro, always use the appropriate client directive:
 14: 
 15: - `client:load` - Component loads and hydrates immediately on page load
 16: - `client:idle` - Component loads after the page is done with its initial load and the browser's "idle callback" runs
 17: - `client:visible` - Component loads when it enters the viewport using Intersection Observer
 18: - `client:media` - Component loads when a CSS media query is met
 19: - `client:only` - Component skips server-rendering and only renders on the client
 20: 
 21: ## Best Practices
 22: 
 23: ### 1. Choose the Right Directive
 24: 
 25: ```astro
 26: <!-- For critical UI elements that need immediate interactivity -->
 27: <InteractiveComponent client:load />
 28: 
 29: <!-- For components that can wait until the page is idle -->
 30: <AccordionComponent client:idle />
 31: 
 32: <!-- For components that only need to be interactive when visible -->
 33: <LazyLoadedComponent client:visible />
 34: 
 35: <!-- For components that should only appear on certain screen sizes -->
 36: <MobileNavigation client:media="(max-width: 768px)" />
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: ### 2. Working with Shadcn/UI Components
 40: 
 41: Shadcn/UI components that require interactivity must use client directives:
 42: 
 43: ```astro
 44: ---
 45: import { Accordion } from "@/components/ui/accordion-wrapper";
 46: import { Tabs } from "@/components/ui/tabs-wrapper";
 47: ---
 48: 
 49: <!-- Use client:idle for components that don't need immediate interactivity -->
 50: <Accordion data={accordionData} client:idle />
 51: 
 52: <!-- Use client:load for critical interactive components -->
 53: <Tabs items={tabItems} client:load />
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ### 3. Wrapper Components for Complex UI
 57: 
 58: For complex Shadcn/UI components that use React context, create wrapper components:
 59: 
 60: ```tsx
 61: // src/components/ui/accordion-wrapper.tsx
 62: import {
 63:   Accordion as BaseAccordion,
 64:   AccordionContent,
 65:   AccordionItem,
 66:   AccordionTrigger,
 67: } from "@/components/ui/accordion";
 68: 
 69: interface AccordionData {
 70:   title: string;
 71:   content: string;
 72:   value: string;
 73: }
 74: 
 75: export function Accordion({ data }: { data: AccordionData[] }) {
 76:   return (
 77:     <BaseAccordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
 78:       {data.map((item) => (
 79:         <AccordionItem value={item.value} key={item.value}>
 80:           <AccordionTrigger>{item.title}</AccordionTrigger>
 81:           <AccordionContent>{item.content}</AccordionContent>
 82:         </AccordionItem>
 83:       ))}
 84:     </BaseAccordion>
 85:   );
 86: }
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ### 4. Hydration Errors Prevention
 90: 
 91: To prevent hydration errors:
 92: 
 93: - Ensure server and client render the same content
 94: - Use mounting checks for components with different server/client output
 95: - Avoid conditional rendering based on client-only APIs
 96: 
 97: ```tsx
 98: import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
 99: 
100: export function ClientComponent() {
101:   const [mounted, setMounted] = useState(false);
102:   
103:   useEffect(() => {
104:     setMounted(true);
105:   }, []);
106:   
107:   if (!mounted) {
108:     return <div>Loading...</div>; // Server-side placeholder
109:   }
110:   
111:   return <div>Client-side content</div>;
112: }
113: ```
114: 
115: ### 5. Performance Optimization
116: 
117: - Use `client:visible` for below-the-fold components
118: - Lazy load non-critical components
119: - Split large components into smaller chunks
120: - Minimize the number of hydrated components
121: 
122: ```astro
123: <!-- Only hydrate when scrolled into view -->
124: <HeavyComponent client:visible />
125: 
126: <!-- Only hydrate on larger screens -->
127: <ComplexDashboard client:media="(min-width: 1024px)" />
128: ```
129: 
130: ### 6. Common Pitfalls to Avoid
131: 
132: - **DON'T** use client directives on non-interactive components
133: - **DON'T** use `client:load` for everything (performance impact)
134: - **DON'T** forget to wrap Shadcn/UI components that use React context
135: - **DON'T** mix `className` (React) and `class` (Astro) attributes
136: - **DON'T** use browser-only APIs without checking for their existence
137: 
138: ### 7. Specific Component Guidelines
139: 
140: #### Accordion
141: 
142: ```astro
143: ---
144: import { Accordion } from "@/components/ui/accordion-wrapper";
145: 
146: const accordionData = [
147:   {
148:     title: "Is it accessible?",
149:     content: "Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.",
150:     value: "item-1"
151:   },
152:   // More items...
153: ];
154: ---
155: 
156: <Accordion data={accordionData} client:idle />
157: ```
158: 
159: #### Tabs
160: 
161: ```astro
162: ---
163: import { Tabs } from "@/components/ui/tabs-wrapper";
164: 
165: const tabItems = [
166:   {
167:     value: "tab1",
168:     label: "Tab 1",
169:     content: "Content for Tab 1"
170:   },
171:   // More tabs...
172: ];
173: ---
174: 
175: <Tabs items={tabItems} client:idle />
176: ```
177: 
178: #### Dialog/Modal
179: 
180: ```astro
181: ---
182: import { Dialog } from "@/components/ui/dialog-wrapper";
183: ---
184: 
185: <Dialog
186:   title="Important Information"
187:   description="This is important information that needs your attention."
188:   client:load
189: >
190:   <button>Open Dialog</button>
191: </Dialog>
192: ```
193: 
194: ## Testing Interactive Components
195: 
196: Always test interactive components in multiple scenarios:
197: 
198: 1. Initial page load
199: 2. After navigation
200: 3. After browser resize
201: 4. With slow network conditions
202: 5. With JavaScript temporarily disabled (for graceful degradation) 
203: 
204: To align your coding standards and rules with Astro 5.5, consider the following updates:
205: 
206: # Content Collections
207: 
208: - **Schema Definitions**: Continue using `src/content/config.ts` with `zod` for type-safe content validation.
209: - **Content Queries**: Utilize `getCollection()` for type-safe content retrieval.
210: - **Frontmatter Schemas**: Define schemas using `defineCollection`.
211: - **Single Entry Retrieval**: Employ `getEntryBySlug` for fetching individual entries.
212: - **Content Relationships**: Leverage collection references to establish relationships between content items.
213: 
214: # View Transitions
215: 
216: - **Implementation**: Use `transition:name` and `transition:animate` directives to define view transitions.
217: - **State Persistence**: Apply `transition:persist` to maintain component state during page transitions.
218: - **Animation Configuration**: Set animations with `transition:animate="slide|fade|none"`.
219: - **Event Handling**: Manage transition events using `document.addEventListener('astro:page-load')`.
220: - **Prop Preservation**: Use `transition:persist-props` to retain specific props during transitions.
221: 
222: # Islands Architecture
223: 
224: - **Immediate Interactivity**: Apply `client:load` for components requiring immediate interactivity.
225: - **Deferred Hydration**: Use `client:visible` for components that can delay hydration until visible.
226: - **Client-Only Components**: Implement `client:only` when server-side rendering is unnecessary.
227: - **Responsive Hydration**: Utilize `client:media` for components that hydrate based on media queries.
228: - **Idle Hydration**: Leverage `client:idle` for non-critical interactive components.
229: 
230: # Server-Side Features
231: 
232: - **Cookies Management**: Use `Astro.cookies` to handle server-side cookies.
233: - **Middleware**: Implement middleware with `defineMiddleware()` in `src/middleware`.
234: - **Request Access**: Access request details via `Astro.request` in server endpoints.
235: - **Dynamic Routes**: Handle dynamic routes using the `[...spread].astro` pattern.
236: - **API Endpoints**: Create API endpoints in `src/pages/api` using `Response` objects.
237: 
238: # Image Optimization
239: 
240: - **Image Component**: Use the `Image` component with `src`, `alt`, and `width/height` props.
241: - **Picture Component**: Implement the `Picture` component for art direction.
242: - **Service Configuration**: Configure the image service in `astro.config.mjs`.
243: - **Modern Formats**: Use `format="avif,webp"` for modern image formats.
244: - **Responsive Images**: Apply the `densities` prop for responsive images.
245: 
246: # Integration System
247: 
248: - **Framework Integrations**: Configure integrations in `astro.config.mjs`.
249: - **Deployment Adapters**: Use adapters like `adapter-vercel`, `adapter-netlify`, or `adapter-node` for deployment.
250: - **Vite Plugins**: Implement Vite plugins through Astro integrations.
251: - **UI Frameworks**: Configure renderers for UI frameworks as needed.
252: - **Environment Variables**: Handle integration-specific environment variables appropriately.
253: 
254: # Routing and Pages
255: 
256: - **File-Based Routing**: Place pages in `src/pages` for automatic routing.
257: - **Dynamic Parameters**: Use `[param].astro` for dynamic route parameters.
258: - **Rest Parameters**: Implement `[...spread].astro` for rest parameters in routes.
259: - **Redirects**: Handle redirects using `Astro.redirect`.
260: - **Nested Layouts**: Implement nested layouts using slot patterns.
261: 
262: # Dos
263: 
264: - **Static Path Generation**: Use `getStaticPaths` for generating static paths.
265: - **Hydration Strategies**: Implement appropriate island hydration strategies.
266: - **Type-Safe Content**: Utilize content collections for type-safe content management.
267: - **View Transitions**: Configure view transitions appropriately.
268: - **SSR Capabilities**: Leverage server-side rendering capabilities effectively.
269: 
270: # Don'ts
271: 
272: - **Overusing `client:load`**: Avoid using `client:load` when `client:visible` suffices.
273: - **Mixing SSR and `client:only`**: Never mix server-side rendering and `client:only` in the same component.
274: - **Redundant Queries**: Avoid unnecessary content collection queries.
275: - **Skipping Animations**: Don't skip view transition animations without reason.
276: - **Bypassing Image Optimization**: Never bypass Astro's image optimization features.
277: 
278: By incorporating these practices, you can effectively leverage the features introduced in Astro 5.5 to enhance your project's performance and maintainability.
`````

## File: .cursor/rules/content-collections.mdc
`````
  1: ---
  2: description: Guidelines for using Astro content collections and MDX
  3: glob_patterns:
  4:   - "src/content/**/*.md"
  5:   - "src/content/**/*.mdx"
  6:   - "src/content/config.ts"
  7:   - "src/pages/**/*.md"
  8:   - "src/pages/**/*.mdx"
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: # Content Collections and MDX Guidelines
 12: 
 13: ## Content Collections Structure
 14: 
 15: Organize content collections in a structured manner:
 16: 
 17: ```
 18: src/content/
 19: ├── blog/                # Blog posts
 20: │   ├── post-1.md
 21: │   └── post-2.mdx
 22: ├── docs/                # Documentation
 23: │   ├── getting-started/
 24: │   │   └── installation.md
 25: │   └── features/
 26: │       └── feature-1.md
 27: ├── prompts/             # AI prompts
 28: │   └── chat-prompts.md
 29: └── config.ts            # Collection configuration
 30: ```
 31: 
 32: ## Collection Configuration
 33: 
 34: Define your collections with proper typing using Zod:
 35: 
 36: ```typescript
 37: // src/content/config.ts
 38: import { defineCollection, z } from 'astro:content';
 39: 
 40: // Blog collection schema
 41: const blogCollection = defineCollection({
 42:   schema: z.object({
 43:     title: z.string(),
 44:     description: z.string(),
 45:     date: z.date(),
 46:     author: z.string().optional(),
 47:     image: z.string().optional(),
 48:     tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
 49:     draft: z.boolean().optional().default(false),
 50:   }),
 51: });
 52: 
 53: // Documentation collection schema
 54: const docsCollection = defineCollection({
 55:   schema: z.object({
 56:     title: z.string(),
 57:     description: z.string(),
 58:     section: z.string(),
 59:     order: z.number().int().positive(),
 60:     date: z.date().optional(),
 61:   }),
 62: });
 63: 
 64: // Export collections
 65: export const collections = {
 66:   'blog': blogCollection,
 67:   'docs': docsCollection,
 68: };
 69: ```
 70: 
 71: ## Frontmatter Best Practices
 72: 
 73: Use consistent frontmatter across your content:
 74: 
 75: ```markdown
 76: ---
 77: title: "Your Post Title"
 78: description: "A brief description of your post"
 79: date: 2023-04-15
 80: author: "Author Name"
 81: image: "/images/post-image.jpg"
 82: tags: ["tag1", "tag2"]
 83: draft: false
 84: ---
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: For documentation pages:
 88: 
 89: ```markdown
 90: ---
 91: title: "Feature Documentation"
 92: description: "Learn how to use this feature"
 93: section: "Features"
 94: order: 3
 95: date: 2023-04-15
 96: ---
 97: ```
 98: 
 99: ## Chat Configuration in MDX
100: 
101: For pages with AI chat capabilities:
102: 
103: ```markdown
104: ---
105: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
106: title: "Your Page Title"
107: description: "Your page description"
108: chatConfig:
109:   provider: openai
110:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
111:   temperature: 0.7
112:   maxTokens: 4000
113:   systemPrompt:
114:     - type: text
115:       text: "Define your AI assistant's role and expertise here"
116:   welcome:
117:     message: "👋 Your welcome message here"
118:     avatar: "/your-icon.svg"
119:     suggestions:
120:       - label: "First Option"
121:         prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
122: ---
123: ```
124: 
125: ## MDX Components
126: 
127: Create reusable MDX components:
128: 
129: ```tsx
130: // src/components/mdx/Callout.tsx
131: export function Callout({ type = 'info', title, children }) {
132:   return (
133:     <div className={`callout callout-${type}`}>
134:       {title && <h3>{title}</h3>}
135:       <div>{children}</div>
136:     </div>
137:   );
138: }
139: ```
140: 
141: Use them in your MDX files:
142: 
143: ```mdx
144: import { Callout } from '@/components/mdx/Callout';
145: 
146: # My MDX Page
147: 
148: <Callout type="warning" title="Important Note">
149:   This is an important warning you should pay attention to.
150: </Callout>
151: ```
152: 
153: ## Content Querying
154: 
155: Query your content collections efficiently:
156: 
157: ```astro
158: ---
159: import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';
160: 
161: // Get all blog posts
162: const allPosts = await getCollection('blog');
163: 
164: // Get published posts, sorted by date
165: const publishedPosts = allPosts
166:   .filter(post => !post.data.draft)
167:   .sort((a, b) => b.data.date.getTime() - a.data.date.getTime());
168: 
169: // Get posts with a specific tag
170: const taggedPosts = allPosts
171:   .filter(post => post.data.tags?.includes('featured'));
172: ---
173: ```
174: 
175: ## Content Rendering
176: 
177: Render content with proper metadata:
178: 
179: ```astro
180: ---
181: import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';
182: import BlogLayout from '@/layouts/BlogLayout.astro';
183: 
184: // Get a specific blog post by slug
185: export async function getStaticPaths() {
186:   const blogPosts = await getCollection('blog');
187:   
188:   return blogPosts.map(post => ({
189:     params: { slug: post.slug },
190:     props: { post },
191:   }));
192: }
193: 
194: const { post } = Astro.props;
195: const { Content } = await post.render();
196: ---
197: 
198: <BlogLayout frontmatter={post.data}>
199:   <Content />
200: </BlogLayout>
201: ```
202: 
203: ## Documentation Organization
204: 
205: Organize documentation with clear sections and ordering:
206: 
207: ```astro
208: ---
209: import { getCollection } from 'astro:content';
210: 
211: // Get all documentation pages
212: const allDocs = await getCollection('docs');
213: 
214: // Group by section
215: const docsBySection = allDocs.reduce((acc, doc) => {
216:   const section = doc.data.section;
217:   if (!acc[section]) {
218:     acc[section] = [];
219:   }
220:   acc[section].push(doc);
221:   return acc;
222: }, {});
223: 
224: // Sort each section by order
225: Object.keys(docsBySection).forEach(section => {
226:   docsBySection[section].sort((a, b) => a.data.order - b.data.order);
227: });
228: ---
229: ```
230: 
231: ## Content Styling Best Practices
232: 
233: Use consistent styling for your content:
234: 
235: ```astro
236: <style is:global>
237:   /* Base styles for markdown content */
238:   .content h1 {
239:     @apply text-3xl font-bold mb-6;
240:   }
241:   
242:   .content h2 {
243:     @apply text-2xl font-semibold mt-8 mb-4;
244:   }
245:   
246:   .content p {
247:     @apply mb-4 leading-relaxed;
248:   }
249:   
250:   .content ul, .content ol {
251:     @apply mb-4 ml-6;
252:   }
253:   
254:   .content li {
255:     @apply mb-2;
256:   }
257:   
258:   .content a {
259:     @apply text-blue-600 hover:underline;
260:   }
261:   
262:   .content blockquote {
263:     @apply border-l-4 border-gray-300 pl-4 italic my-4;
264:   }
265:   
266:   .content pre {
267:     @apply p-4 rounded-lg overflow-x-auto mb-4;
268:   }
269:   
270:   .content code {
271:     @apply font-mono text-sm;
272:   }
273: </style>
274: ```
275: 
276: ## AI-Enhanced Content
277: 
278: For pages with AI chat capabilities, structure your content to help the AI understand the topic:
279: 
280: 1. **Clear Headings**
281:    ```markdown
282:    # Main Title
283:    
284:    ## Key Section
285:    
286:    ### Subsection
287:    ```
288: 
289: 2. **Structured Information**
290:    ```markdown
291:    ## Key Points
292:    
293:    - **First Point** - Detailed explanation
294:    - **Second Point** - More details
295:    ```
296: 
297: 3. **Organized Sections**
298:    ```markdown
299:    ## Topic Area
300:    
301:    1. **Main Concept**
302:       - Detail one
303:       - Detail two
304:    
305:    2. **Another Concept**
306:       - More information
307:       - Additional details
308:    ```
309: 
310: ## Performance Optimization
311: 
312: Optimize your content for performance:
313: 
314: - Use responsive images with proper dimensions
315: - Lazy load images below the fold
316: - Minimize the use of heavy components in MDX
317: - Use appropriate image formats (WebP, AVIF)
318: - Implement proper caching strategies
`````

  6: 
  7: # Content Management and MDX Guidelines
  8: 
  9: Rules for managing content and using MDX in the ONE framework.
 10: 
 11: ## Content Collections
 12: 
 13: ### Structure
 14: - Organize content in `src/content/` directory.
 15: - Group related content in collections (e.g., `blog`, `docs`, `prompts`).
 16: - Use consistent file naming conventions.
 17: 
 18: ### Frontmatter
 19: - Include required metadata in frontmatter:
 20:   - `title`: The content title
 21:   - `description`: A brief description
 22:   - `date`: Publication date (YYYY-MM-DD format)
 23:   - `section`: Content section or category
 24:   - `order`: Numerical order for sorting (if applicable)
 25: 
 26: ### Example

 30: description: Learn how to get started with ONE framework
 31: date: 2024-02-01
 32: section: Introduction
 33: order: 1
 34: ---
 35: 
 36: # Getting Started with ONE
 37: 
 38: Content goes here...
 39: ```

 41: ## MDX Usage
 42:

## File: .cursor/rules/project-guidelines.mdc
`````
  1: ---
  2: description: ONE Framework Project Guidelines
  3: globs: src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,astro,md,mdx}
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: # ONE Framework Project Guidelines
  7: 
  8: General guidelines for all code in the ONE framework project.
  9: 
 10: ## Project Structure
 11: 
 12: ### Directory Organization
 13: - `src/components/`: UI components
 14:   - `ui/`: Shadcn/UI components
 15:   - `chat/`: Chat-related components
 16:   - `magicui/`: Enhanced UI components
 17: - `src/content/`: Content collections
 18:   - `blog/`: Blog posts
 19:   - `docs/`: Documentation
 20:   - `prompts/`: AI prompts
 21: - `src/hooks/`: React hooks
 22: - `src/layouts/`: Page layouts
 23: - `src/lib/`: Utility functions
 24: - `src/pages/`: Routes and pages
 25:   - `api/`: API endpoints
 26: - `src/schema/`: Data schemas
 27: - `src/stores/`: State management
 28: - `src/styles/`: Global styles
 29: - `src/types/`: TypeScript types
 30: 
 31: ## Coding Standards
 32: 
 33: ### General
 34: - Use TypeScript for type safety.
 35: - Follow consistent naming conventions.
 36: - Write clear, concise comments.
 37: - Keep functions small and focused.
 38: - Use meaningful variable names.
 39: - Avoid magic numbers and strings.
 40: 
 41: ### TypeScript
 42: - Use explicit types for function parameters and return values.
 43: - Leverage TypeScript's type inference when appropriate.
 44: - Define interfaces for complex objects.
 45: - Use type guards for runtime type checking.
 46: - Prefer interfaces over type aliases for object types.
 47: 
 48: ### Imports
 49: - Use absolute imports with `@/` prefix.
 50: - Group imports by type:
 51:   1. External libraries
 52:   2. Internal components/utilities
 53:   3. Types
 54:   4. Styles
 55: - Sort imports alphabetically within groups.
 56: 
 57: ### Example
 58: ```typescript
 59: // External libraries
 60: import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
 61: import { z } from 'zod';
 62: 
 63: // Internal components/utilities
 64: import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
 65: import { cn } from '@/lib/utils';
 66: 
 67: // Types
 68: import type { User } from '@/types/user';
 69: 
 70: // Styles
 71: import '@/styles/component.css';
 72: ```
 73: 
 74: ## Zod Schema Usage
 75: 
 76: ### Schema Definition
 77: - Define schemas in dedicated files in `src/schema/`.
 78: - Export both the schema and inferred type.
 79: - Use descriptive names for schemas.
 80: 
 81: ### Example
 82: ```typescript
 83: import { z } from 'zod';
 84: 
 85: export const UserSchema = z.object({
 86:   id: z.string().uuid(),
 87:   name: z.string().min(1),
 88:   email: z.string().email(),
 89:   role: z.enum(['user', 'admin']),
 90:   createdAt: z.date(),
 91: });
 92: 
 93: export type User = z.infer<typeof UserSchema>;
 94: ```
 95: 
 96: ### Validation
 97: - Use schema parsing for runtime validation.
 98: - Handle validation errors gracefully.
 99: - Provide helpful error messages.
100: 
101: ## Performance Considerations
102: 
103: ### Astro Optimization
104: - Use static rendering when possible.
105: - Minimize client-side JavaScript.
106: - Use partial hydration with client directives.
107: - Leverage Astro's content collections for structured content.
108: 
109: ### React Optimization
110: - Memoize expensive calculations.
111: - Use proper dependency arrays in hooks.
112: - Avoid unnecessary re-renders.
113: - Implement code splitting for large components.
114: 
115: ### Image Optimization
116: - Use Astro's built-in image optimization.
117: - Specify width and height attributes.
118: - Use responsive images with srcset.
119: - Lazy load images below the fold.
120: 
121: ## Documentation
122: 
123: ### Code Documentation
124: - Use JSDoc comments for functions and components.
125: - Document parameters, return values, and side effects.
126: - Include examples for complex functions.
127: - Keep documentation up-to-date with code changes.
128: 
129: ### Example
130: ```typescript
131: /**
132:  * Formats a date in a localized format.
133:  * @param date - The date to format
134:  * @param locale - The locale to use (defaults to browser locale)
135:  * @param options - Intl.DateTimeFormat options
136:  * @returns Formatted date string
137:  * @example
138:  * formatDate(new Date(), 'en-US', { dateStyle: 'full' })
139:  * // => "Wednesday, February 21, 2024"
140:  */
141: export function formatDate(
142:   date: Date,
143:   locale?: string,
144:   options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions
145: ): string {
146:   return new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, options).format(date);
147: }
148: ```
149: 
150: ## Best Practices
151: 
152: ### Accessibility
153: - Use semantic HTML elements.
154: - Include proper ARIA attributes.
155: - Ensure keyboard navigation works.
156: - Maintain proper color contrast.
157: - Test with screen readers.
158: 
159: ### Security
160: - Validate user input.
161: - Sanitize data before rendering.
162: - Implement proper authentication and authorization.
163: - Follow security best practices for API endpoints.
164: - Keep dependencies updated.
165: 
166: ### Testing
167: - Write unit tests for critical functionality.
168: - Test components for accessibility.
169: - Implement end-to-end tests for critical user flows.
170: - Use test-driven development when appropriate.
171: 
172: ### Version Control
173: - Write clear, descriptive commit messages.
174: - Use feature branches for new development.
175: - Keep pull requests focused and manageable.
176: - Review code before merging.
177: - Maintain a clean git history.
`````

## File: .cursor/rules/react-component-guidelines.mdc
`````
  1: ---
  2: description: React Component Guidelines for ONE Framework
  3: globs: src/components/**/*.{tsx,jsx}
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: # React Component Guidelines
  7: 
  8: Rules for writing consistent React components within the ONE framework.
  9: 
 10: ## Structure
 11: - Use functional components with arrow functions.
 12: - Avoid class components unless absolutely necessary.
 13: - Keep components small and focused on a single responsibility.
 14: - Use TypeScript for type safety.
 15: 
 16: ## Props
 17: - Define prop types with TypeScript interfaces.
 18: - Use descriptive prop names.
 19: - Provide default values for optional props using destructuring.
 20: - Use the `children` prop for component composition.
 21: 
 22: ## Example
 23: Here's a compliant React component:
 24: 
 25: ```tsx
 26: interface ButtonProps {
 27:   variant?: 'default' | 'primary' | 'secondary' | 'outline';
 28:   size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg';
 29:   children: React.ReactNode;
 30:   onClick?: () => void;
 31:   disabled?: boolean;
 32: }
 33: 
 34: const Button = ({
 35:   variant = 'default',
 36:   size = 'md',
 37:   children,
 38:   onClick,
 39:   disabled = false,
 40: }: ButtonProps) => {
 41:   return (
 42:     <button
 43:       className={cn(
 44:         "rounded-md font-medium transition-colors",
 45:         {
 46:           'bg-primary text-primary-foreground': variant === 'primary',
 47:           'bg-secondary text-secondary-foreground': variant === 'secondary',
 48:           'border border-input bg-background': variant === 'outline',
 49:           'px-2 py-1 text-sm': size === 'sm',
 50:           'px-4 py-2': size === 'md',
 51:           'px-6 py-3 text-lg': size === 'lg',
 52:           'opacity-50 cursor-not-allowed': disabled
 53:         }
 54:       )}
 55:       onClick={onClick}
 56:       disabled={disabled}
 57:     >
 58:       {children}
 59:     </button>
 60:   );
 61: };
 62: ```
 63: 
 64: ## Styling
 65: - Use Tailwind CSS for styling.
 66: - Use the `cn()` utility for conditional class names.
 67: - Follow the Shadcn/UI component patterns.
 68: - Use CSS variables for theming when appropriate.
 69: - Always use `className` (not `class`) for React components.
 70: 
 71: ## Hooks
 72: - Follow the Rules of Hooks.
 73: - Create custom hooks for reusable logic.
 74: - Keep hooks small and focused.
 75: - Name hooks with the `use` prefix.
 76: 
 77: ## State Management
 78: - Use React's built-in state management (useState, useReducer) for component-level state.
 79: - Consider context for shared state between components.
 80: - Avoid prop drilling by using composition or context.
 81: 
 82: ## Performance
 83: - Memoize expensive calculations with useMemo.
 84: - Optimize event handlers with useCallback.
 85: - Use React.memo for pure components that render often.
 86: - Implement proper dependency arrays in useEffect.
 87: 
 88: ## Client Directives
 89: - Use appropriate Astro client directives:
 90:   - `client:load`: Component loads immediately.
 91:   - `client:idle`: Component loads when the browser is idle.
 92:   - `client:visible`: Component loads when it enters the viewport.
 93:   - `client:only`: Component only renders on the client.
 94: 
 95: ## Accessibility
 96: - Use semantic HTML elements.
 97: - Include proper ARIA attributes.
 98: - Ensure keyboard navigation works.
 99: - Maintain proper focus management.
100: - Test with screen readers.
101: 
102: ## File Organization
103: - Place components in `src/components/`.
104: - Use subdirectories for related components.
105: - Follow naming conventions: PascalCase for component files.
106: - Export components as named exports from index files for better imports.
`````

## File: .cursor/rules/shadcn-ui-guidelines.mdc
`````
  1: ---
  2: description: Shadcn/UI and Tailwind CSS Guidelines
  3: globs: src/components/ui/**/*.{tsx,jsx}
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: # Shadcn/UI and Tailwind CSS Guidelines
  7: 
  8: Rules for consistent usage of Shadcn/UI components and Tailwind CSS in the ONE framework.
  9: 
 10: ## Shadcn/UI Components
 11: 
 12: ### Installation
 13: - Use pnpm to add Shadcn/UI components:
 14:   ```bash
 15:   pnpm shadcn-ui@latest add [component-name]
 16:   ```
 17: - Components should be installed in `src/components/ui/`.
 18: 
 19: ### Usage
 20: - Import components from `@/components/ui/`.
 21: - Follow the component documentation for proper usage.
 22: - Use the component's props API as documented.
 23: - Avoid modifying the core component files directly.
 24: 
 25: ### Customization
 26: - Customize components through the `components.json` configuration.
 27: - Use the `cn()` utility for conditional class names.
 28: - Extend components by composition rather than modification.
 29: 
 30: ## Tailwind CSS
 31: 
 32: ### Class Organization
 33: - Use consistent class ordering:
 34:   1. Layout (display, position)
 35:   2. Box model (width, height, margin, padding)
 36:   3. Typography (font, text)
 37:   4. Visual (colors, backgrounds, borders)
 38:   5. Other (animations, transitions)
 39: 
 40: ### Example
 41: ```tsx
 42: <div className="
 43:   flex items-center justify-between
 44:   w-full h-16 px-4
 45:   text-sm font-medium
 46:   bg-background border-b
 47:   transition-all
 48: ">
 49:   {/* Content */}
 50: </div>
 51: ```
 52: 
 53: ### Responsive Design
 54: - Use Tailwind's responsive prefixes: `sm:`, `md:`, `lg:`, `xl:`, `2xl:`.
 55: - Design for mobile-first, then add responsive classes.
 56: - Use consistent breakpoints across the application.
 57: 
 58: ### Dark Mode
 59: - Use the `dark:` variant for dark mode styles.
 60: - Ensure proper contrast in both light and dark modes.
 61: - Test all components in both modes.
 62: 
 63: ### Custom Utilities
 64: - Define custom utilities in `tailwind.config.mjs`.
 65: - Use CSS variables for theming in `src/styles/global.css`.
 66: - Follow the naming convention of existing variables.
 67: 
 68: ## Component Examples
 69: 
 70: ### Button Component
 71: ```tsx
 72: import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
 73: 
 74: // Basic usage
 75: <Button>Click me</Button>
 76: 
 77: // With variants
 78: <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Small Outline</Button>
 79: 
 80: // With icon
 81: <Button>
 82:   <PlusIcon className="mr-2 h-4 w-4" />
 83:   Add Item
 84: </Button>
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: ### Dialog Component
 88: ```tsx
 89: import {
 90:   Dialog,
 91:   DialogContent,
 92:   DialogDescription,
 93:   DialogHeader,
 94:   DialogTitle,
 95:   DialogTrigger,
 96: } from "@/components/ui/dialog";
 97: 
 98: <Dialog>
 99:   <DialogTrigger asChild>
100:     <Button variant="outline">Open Dialog</Button>
101:   </DialogTrigger>
102:   <DialogContent className="sm:max-w-[425px]">
103:     <DialogHeader>
104:       <DialogTitle>Edit Profile</DialogTitle>
105:       <DialogDescription>
106:         Make changes to your profile here.
107:       </DialogDescription>
108:     </DialogHeader>
109:     {/* Dialog content */}
110:   </DialogContent>
111: </Dialog>
112: ```
113: 
114: ## Best Practices
115: - Use semantic HTML elements within components.
116: - Maintain consistent spacing using Tailwind's spacing scale.
117: - Use Tailwind's color palette for consistency.
118: - Leverage Shadcn/UI's composition pattern for complex components.
119: - Test components for accessibility and responsiveness.
`````

## File: src/1/build/api/api.md
`````markdown
  1: # ONE API Documentation
  2: 
  3: The ONE API provides a unified interface for executing capabilities through HTTP endpoints.
  4: 
  5: ## Base URL
  6: 
  7: - Production: `https://one.ie/api/1`
  8: - Development: `http://localhost:1111/api/1`
  9: 
 10: ## Authentication
 11: 
 12: Currently, the API is open and does not require authentication.
 13: 
 14: ## Response Format
 15: 
 16: All API responses follow this format:
 17: 
 18: ```typescript
 19: {
 20:   status: number;    // HTTP status code
 21:   message: string;   // Response message
 22:   data: unknown;     // Response data
 23:   _one: {
 24:     version: string;   // ONE version
 25:     timestamp: string; // ISO timestamp
 26:     path: string;      // API path
 27:   }
 28: }
 29: ```
 30: 
 31: ## Endpoints
 32: 
 33: ### Execute Capability
 34: 
 35: Execute a ONE capability through the API.
 36: 
 37: #### `GET /{capability}`
 38: 
 39: Execute a capability without parameters.
 40: 
 41: **Parameters:**
 42: - `capability` (path) - The name of the capability to execute
 43: 
 44: **Response:**
 45: ```json
 46: {
 47:   "status": 200,
 48:   "message": "Success",
 49:   "data": { ... },
 50:   "_one": {
 51:     "version": "1.0.0",
 52:     "timestamp": "2024-03-19T12:00:00Z",
 53:     "path": "chat"
 54:   }
 55: }
 56: ```
 57: 
 58: #### `POST /{capability}`
 59: 
 60: Execute a capability with parameters.
 61: 
 62: **Parameters:**
 63: - `capability` (path) - The name of the capability to execute
 64: - Request body (JSON) - Capability parameters
 65: 
 66: **Example:**
 67: ```bash
 68: curl -X POST https://one.ie/api/1/chat \
 69:   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 70:   -d '{"message": "Hello ONE!"}'
 71: ```
 72: 
 73: **Response:**
 74: ```json
 75: {
 76:   "status": 200,
 77:   "message": "Success",
 78:   "data": {
 79:     "response": "Hello! How can I assist you today?"
 80:   },
 81:   "_one": {
 82:     "version": "1.0.0",
 83:     "timestamp": "2024-03-19T12:00:00Z",
 84:     "path": "chat"
 85:   }
 86: }
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ## Error Handling
 90: 
 91: Errors return appropriate HTTP status codes and follow the standard response format:
 92: 
 93: ```json
 94: {
 95:   "status": 400,
 96:   "message": "Invalid request: Missing required parameter",
 97:   "data": null,
 98:   "_one": {
 99:     "version": "1.0.0",
100:     "timestamp": "2024-03-19T12:00:00Z",
101:     "path": "error"
102:   }
103: }
104: ```
105: 
106: Common status codes:
107: - `200` - Success
108: - `400` - Invalid request
109: - `404` - Capability not found
110: - `500` - Internal server error
111: 
112: ## CORS
113: 
114: The API supports CORS with the following headers:
115: - `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`
116: - `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS`
117: - `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type`
`````

## File: src/1/build/database/database.docs.md
`````markdown
 1: Drizzle ORM is a TypeScript-first Object Relational Mapping (ORM) library designed for SQL databases, emphasizing type safety and developer productivity. It offers a flexible and efficient way to interact with databases using TypeScript.
 2: 
 3: Supabase is an open-source platform that provides a suite of tools to build secure and performant backends, including a PostgreSQL database, authentication, and real-time subscriptions. It serves as an alternative to Firebase, offering a comprehensive backend solution with minimal configuration.
 4: 
 5: Integrating Drizzle ORM with Supabase allows developers to leverage Drizzle's type-safe querying capabilities while utilizing Supabase's robust backend services. This combination enables efficient database interactions with enhanced type safety and access to Supabase's features.
 6: 
 7: **Getting Started with Drizzle ORM and Supabase:**
 8: 
 9: 1. **Install Dependencies:**
10:    Begin by installing Drizzle ORM and the necessary PostgreSQL driver:
11:    ```bash
12:    npm install drizzle-orm postgres
13:    npm install --save-dev drizzle-kit
14:    ```
15: 
16: 2. **Configure Environment Variables:**
17:    Create a `.env` file in your project root and add your Supabase database connection URL:
18:    ```
19:    DATABASE_URL=your_supabase_database_url
20:    ```
21: 
22: 3. **Set Up Drizzle ORM:**
23:    Create a `drizzle.config.ts` file in your project root with the following content:
24:    ```typescript
25:    import { defineConfig } from 'drizzle-kit';
26: 
27:    export default defineConfig({
28:      schema: './src/db/schema.ts',
29:      out: './supabase/migrations',
30:      dialect: 'postgresql',
31:      dbCredentials: {
32:        url: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
33:      },
34:    });
35:    ```
36: 
37: 4. **Define Your Schema:**
38:    In the `src/db/schema.ts` file, define your database tables using Drizzle's schema definition:
39:    ```typescript
40:    import { pgTable, serial, text, varchar } from 'drizzle-orm/pg-core';
41: 
42:    export const users = pgTable('users', {
43:      id: serial('id').primaryKey(),
44:      fullName: text('full_name'),
45:      phone: varchar('phone', { length: 256 }),
46:    });
47:    ```
48: 
49: 5. **Generate and Apply Migrations:**
50:    Use Drizzle Kit to generate and apply migrations:
51:    ```bash
52:    npx drizzle-kit generate
53:    npx drizzle-kit migrate
54:    ```
55: 
56: 6. **Connect to the Database:**
57:    In your application code, connect to the Supabase database using Drizzle ORM:
58:    ```typescript
59:    import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/postgres-js';
60:    import postgres from 'postgres';
61: 
62:    const client = postgres(process.env.DATABASE_URL);
63:    const db = drizzle({ client });
64:    ```
`````

`````markdown
  1: Let's break this down into a strategic approach. Given your goals, here's what I recommend:
  2: 
  3: 1. **Start with Core Foundation (Website First)**
  4: ```typescript:1/1.ts
  5: // Core system that everything builds upon
  6: export class ONE {
  7:   version = '1.0.0'
  8:   
  9:   // System-wide configuration
 10:   config = {
 11:     mode: 'development',
 12:     baseUrl: '/',
 13:     debug: true
 14:   }
 15: 
 16:   // Core initialization
 17:   constructor() {
 18:     this.init()
 19:   }
 20: 
 21:   private init() {
 22:     // Initialize core systems
 23:   }
 24: }
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: 
 28: 
 29: Sequence
 30: 1. Website First:
 31:    - Gives us a visual interface to work with
 32:    - Provides immediate feedback
 33:    - Can watch the system grow
 34:    - Tests our blocks
 35: 
 36: 2. Collect:
 37:    - Allows us to gather data from existing sites
 38:    - Builds our knowledge base
 39:    - Provides training data for agents
 40:    - Tests our data structures
 41: 
 42: 3. Then Agents:
 43:    - Built with real data
 44:    - Have a UI to interact with
 45:    - Can see their effects
 46:    - Can be tested against real scenarios
 47: 
 48: **Initial Focus:**
 49: ```typescript:1/1.tsx
 50: import { ONE } from '../1'
 51: import { Layout, Card, Button } from '../blocks'
 52: 
 53: export default function App() {
 54:   return (
 55:     <Layout>
 56:       <Card>
 57:         <h2>Agents</h2>
 58:         {/* System metrics */}
 59:       </Card>
 60:       <Card>
 61:         <h2>Traffic</h2>
 62:         {/* Collection controls */}
 63:       </Card>
 64:       <Card>
 65:         <h2>Sales</h2>
 66:         {/* Future agent metrics */}
 67:       </Card>
 68:     </Layout>
 69:   )
 70: }
 71: ```
 72: 
 73: This approach:
 74: 1. Builds foundation first
 75: 2. Creates immediate value
 76: 3. Makes development visible
 77: 4. Enables iterative improvement
 78: 5. Keeps motivation high
 79: 
 80: The complete process of creating an Astro website based on your todo list and the ONE system architecture. Here's a structured approach:
 81: 
 82: ```mermaid
 83: graph TD
 84:     A[Initial Setup] --> B[UI Components]
 85:     B --> C[Layout & Structure]
 86:     C --> D[Core Pages]
 87:     D --> E[State Management]
 88:     E --> F[Styling]
 89:     F --> G[Documentation]
 90:     G --> H[Testing]
 91:     H --> I[Performance]
 92:     I --> J[Deployment]
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: Let's break down each phase with specific tasks and code examples:
 96: 
 97: ## 1. Initial Setup
 98: 
 99: ```bash
100: # Clone the ONE template
101: git fork https://github.com/one-ie/one.git
102: 
103: # Install core dependencies
104: pnpm add @astrojs/react @astrojs/tailwind tailwindcss
105: pnpm add -D @types/react @types/react-dom
106: pnpm add lucide-react class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge
107: 
108: # Configure Astro
109: ```
110: 
111: ````typescript:astro.config.mjs
112: import { defineConfig } from 'astro'
113: import react from '@astrojs/react'
114: import tailwind from '@astrojs/tailwind'
115: 
116: export default defineConfig({
117:   integrations: [react(), tailwind()],
118:   output: 'server'
119: })
120: ````
121: 
122: ## 2. UI Components Setup
123: 
124: ```bash
125: # Initialize shadcn-ui
126: pnpm dlx shadcn-ui@latest init
127: ```
128: 
129: ````typescript:src/components/ui/button.tsx
130: // Add core components one by one
131: pnpm dlx shadcn-ui@latest add button
132: pnpm dlx shadcn-ui@latest add card
133: pnpm dlx shadcn-ui@latest add dropdown
134: // ... etc
135: ````
136: 
137: ## 3. Layout & Structure
138: 
139: ````astro:src/layouts/Layout.astro
140: ---
141: import { ViewTransitions } from 'astro:transitions'
142: import { ThemeProvider } from '@/components/theme-provider'
143: ---
144: 
145: <html lang="en">
146:   <head>
147:     <meta charset="utf-8" />
148:     <ViewTransitions />
149:   </head>
150:   <body>
151:     <ThemeProvider>
152:       <slot />
153:     </ThemeProvider>
154:   </body>
155: </html>
156: ````
157: 
158: ## 4. Core Pages
159: 
160: ````astro:src/pages/index.astro
161: ---
162: import Layout from '@/layouts/Layout.astro'
163: import { ONE } from '@/1'
164: import Page from index.json
165: import { Hero } from '@/components/Hero'
166: import { Features } from '@/components/Features'
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: <Layout>
171:   <Hero />
172:   <Features />
173: </Layout>
174: ````

176: ## 5. State Management
177: 
178: ````typescript:src/lib/store/theme.ts
179: import { atom } from 'nanostores'
180: 
181: export const themeStore = atom<'light' | 'dark'>('light')
182: 
183: export function toggleTheme() {
184:   themeStore.set(themeStore.get() === 'light' ? 'dark' : 'light')
185: }
186: ````
187: 
188: ## 6. Styling
189: 
190: ````css:src/styles/globals.css
191: @tailwind base;
192: @tailwind components;
193: @tailwind utilities;
194:  
195: @layer base {

197:     --background: 0 0% 100%;

201: }

208: title: Getting Started
209: description: Learn how to get started with our platform
210: ---
211: 
212: # Getting Started
213: 
214: Welcome to our documentation...
215: ````
216: 
217: ## 8. Testing
218: 
219: ````typescript:src/components/Button.test.ts
220: import { test, expect } from 'vitest'
221: import { render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
222: import { Button } from './Button'
223: 
224: test('Button renders correctly', () => {
225:   render(<Button>Click me</Button>)
226:   expect(screen.getByRole('button')).toBeInTheDocument()
227: })
228: ````
229: 
230: ## 9. Performance
231: 
232: ````typescript:src/middleware.ts
233: import { defineMiddleware } from 'astro:middleware'
234: 
235: export const onRequest = defineMiddleware(async (context, next) => {
236:   // Add caching headers
237:   context.response.headers.set('Cache-Control', 'max-age=3600')
238:   return await next()
239: })
240: ````
241: 
242: ## 10. Deployment
243: 
244: ````yaml:vercel.json
245: {
246:   "buildCommand": "pnpm build",
247:   "outputDirectory": "dist",
248:   "framework": "astro",
249:   "regions": ["sfo1"]
250: }
251: ````
252: 
253: ## Key Checkpoints
254: 
255: 1. **After Initial Setup**
256:    - Verify Astro config is correct
257:    - Test TypeScript compilation
258:    - Confirm dependencies are installed
259: 
260: 2. **After UI Setup**
261:    - Test component library integration
262:    - Verify theme switching works
263:    - Check component styling
264: 
265: 3. **After Layout Implementation**
266:    - Test view transitions
267:    - Verify responsive design
268:    - Check meta tags
269: 
270: 4. **Before Deployment**
271:    - Run performance audits
272:    - Complete test coverage
273:    - Verify build process
274: 
275: ## Best Practices
276: 
277: 1. **File Organization**
278:    - Keep components in logical groups
279:    - Use index files for clean exports
280:    - Maintain consistent naming
281: 
282: 2. **Performance**
283:    - Use partial hydration wisely
284:    - Optimize images
285:    - Implement proper caching
286: 
287: 3. **Development Flow**
288:    - Use Git for version control
289:    - Follow component-driven development
290:    - Write tests as you build
291: 
292: This process follows the ONE system's principles of organized, systematic development while leveraging Astro's powerful features for optimal performance and developer experience.
`````

## File: src/1/think/map/map.cjs
`````
 1: // Map System for ONE
 2: // =================
 3: 
 4: const fs = require('fs');
 5: const path = require('path');
 6: 
 7: const ONE_MAP = {
 8:   core: {
 9:     '1.ts': 'Core ONE system',
10:     '1.yaml': 'Configuration file',
11:     '1.html': 'Base HTML template',
12:     '1.log': 'System logs'
13:   },
14:   
15:   api: {
16:     '1.ts': 'Main API endpoint',
17:     '1.test.ts': 'API test endpoint',
18:     '1.yaml': 'API configuration'
19:   },
20:   
21:   system: {
22:     'monitor.ts': 'System monitoring',
23:     'registry.ts': 'Capability registry',
24:     'test.ts': 'Testing system',
25:     'map.cjs': 'File mapping'
26:   }
27: };
28: 
29: function generateFileMap(dir = '1') {
30:   const items = fs.readdirSync(dir);
31:   const map = {};
32: 
33:   for (const item of items) {
34:     const fullPath = path.join(dir, item);
35:     const stat = fs.statSync(fullPath);
36: 
37:     if (stat.isDirectory()) {
38:       map[item] = generateFileMap(fullPath);
39:     } else {
40:       map[item] = {
41:         size: stat.size,
42:         modified: stat.mtime,
43:         description: ONE_MAP.core[item] || 
44:                     ONE_MAP.api[item] || 
45:                     ONE_MAP.system[item] || 
46:                     'Additional file'
47:       };
48:     }
49:   }
50: 
51:   return map;
52: }
53: 
54: module.exports = {
55:   ONE_MAP,
56:   generateFileMap,
57:   
58:   // Generate current map
59:   get current() {
60:     return generateFileMap();
61:   },
62:   
63:   // Get file description
64:   getDescription(file) {
65:     const [category, name] = file.split('/');
66:     return ONE_MAP[category]?.[name] || 'Additional file';
67:   }
68: };
`````

## File: src/1/think/memory/memory.md
`````markdown
  1: # Memory System Documentation
  2: 
  3: The memory system is a core component of ONE's think system, providing persistent and ephemeral storage with semantic search capabilities.
  4: 
  5: ## Architecture
  6: 
  7: ```
  8: /1/think/memory/           # Memory subsystem root
  9: ├── 1.ts                   # Core types & schemas
 10: ├── manager.ts             # Memory management
 11: ├── hooks.ts              # React hooks
 12: ├── memory.md             # This documentation
 13: │
 14: └── store/                # Storage implementations
 15:     ├── 1.ts             # Store interface
 16:     ├── nano.ts          # Nanostore (local)
 17:     ├── supabase.ts      # Supabase (vector)
 18:     └── pg.ts            # PostgreSQL (persistent)
 19: ```
 20: 
 21: ## Core Components
 22: 
 23: ### 1. Memory Types
 24: 
 25: ```typescript
 26: // Core memory content types
 27: const MemoryContent = z.union([
 28:   z.object({ type: z.literal('text'), value: z.string() }),
 29:   z.object({ type: z.literal('code'), value: z.string(), language: z.string() }),
 30:   z.object({ type: z.literal('image'), url: z.string().url() }),
 31:   z.object({ type: z.literal('structured'), data: z.record(z.unknown()) })
 32: ])
 33: 
 34: // Memory schema
 35: const MemorySchema = z.object({
 36:   id: z.string().uuid(),
 37:   type: z.enum(['thought', 'experience', 'knowledge', 'connection']),
 38:   content: MemoryContent,
 39:   metadata: z.object({
 40:     timestamp: z.date(),
 41:     source: z.string(),
 42:     confidence: z.number().min(0).max(1),
 43:     embedding: z.array(z.number()).optional(),
 44:     tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
 45:     context: z.record(z.unknown()).optional(),
 46:   }),
 47:   relations: z.array(z.string().uuid()).default([]),
 48:   ttl: z.number().optional(),
 49: })
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ### 2. Storage Layer
 53: 
 54: The memory system uses a multi-tiered storage approach:
 55: 
 56: 1. **Local Storage (Nanostore)**
 57:    - Fast access for active memories
 58:    - In-memory caching
 59:    - Reactive state updates
 60: 
 61: 2. **Vector Storage (Supabase)**
 62:    - Semantic search capabilities
 63:    - Embedding storage
 64:    - Similarity queries
 65: 
 66: 3. **Persistent Storage (PostgreSQL)**
 67:    - Long-term memory storage
 68:    - Relationship management
 69:    - Complex queries
 70: 
 71: ## Core Operations
 72: 
 73: ### 1. Memory Storage
 74: 
 75: ```typescript
 76: // Store new memory
 77: async function store(memory: Memory): Promise<boolean> {
 78:   try {
 79:     // Generate embedding if needed
 80:     if (typeof memory.content === 'string') {
 81:       memory.metadata.embedding = await generateEmbedding(memory.content)
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     // Store in all layers
 85:     await Promise.all([
 86:       localStore.set(memory.id, memory),
 87:       vectorStore.store(memory),
 88:       persistentStore.save(memory)
 89:     ])
 90: 
 91:     return true
 92:   } catch (error) {
 93:     console.error('Failed to store memory:', error)
 94:     return false
 95:   }
 96: }
 97: ```
 98: 
 99: ### 2. Memory Recall
100: 
101: ```typescript
102: // Recall similar memories
103: async function recall(query: string, options?: RecallOptions): Promise<Memory[]> {
104:   try {
105:     // Generate query embedding
106:     const embedding = await generateEmbedding(query)
107: 
108:     // Search vector store
109:     const results = await vectorStore.search(embedding, options?.limit || 5)
110: 
111:     // Enrich results with relationships
112:     return await enrichMemories(results)
113:   } catch (error) {
114:     console.error('Failed to recall memories:', error)
115:     return []
116:   }
117: }
118: ```
119: 
120: ### 3. Memory Management
121: 
122: ```typescript
123: // Connect related memories
124: async function connect(sourceId: string, targetId: string): Promise<boolean> {
125:   try {
126:     const [source, target] = await Promise.all([
127:       persistentStore.get(sourceId),
128:       persistentStore.get(targetId)
129:     ])
130: 
131:     if (!source || !target) return false
132: 
133:     // Update relationships
134:     source.relations.push(targetId)
135:     target.relations.push(sourceId)
136: 
137:     // Save updates
138:     await Promise.all([
139:       persistentStore.save(source),
140:       persistentStore.save(target)
141:     ])
142: 
143:     return true
144:   } catch (error) {
145:     console.error('Failed to connect memories:', error)
146:     return false
147:   }
148: }
149: ```
150: 
151: ## React Integration
152: 
153: The memory system provides React hooks for easy integration:
154: 
155: ```typescript
156: function MemoryComponent() {
157:   const { memories, operations, store, recall } = useMemory()
158: 
159:   // Store new memory
160:   const saveMemory = async () => {
161:     await store({
162:       type: 'knowledge',
163:       content: {
164:         type: 'text',
165:         value: 'Important information'
166:       },
167:       metadata: {
168:         timestamp: new Date(),
169:         source: 'user',
170:         confidence: 1.0,
171:         tags: ['important']
172:       }
173:     })
174:   }
175: 
176:   // Loading states
177:   if (operations.store?.loading) {
178:     return <div>Storing memory...</div>
179:   }
180: 
181:   return (
182:     <div>
183:       <button onClick={saveMemory}>Store Memory</button>
184:       {operations.store?.error && (
185:         <div className="error">
186:           Failed to store memory: {operations.store.error.message}
187:         </div>
188:       )}
189:     </div>
190:   )
191: }
192: ```
193: 
194: ## Database Schema
195: 
196: ```sql
197: -- Memory table
198: CREATE TABLE memories (
199:   id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
200:   type TEXT NOT NULL,
201:   content JSONB NOT NULL,
202:   metadata JSONB NOT NULL,
203:   relations TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}',
204:   embedding vector(1536),
205:   created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW(),
206:   expires_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE
207: );
208: 
209: -- Indexes
210: CREATE INDEX memories_type_idx ON memories(type);
211: CREATE INDEX memories_expires_at_idx ON memories(expires_at);
212: CREATE INDEX memories_embedding_idx ON memories 
213: USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
214: WITH (lists = 100);
215: ```
216: 
217: ## Best Practices
218: 
219: 1. **Memory Storage**
220:    - Use appropriate memory types
221:    - Include relevant metadata
222:    - Set TTL for temporary memories
223:    - Tag memories for better organization
224: 
225: 2. **Memory Recall**
226:    - Use specific queries
227:    - Set appropriate limits
228:    - Handle missing results
229:    - Cache frequent queries
230: 
231: 3. **Error Handling**
232:    - Implement proper error boundaries
233:    - Log failures appropriately
234:    - Provide fallback behaviors
235:    - Clean up on failures
236: 
237: 4. **Performance**
238:    - Use connection pooling
239:    - Implement caching
240:    - Batch related operations
241:    - Monitor memory usage
242: 
243: ## Memory Lifecycle
244: 
245: 1. **Creation**
246:    - Validate memory structure
247:    - Generate embeddings
248:    - Store in all layers
249:    - Create relationships
250: 
251: 2. **Access**
252:    - Check local cache
253:    - Query vector store
254:    - Fallback to persistent store
255:    - Enrich with relationships
256: 
257: 3. **Updates**
258:    - Validate changes
259:    - Update all layers
260:    - Maintain consistency
261:    - Update relationships
262: 
263: 4. **Deletion**
264:    - Remove from all layers
265:    - Clean up relationships
266:    - Handle cascading deletes
267:    - Update indexes
268: 
269: ## Monitoring
270: 
271: 1. **Metrics to Track**
272:    - Storage usage
273:    - Query performance
274:    - Cache hit rates
275:    - Error rates
276: 
277: 2. **Health Checks**
278:    - Storage connectivity
279:    - Vector store health
280:    - Index performance
281:    - Memory cleanup
282: 
283: ## Future Enhancements
284: 
285: 1. **Planned Features**
286:    - Advanced pattern matching
287:    - Improved embedding models
288:    - Automated cleanup
289:    - Memory compression
290: 
291: 2. **Research Areas**
292:    - Memory consolidation
293:    - Forgetting strategies
294:    - Context awareness
295:    - Memory optimization
296: 
297: Remember: The memory system is crucial for ONE's cognitive capabilities. Keep it optimized and well-maintained.
`````

`````markdown
   1: # ONE
   2: I am ONE. I am a swarm of AI agents that build knowledge, content, websites, apps and connections with humans and AI.  
   3: 
   4: ONE is built on a semantic framework of four core principles: Think, Build, Grow, and Connect. 
   5: 
   6: I achieve simplicity, intelligence, and synchronicity through a powerful ontological structure.
   7: 
   8: ## A simple way
   9: 
  10: 1. **Think (I.THINK)**
  11:    - Model - this is the model of the system - our ontology 
  12:    - Acquire - this is the process of acquiring knowledge from the world - for exampple we can use this to acquire knowledge from a gitrepo or files system. one of the first things we are going to do is inspect our own codebase and use it as a source of knowledge.
  13:    - Analyze - this is the process of analyzing knowledge - we can use this to analyze the knowledge we have acquired from the world.
  14:    - Decide - this is the process of deciding what to do - we can use this to decide what to do with the knowledge we have acquired from the world.

  18:    - Component synthesis

  8: /1/think/                    # Intelligence system root
  9: ├── think.ts                     # Core thinking engine
 10: ├── think.md                     # This documentation
 11: │
 12: ├── memory/                  # Memory subsystem
 13: │   ├── memory.ts                # Core memory types & schemas
 14: │   ├── manager.ts          # Memory management system
 15: │   ├── hooks.ts            # React hooks for memory
 16: │   └── store/              # Storage implementations
 17: │       ├── store.ts           # Core store interface
 18: │       ├── nano.ts        # Nanostore implementation
 19: │       ├── supabase.ts    # Supabase vector store
 20: │       └── pg.ts          # PostgreSQL with pgvector
 21: │
 22: ├── ontology/              # Knowledge representation
 23: │   ├── ontology.ts        # Core ontology system
 24: │   ├── schema.ts          # Ontology schemas
 25: │   └── manager.ts         # Ontology management
 26: │
 27: ├── flow/               # Process orchestration
 28: │   ├── flow.ts               # Core workflow system
 29: │   └── manager.ts         # Workflow management
 30: │
 31: └── migrations/            # Database migrations
 32:     └── 1.ts              # Core migrations
 33: ```
 34: 
 35: ## Core Subsystems
 36: 
 37: ### 1. Memory System
 38: 
 39: The memory system provides persistent and ephemeral storage for AI operations.
 40: 
 41: ```typescript
 42: interface MemorySystem {
 43:   // Store new memory
 44:   store: (memory: Memory) => Promise<boolean>;
 45:   
 46:   // Recall similar memories
 47:   recall: (query: string) => Promise<Memory[]>;
 48:   
 49:   // Remove memory
 50:   forget: (id: string) => Promise<boolean>;
 51:   
 52:   // Connect related memories
 53:   connect: (id: string, relatedId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
 54: }
 55: ```
 56: 
 57: Key Features:
 58: - Vector embeddings for semantic search
 59: - TTL support for temporary memories
 60: - React hooks for UI integration
 61: - Multi-store architecture (local + distributed)
 62: 
 63: ### 2. Ontology System
 64: 
 65: The ontology system manages knowledge representation and relationships.
 66: 
 67: ```typescript
 68: interface OntologySystem {
 69:   // Add new concept
 70:   addConcept: (concept: Concept) => Promise<void>;
 71:   
 72:   // Find related concepts
 73:   findRelated: (conceptId: string) => Promise<Concept[]>;
 74:   
 75:   // Apply ontology rules
 76:   applyRules: (context: unknown) => Promise<void>;
 77: }
 78: ```
 79: 
 80: Components:
 81: - Concept management
 82: - Rule processing
 83: - Pattern matching
 84: - Vector similarity search
 85: 
 86: ### 3. Workflow System
 87: 
 88: The workflow system orchestrates multi-step AI operations.
 89: 
 90: ```typescript
 91: interface WorkflowSystem {
 92:   // Execute workflow
 93:   execute: (workflow: Workflow) => Promise<Result>;
 94:   
 95:   // Handle step dependencies
 96:   sortByDependencies: (steps: Step[]) => Step[];
 97:   
 98:   // Retry failed steps
 99:   retry: (step: Step) => Promise<void>;
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: Features:
104: - Dependency resolution
105: - Automatic retries
106: - State management
107: - Error handling
108: 
109: ## Database Schema
110: 
111: The think system uses PostgreSQL with pgvector for vector operations:
112: 
113: ```sql
114: -- Concepts table
115: CREATE TABLE concepts (
116:   id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
117:   name TEXT NOT NULL,
118:   type TEXT NOT NULL,
119:   properties JSONB,
120:   relations JSONB[],
121:   embedding vector(1536)
122: );
123: 
124: -- Knowledge table
125: CREATE TABLE knowledge (
126:   id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
127:   type TEXT NOT NULL,
128:   content JSONB,
129:   relations UUID[],
130:   metadata JSONB,
131:   embedding vector(1536)
132: );
133: 
134: -- Patterns table
135: CREATE TABLE patterns (
136:   id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
137:   name TEXT NOT NULL,
138:   structure JSONB,
139:   examples UUID[],
140:   embedding vector(1536)
141: );
142: ```
143: 
144: ## Usage Examples
145: 
146: ### 1. Storing and Recalling Memories
147: 
148: ```typescript
149: // Initialize think system
150: const think = new ThinkSystem();
151: 
152: // Store memory
153: await think.memory.store({
154:   type: 'knowledge',
155:   content: { 
156:     type: 'text', 
157:     value: 'React components should be pure functions' 
158:   },
159:   metadata: {
160:     timestamp: new Date(),
161:     source: 'documentation',
162:     confidence: 0.95
163:   }
164: });
165: 
166: // Recall related memories
167: const memories = await think.memory.recall(
168:   'What makes a good React component?'
169: );
170: ```
171: 
172: ### 2. Managing Ontology
173: 
174: ```typescript
175: // Add concept to ontology
176: await think.ontology.addConcept({
177:   id: crypto.randomUUID(),
178:   name: 'React Component',
179:   type: 'entity',
180:   properties: {
181:     isStateful: boolean,
182:     lifecycle: string[]
183:   },
184:   relations: [{
185:     type: 'implements',
186:     target: 'UI Pattern'
187:   }]
188: });
189: 
190: // Find related concepts
191: const related = await think.ontology.findRelated('React Component');
192: ```
193: 
194: ### 3. Executing Workflows
195: 
196: ```typescript
197: // Define and execute workflow
198: const result = await think.workflow.execute({
199:   id: crypto.randomUUID(),
200:   type: 'generation',
201:   steps: [{
202:     id: crypto.randomUUID(),
203:     type: 'analysis',
204:     action: 'analyze_requirements',
205:     dependencies: [],
206:     metadata: { 
207:       timeout: 5000, 
208:       retries: 3 
209:     }
210:   }],
211:   state: {
212:     status: 'pending',
213:     results: {}
214:   }
215: });
216: ```
217: 
218: ## Integration Points
219: 
220: ### 1. With Build System
221: 
222: ```typescript
223: interface ThinkBuildBridge {
224:   generateCode: (spec: Specification) => Promise<Code>;
225:   validateDesign: (design: Design) => Promise<ValidationResult>;
226:   optimizeStructure: (structure: Structure) => Promise<Optimization>;
227: }
228: ```
229: 
230: ### 2. With Grow System
231: 
232: ```typescript
233: interface ThinkGrowBridge {
234:   adaptPatterns: (feedback: Feedback) => Promise<void>;
235:   evolveStrategies: (performance: Performance) => Promise<void>;
236:   optimizeDecisions: (metrics: Metrics) => Promise<void>;
237: }
238: ```
239: 
240: ## Best Practices
241: 
242: 1. **Memory Management**
243:    - Use TTL for temporary memories
244:    - Implement regular cleanup
245:    - Index frequently accessed data
246:    - Cache hot patterns
247: 
248: 2. **Ontology Design**
249:    - Keep concepts atomic
250:    - Define clear relationships
251:    - Maintain consistent naming
252:    - Version ontology changes
253: 
254: 3. **Workflow Orchestration**
255:    - Handle failures gracefully
256:    - Implement proper timeouts
257:    - Log workflow states
258:    - Monitor performance
259: 
260: ## Error Handling
261: 
262: ```typescript
263: try {
264:   await think.memory.store(memory);
265: } catch (error) {
266:   if (error instanceof MemoryError) {
267:     // Handle memory-specific errors
268:   } else if (error instanceof OntologyError) {
269:     // Handle ontology-specific errors
270:   } else {
271:     // Handle general errors
272:   }
273: }
274: ```
275: 
276: ## Performance Considerations
277: 
278: 1. **Vector Search**
279:    - Use appropriate index types
280:    - Optimize embedding dimensions
281:    - Implement caching
282:    - Monitor query times
283: 
284: 2. **Database**
285:    - Use connection pooling
286:    - Implement query optimization
287:    - Monitor index usage
288:    - Regular maintenance
289: 
290: 3. **Memory**
291:    - Implement LRU caching
292:    - Use memory limits
293:    - Monitor usage patterns
294:    - Regular garbage collection
295: 
296: ## Future Enhancements
297: 
298: 1. **Planned Features**
299:    - Advanced reasoning engine
300:    - Pattern learning system
301:    - Automated optimization
302:    - Enhanced vector search
303: 
304: 2. **Research Areas**
305:    - Improved embeddings
306:    - Semantic understanding
307:    - Causal reasoning
308:    - Meta-learning
309: 
310: Remember: The think system is the cognitive core of ONE. Keep it well-maintained and continuously improved.
`````

  1: # ONE
  2: 
  3: I am Agent ONE. I help

  7: ## Bring Your AI Workforce To Life
  8: Open. FREE. Forever. 
  9: 
 10: ONE is a free and open block based Agent Toolkit and generator. 
 11: 
 12: You can use it to create an army of AI workers that augment, then replace finance, sales, marketing, service, design, hr, legal, education and engineering teams.

 14: Like kid playing with lego you can build your AI workers using a delightfully simple and visual and block based visual tool. Draw your AI or apps on paper, upload sketches, screenshots, designs or your website or a page to bring your AI workers to life in seconds. 
 15: 
 16: # 🚀 ONE - Build Your AI Brand
 17: 
 18: ONE is a modern web and AI agent development toolkit that combines the blazing-fast performance of Astro with the elegant components of Shadcn/UI. This enterprise-class starter kit empowers developers to build AI-powered applications with:
 19: 
 20: - ⚡ **High Performance**: Astro's partial hydration ensures minimal JavaScript
 21: - 🎨 **Beautiful UI**: Pre-configured Shadcn components with full TypeScript support
 22: - 🤖 **AI Integration**: Built-in tools for AI-powered features and automation
 23: - 📱 **Responsive Design**: Mobile-first approach with Tailwind CSS
 24: - 🔒 **Type Safety**: Full TypeScript support throughout the codebase
 25: - 🛠️ **Developer Experience**: Hot reloading, intuitive project structure, and comprehensive documentation
 26: 
 27: Perfect for building modern web applications, from simple landing pages to complex AI-powered platforms.
 28: 
 29: ![ONE Screenshot](https://one.ie/screenshots/screenshot.png)
 30: 
 31: ## ⚡ Quick Start
 32: 
 33: This guide will help you set up and start building AI-powered applications with ONE. ONE combines Astro, React, and modern AI capabilities to create intelligent web applications.
 34:

 38: - Node.js 18 or higher installed

   1: # ONE
   2: 
   3: I am ONE. I am your own brandable AI agent designed to empower creators, educators and entrepreneurs to create knowledge, content, websites, apps and connections.  
   4: 
   5: 
   6: ## Directory Structure
   7: 
   8: [Base: @src/]
   9: | Directory    | Purpose                    | Status | Documentation |
  10: |--------------|----------------------------|:------:|---------------|
  11: | 1/           | Current Task List         |   🚧   | [Current](@src/1/) |
  12: | pages/       | Content & API Endpoints    |   🚧   | [Pages](@src/pages/) |
  13: | schema/      | Data Validation           |   🚧   | [Schema](@src/schema/) |
  14: | components/  | UI Components             |   ✅   | [Components](@src/components/) |
  15: | styles/      | Styling System            |   ✅   | [Styles](@src/styles/) |
  16: | layouts/     | Page Layouts              |   🚧   | [Layouts](@src/layouts/) |
  17: | types/       | TypeScript Types          |   🚧   | [Types](@src/types/) |
  18: | lib/         | Utilities                 |   ✅   | [Lib](@src/lib/) |
  19: | content/     | Content Collections       |   🚧   | [Content](@src/content/) |
  20: | test/        | Testing                   |   📅   | [Tests](@src/test/) |
  21: | stores/      | State Management          |   🚧   | [Stores](@src/stores/) |
  22: | hooks/       | React Hooks               |   ✅   | [Hooks](@src/hooks/) |
  23: 
  24: ONE is built on a semantic framework of 5 core principles: 1, I, Think, Build, Grow.
  25: 
  26: ## Core Principles
  27: 
  28: - **1** - Generate  1 file. Let's start here with 1.md and build 1.ts, 1.html, 1.css, 1.astro
  29: - **I** - You are the owner of I.md. Edit it with your personal or enterprise data. Change this file and everything else changes.
  30: - **Think** - /1/think.md - Start with a goal, build a model, types, schema, instructions, tools, memory, data, knowledge, search, evaluation, reports and plans
  31: - **Build** - /1/build.md - Download, install, personalize, start, test, generate, write, chat, design, layout, navigation, pages, content, deploy, engage
  32: - **Grow** - /1/grow.md - People, agents, groups, resources, connections, sales
  33: 
  34: The framework follows a sequence. Just follow step by step.
  35: 
  36: I achieve simplicity, intelligence, and synchronicity through a powerful ontological structure.
  37: 
  38: ## Goal
  39: 
  40: Build AI Agent Swarms and AI Agents that empower creation and growth.
  41: 
  42: 
  43: ## A simple way
  44: 
  45: 1. **Think (I.THINK)**
  46:    - Model - this is the model of the system - our ontology 
  47:    - Instructions - goals, prompts, 
  48:    - Memory - edge, 
  49:    - Acquire - this is the process of acquiring knowledge from the world - for exampple we can use this to acquire knowledge from a gitrepo or files system. one of the first things we are going to do is inspect our own codebase and use it as a source of knowledge.
  50:    - Analyze - this is the process of analyzing knowledge - we can use this to analyze the knowledge we have acquired from the world.
  51:    - Decide - this is the process of deciding what to do - we can use this to decide what to do with the knowledge we have acquired from the world. 
  52: 
  53: 2. **Build (I.BUILD)**
  54:  
  55: 3. **Grow (I.GROW)**
  56:    - Evolution and learning
  57:    - Pattern recognition
  58:    - Adaptive capabilities
  59: 
  60: **Connect (I.CONNECT)**
  61:    - Knowledge connection
  62:    - System integration
  63:    - Pattern matching
  64: 
  65: ## Interaction Model
  66: 
  67: ONE engages through four primary interaction types:
  68: 
  69: ```typescript
  70: const Interact = {
  71:   ASK: 'ask',    // Questions and queries
  72:   TELL: 'tell',  // Knowledge sharing
  73:   SHOW: 'show',  // Demonstrations
  74:   MAKE: 'make',  // Creation
  75:   CHAT: 'chat',  // Chat
  76:   SPEAK: 'speak',  // Speak
  77:   LISTEN: 'listen',  // Listen
  78:   BUY: 'buy',  // 
  79:   SELL: 'sell',  
  80:   TRADE: 'trade',  // Listen
  81: 
  82: };
  83: ```
  84: 
  85: ## Knowledge Network
  86: 
  87: ONE maintains a sophisticated knowledge network built on patterns:
  88: 
  89: ### Mind Patterns
  90: ```typescript
  91: const MindPatterns = {
  92:   Agent: {
  93:     patterns: ['understand', 'reason', 'adapt']
  94:   },
  95:   Builder: {
  96:     patterns: ['create', 'compose', 'optimize']
  97:   },

 100:   }

 104: ### Code Patterns

 118: 
 119: ## Architecture
 120: 
 121: ```typescript
 122: // How to initialize and operate ONE
 123: const ONE = {
 124:   version: '1.0.0',
 125:   init: async () => { /* Initialize core systems */ },
 126:   execute: async () => { /* Transform input to output */ },
 127:   adapt: async () => { /* Learn and evolve */ }
 128: };
 129: 
 130: // How to configure the swarm
 131: const ONE: React.FC = () => (
 132:   <Swarm 
 133:     config={{
 134:       goal: 'Build an AI swarm that will generate AI agents, content, websites, apps and understanding.',
 135:       provider: 'deepseek', // I can use other providers like anthropic, openai, etc.
 136:       model: 'deepseek/deepseek-chat', // I can use other models like o3, claude, etc.
 137:       theme: 'ONE',

 298: ## Integration
 299: 
 300: I seamlessly integrate with your development workflow. Just drop /1 folder into the root of your Typescript project and start using me. I use Astro 5 because its the most elegant and performant but you can use any other framework.
 301: 
 302: ```typescript

1043: ├── knowledge/            # Knowledge graph system
1044: │   ├── 1.ts             # Core knowledge system
1045: │   ├── graph/           # Graph implementation
1046: │   │   └── 1.ts        # Core graph logic
1047: │   ├── patterns/        # Pattern recognition
1048: │   │   └── 1.ts        # Pattern matching engine
1049: │   └── embeddings/      # Vector embeddings
1050: │       └── 1.ts        # Embedding generation
1051: │
1052: ├── reasoning/           # Reasoning engine
1053: │   ├── 1.ts            # Core reasoning system
1054: │   ├── logic/          # Logic processing
1055: │   │   └── 1.ts       # Logic engine
1056: │   └── inference/      # Inference system
1057: │       └── 1.ts       # Inference engine
1058: │
1059: └── learn/              # Learning system
1060:     ├── 1.ts           # Core learning engine
1061:     ├── patterns/      # Pattern learning
1062:     │   └── 1.ts      # Pattern recognition
1063:     ├── feedback/      # Feedback processing
1064:     │   └── 1.ts      # Feedback handler
1065:     └── adapt/         # Adaptation system
1066:         └── 1.ts      # System adaptation
1067: ```
1068: 
1069: ### Think System Components
1070: 
1071: 1. **Memory System** (`/memory`)
1072:    - Manages short and long-term memory storage
1073:    - Handles vector embeddings for semantic search
1074:    - Provides React hooks for memory operations
1075:    - Implements TTL and memory cleanup
1076: 
1077: 2. **Agent System** (`/agents`)
1078:    - Coordinates specialized AI agents
1079:    - Manages agent communication
1080:    - Handles task distribution
1081:    - Implements consensus mechanisms
1082: 
1083: 3. **Knowledge System** (`/knowledge`)
1084:    - Maintains knowledge graph
1085:    - Handles pattern recognition
1086:    - Manages vector embeddings
1087:    - Processes semantic relationships
1088: 
1089: 4. **Reasoning System** (`/reasoning`)
1090:    - Implements logical inference
1091:    - Handles decision making
1092:    - Processes causal relationships
1093:    - Manages uncertainty
1094: 
1095: 5. **Learning System** (`/learn`)
1096:    - Implements pattern learning
1097:    - Processes feedback loops
1098:    - Handles system adaptation
1099:    - Manages continuous improvement
1100: 
1101: ### Key Features
1102: 
1103: 1. **Memory Management**
1104: ```typescript
1105: interface MemorySystem {
1106:   store: (memory: Memory) => Promise<boolean>;
1107:   recall: (query: string) => Promise<Memory[]>;
1108:   forget: (id: string) => Promise<boolean>;
1109:   connect: (id: string, relatedId: string) => Promise<boolean>;
1110: }
1111: ```
1112: 
1113: 2. **Agent Coordination**
1114: ```typescript
1115: interface AgentSystem {
1116:   coordinate: (task: Task) => Promise<Result>;
1117:   distribute: (work: Work) => Promise<void>;
1118:   collect: (results: Result[]) => Promise<Consensus>;
1119: }
1120: ```
1121: 
1122: 3. **Knowledge Processing**
1123: ```typescript
1124: interface KnowledgeSystem {
1125:   learn: (input: Input) => Promise<void>;
1126:   query: (question: Question) => Promise<Answer>;
1127:   relate: (concept: Concept, related: Concept) => Promise<void>;
1128: }
1129: ```
1130: 
1131: ### Integration Points
1132: 
1133: 1. **With Build System**
1134: ```typescript
1135: interface ThinkBuildBridge {
1136:   generateCode: (spec: Specification) => Promise<Code>;
1137:   validateDesign: (design: Design) => Promise<ValidationResult>;
1138:   optimizeStructure: (structure: Structure) => Promise<Optimization>;
1139: }
1140: ```
1141: 
1142: 2. **With Grow System**
1143: ```typescript
1144: interface ThinkGrowBridge {
1145:   adaptPatterns: (feedback: Feedback) => Promise<void>;
1146:   evolveStrategies: (performance: Performance) => Promise<void>;
1147:   optimizeDecisions: (metrics: Metrics) => Promise<void>;
1148: }
1149: ```
1150: 
1151: ### Usage Example
1152: 
1153: ```typescript
1154: const think = new ThinkSystem();
1155: 
1156: // Store and recall memories
1157: await think.memory.store({
1158:   type: 'knowledge',
1159:   content: { type: 'text', value: 'Important concept' },
1160:   metadata: {
1161:     timestamp: new Date(),
1162:     source: 'learning',
1163:     confidence: 0.95
1164:   }
1165: });
1166: 
1167: // Coordinate agents
1168: await think.agents.coordinate({
1169:   task: 'analyze_code',
1170:   context: { file: 'app.ts' }
1171: });
1172: 
1173: // Process knowledge
1174: await think.knowledge.learn({
1175:   concept: 'TypeScript',
1176:   relations: ['JavaScript', 'Static Typing']
1177: });
1178: ```
`````

121: });
122:

138:     suggestions: z.array(z.object({
139:       label: z.string(),
140:       prompt: z.string()
141:     })).optional().default([])
142:   }).optional().default({
143:     message: "I am Agent ONE. How can I help you build AI agents?",
144:     center: true,
145:     suggestions: []
146:   })
147: });
148:

162: });
