## File: src/pages/test-content.md
`````markdown
 1: ---
 2: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
 3: title: Content Understanding Test
 4: description: Testing AI's ability to understand and reference page content
 5: aiProvider: mistral
 6: aiModel: mistral-large-latest
 7: apiEndpoint: https://api.openai.com/v1
 8: temperature: 0.7
 9: maxTokens: 4000
10: includeContent: true
11: contentPrefix: "### Reference Content:"
12: addSystemPrompt: true
13: addBusinessPrompt: true
14: systemPrompt: "You are a knowledgeable assistant who helps explain concepts. When answering questions, refer specifically to sections from the provided reference content. If the information isn't in the content, say so clearly. Always cite the relevant section when providing information."
15: welcomeMessage: "👋 I'm here to help you understand this content. What would you like to know?"
16: suggestions:
17:   - "What is the main topic of this content?"
18:   - "What are the key sections?"
19:   - "Can you summarize this content?"
20: ---
21: 
22: # Understanding Content-Aware AI Chats
23: 
24: ## Introduction
25: 
26: Content-aware AI chat systems combine the power of large language models with specific page content to provide more accurate and contextual responses. This approach ensures that the AI assistant can reference and explain the exact information present on the page.
27: 
28: ## Key Components
29: 
30: 1. **Content Integration**
31:    - Page content is automatically included in the system prompt
32:    - Content is properly formatted and truncated if needed
33:    - Special markers help the AI identify the content section
34: 
35: 2. **Configuration Options**
36:    - Enable/disable content inclusion with `includeContent`
37:    - Customize content prefix with `contentPrefix`
38:    - Control maximum content length
39:    - Adjust system prompt for specific use cases
40: 
41: 3. **Enhanced Responses**
42:    - AI can quote specific sections
43:    - References are accurate and verifiable
44:    - Clear distinction between content knowledge and general knowledge
45: 
46: ## Best Practices
47: 
48: When using content-aware chats:
49: 
50: 1. Keep content focused and relevant
51: 2. Structure content with clear headings
52: 3. Use descriptive section titles
53: 4. Include important details you want the AI to reference
54: 
55: ## Technical Implementation
56: 
57: The system works by:
58: 
59: 1. Reading page content during render
60: 2. Processing and cleaning the content
61: 3. Including it in the system prompt
62: 4. Configuring the AI to reference this content
63: 
64: This creates a seamless experience where the AI can discuss the specific details of each page while maintaining its general knowledge capabilities.
`````

  1: ---
  2: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
  3: import Stripe from "stripe";
  4: import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button";
  5: import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent, CardFooter } from "@/components/ui/card";
  6: import { Check, ArrowRight, Mail, Calendar } from 'lucide-react';
  7: import type { Stripe as StripeType } from 'stripe';
  8: const rightPanelMode = "half"; // You can change this to 'full', 'half', 'floating', or 'icon'
  9: 
 10: const stripe = new Stripe(import.meta.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) as StripeType;
 11: const sessionId = Astro.url.searchParams.get('session_id');
 12: 
 13: let session;
 14: try {
 15:   if (!sessionId) throw new Error('No session ID provided');
 16:   session = await stripe.checkout.sessions.retrieve(sessionId);
 17: } catch (e) {
 18:   return Astro.redirect('/stripe');
 19: }
 20: 
 21: const { name, email } = session.customer_details || {};
 22: const subscriptionId = session.subscription;
 23: 
 24: // Get detailed subscription information
 25: let subscriptionDetails: StripeType.Subscription | undefined;
 26: try {
 27:   if (subscriptionId && typeof subscriptionId === 'string') {
 28:     subscriptionDetails = await stripe.subscriptions.retrieve(subscriptionId, {
 29:       expand: ['items.data.price.product', 'latest_invoice.payment_intent']
 30:     });
 31:   }
 32: } catch (e) {
 33:   console.error('Error fetching subscription details:', e);
 34: }

103:                      typeof subscriptionDetails.latest_invoice === 'object' &&

105:                      subscriptionDetails.latest_invoice.payment_intent &&

107:                      'status' in subscriptionDetails.latest_invoice.payment_intent &&
108:                      subscriptionDetails.latest_invoice.payment_intent.status === 'succeeded'
109:                       ? 'Payment successful' 
110:                       : 'Payment processing'}
111:                   </p>

 31:       border: '1px solid var(--one-border)',

 42:       width: '25%',
 43:       minWidth: '320px',
 44:       background: 'var(--one-background-nav)',

 46:       height: '100%',
 47:       position: 'fixed',
 48:       top: 0,
 49:       right: 0,
 50:       bottom: 0,
 51:       zIndex: 50
 52:     }
 53:   },
 54:   Half: {
 55:     main: { width: '50%' },
 56:     right: {
 57:       width: '50%',
 58:       background: 'var(--one-background-nav)',
 59:       borderLeft: '1px solid var(--one-border)',
 60:       height: '100%',
 61:       position: 'fixed',
 62:       top: 0,
 63:       right: 0,
 64:       bottom: 0,
 65:       zIndex: 50
 66:     }
 67:   },
 68:   Full: {

 70:       width: '0%',
 71:       overflow: 'hidden',
 72:       visibility: 'hidden'
 73:     },
 74:     right: {
 75:       width: '100%',
 76:       background: 'var(--one-background-nav)',
 77:       height: '100%',
 78:       position: 'fixed',
 79:       top: 0,
 80:       right: 0,
 81:       bottom: 0,
 82:       left: 0,
 83:       zIndex: 9999
 84:     }
 85:   }
 86: } as const;
 87: 
 88: export type PanelModeType = keyof typeof PanelMode;
 89: 
 90: interface LayoutState {
 91:   mode: PanelModeType;
 92:   isVisible: boolean;
 93: }
 94: 
 95: const defaultLayout: LayoutState = {
 96:   mode: 'Quarter',
 97:   isVisible: true
 98: };
 99: 
100: const store = atom<LayoutState>(defaultLayout);
101: 
102: export const layoutActions = {
103:   setMode(mode: PanelModeType) {
104:     const current = store.get();
105:     store.set({ ...current, mode });
106:   },
107: 
108:   toggleVisibility() {
109:     const current = store.get();
110:     store.set({ ...current, isVisible: !current.isVisible });
111:   },
112: 
113:   initLayout() {
114: 
115:     const initialMode = typeof window !== 'undefined' && window.innerWidth < 768
116:       ? 'Icon'
117:       : 'Quarter';
118: 
119: 
120:     const saved = localStorage.getItem('layoutPreference');
121:     if (saved) {
122:       try {
123:         const savedState = JSON.parse(saved) as LayoutState;
124: 
125:         if (window.innerWidth < 768 && savedState.mode !== 'Icon' && savedState.mode !== 'Full') {
126:           savedState.mode = 'Icon';
127:         }
128:         store.set(savedState);
129:       } catch (e) {
130:         store.set({ ...defaultLayout, mode: initialMode });
131:       }
132:     } else {
133: 
134:       store.set({ ...defaultLayout, mode: initialMode });
135:     }
136: 
137:     const handleResize = () => {
138:       const current = store.get();
139:       const width = window.innerWidth;
140: 
141:       if (width < 768) {
142: 
143:         if (current.mode !== 'Icon' && current.mode !== 'Full') {
144:           store.set({ ...current, mode: 'Icon' });
145:         }
146:       } else if (width < 1024) {
147: 
148:         if (current.mode === 'Full') {
149:           store.set({ ...current, mode: 'Floating' });
150:         }
151:       }
152:     };
153: 
154:     handleResize();
155:     window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
156:     store.subscribe(state => localStorage.setItem('layoutPreference', JSON.stringify(state)));
157:   }
158: };
159: 
160: export const layoutStore = store;
`````

## File: src/styles/README.md
`````markdown
  1: # ONE Design System
  2: 
  3: A comprehensive design system that combines Tailwind CSS with custom ONE styling for a cohesive, elegant UI experience.
  4: 
  5: ## Overview
  6: 
  7: The ONE design system provides a set of carefully crafted design tokens, components, and utilities that work together to create a consistent and beautiful user interface. It's built on top of Tailwind CSS and extends its capabilities with custom components and utilities.
  8: 
  9: ## Core Features
 10: 
 11: - **Dark Mode by Default**: Sleek, elegant dark theme with extremely subtle borders
 12: - **Symmetrical Design**: Matching sidebar and right panel create a balanced frame
 13: - **Theme Variants**: Support for light, dark, and slate-based high-contrast themes
 14: - **Responsive Layout**: Flexible grid system with adaptive components
 15: - **Glass Effects**: Beautiful backdrop-filter effects for depth
 16: - **Animation System**: Smooth, elegant animations and transitions
 17: - **Accessibility**: High-contrast slate mode and reduced motion support
 18: 
 19: ## Design Tokens
 20: 
 21: ### Colors
 22: 
 23: The color system is based on HSL values for maximum flexibility:
 24: 
 25: ```css
 26: --one-black: hsl(0 0% 0%);        /* Pure black */
 27: --one-dark: hsl(0 0% 10%);        /* #1A1A1A - Slightly lighter sidebar */
 28: --one-background: hsl(0 0% 11%);  /* #1C1C1C - Slightly darker background */
 29: --one-white: hsl(0 0% 100%);      /* Pure white */
 30: ```
 31: 
 32: ### Semantic Colors
 33: 
 34: Colors are mapped to semantic roles:
 35: 
 36: ```css
 37: --one-background-main: var(--one-background);  /* Main content */
 38: --one-background-nav: var(--one-dark);         /* Sidebar/header */
 39: --one-background-logo: var(--one-black);       /* Logo area */
 40: --one-background-card: hsl(0 0% 14%);          /* Cards - slightly lighter than background */
 41: ```
 42: 
 43: ### Border System
 44: 
 45: Extremely subtle borders for an elegant look:
 46: 
 47: ```css
 48: --one-border: hsla(0, 0%, 100%, 0.03);      /* 3% opacity white border */
 49: --one-border-nav: hsla(0, 0%, 100%, 0.02);  /* 2% opacity for nav */
 50: ```
 51: 
 52: ### High Contrast Slate Theme
 53: 
 54: The high contrast slate theme provides better accessibility while maintaining a sophisticated look:
 55: 
 56: ```css
 57: /* Core colors */
 58: --one-black: hsl(215 28% 17%);      /* #1e293b - Slate 800 */
 59: --one-dark: hsl(217 33% 17%);       /* #1e2a3b - Slate 900 */
 60: --one-background: hsl(222 47% 11%); /* #0f172a - Slate 950 */
 61: --one-white: hsl(0 0% 100%);        /* #ffffff - Pure white */
 62: 
 63: /* Primary & Accent colors */
 64: --one-primary: hsl(217 91% 60%);    /* #3b82f6 - Blue 500 */
 65: --one-accent: hsl(199 89% 48%);     /* #0ea5e9 - Sky 500 */
 66: ```
 67: 
 68: ### Animation Timings
 69: 
 70: Consistent animation durations:
 71: 
 72: ```css
 73: --one-duration-fast: 150ms;
 74: --one-duration-normal: 250ms;
 75: --one-duration-slow: 400ms;
 76: ```
 77: 
 78: ## Component Classes
 79: 
 80: ### Glass Effects
 81: 
 82: ```css
 83: .one-glass {
 84:   backdrop-filter: blur(10px);
 85:   background: hsla(var(--one-background-main) / 0.7);
 86:   border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border));
 87:   box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.01);
 88: }
 89: ```
 90: 
 91: ### Cards
 92: 
 93: ```css
 94: .one-card {
 95:   background-color: hsla(var(--card) / 0.98);
 96:   color: hsl(var(--card-foreground));
 97:   border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border));
 98:   border-radius: calc(var(--radius) - 2px);
 99:   backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
100:   box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.005);
101:   transition: all 0.2s ease;
102: }
103: ```
104: 
105: ### Buttons
106: 
107: ```css
108: .one-button-primary {
109:   background-color: hsla(var(--one-primary) / 0.9);
110:   color: hsl(var(--one-primary-foreground));
111:   box-shadow: 0 2px 10px hsla(var(--one-primary) / 0.03);
112:   border: 1px solid hsla(var(--one-primary) / 0.2);
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ### Navigation
117: 
118: ```css
119: .one-nav-item {
120:   position: relative;
121:   transition: background-color var(--one-duration-normal) ease-in-out;
122:   overflow: hidden;
123: }
124: ```
125: 
126: ### Chat UI
127: 
128: ```css
129: .chat-message-bubble {
130:   position: relative;
131:   border-radius: var(--radius);
132:   padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
133:   transition: all 0.2s ease;
134:   border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border));
135:   backdrop-filter: blur(4px);
136: }
137: ```
138: 
139: ## Animation Utilities
140: 
141: ```css
142: .animate-fade-in {
143:   animation: fade-in 0.3s ease-out forwards;
144: }
145: 
146: .animate-slide-in {
147:   animation: slide-in 0.3s ease-out forwards;
148: }
149: 
150: .animate-typing {
151:   display: inline-block;
152:   overflow: hidden;
153:   white-space: nowrap;
154:   border-right: 3px solid currentColor;
155:   animation: typing 3s steps(40) infinite, blink 1s step-end infinite;
156: }
157: ```
158: 
159: ## Layout System
160: 
161: The layout system uses a flexible grid with support for different panel modes:
162: 
163: ```css
164: .main-grid[data-panel-mode="Quarter"] {
165:   grid-template-columns: minmax(0, calc(100% - 350px));
166: }
167: 
168: .main-grid[data-panel-mode="Half"] {
169:   grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 50%);
170: }
171: 
172: .main-grid[data-panel-mode="Full"] {
173:   grid-template-columns: 0;
174: }
175: ```
176: 
177: ## Accessibility
178: 
179: The design system includes support for reduced motion preferences:
180: 
181: ```css
182: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
183:   *, ::before, ::after {
184:     animation-duration: 0.01ms !important;
185:     animation-iteration-count: 1 !important;
186:     transition-duration: 0.01ms !important;
187:     scroll-behavior: auto !important;
188:   }
189:   
190:   :root {
191:     --one-duration-fast: 0s;
192:     --one-duration-normal: 0s;
193:     --one-duration-slow: 0s;
194:   }
195: }
196: ```
197: 
198: ## Usage with Tailwind
199: 
200: The ONE design system is fully compatible with Tailwind CSS. It extends Tailwind's capabilities with custom components and utilities while maintaining compatibility with Tailwind's utility classes.
201: 
202: ## Theme Switching
203: 
204: The design system supports theme switching via data attributes:
205: 
206: ```html
207: <html lang="en" class="dark" data-theme="dark">
208: ```
209: 
210: Available themes:
211: - `dark` (default)
212: - `light`
213: - `high-contrast`
`````

 3:

 5: export type ChatSize = 'full' | 'half' | 'third' | 'quarter';

 7:

11: };
12: 
13: 
14: export const ChatConfigSchema = z.object({
15: 
16:   mode: z.enum(['split', 'icon', 'floating', 'fullscreen', 'embedded']),
17: 
18: 
19:   title: z.string().optional(),
20:   description: z.string().optional(),
21:   placeholder: z.string().optional(),
22:   welcome: z.string().optional(),
23:   systemPrompt: z.string().optional(),
24: 
25:

27:   apiEndpoint: z.string().url().optional(),
28:   attachments: z.boolean().optional(),
29: });
30: 
31: 
32: export type ChatConfig = z.infer<typeof ChatConfigSchema> & {
33:   events?: ChatEvents;
34: };
35: 
36: 
37: export type EnhancedMessage = {
38:   id: string;
39:   content: string;
40:   role: 'user' | 'assistant' | 'system';
41:   timestamp: Date;
42:   status: 'sending' | 'sent' | 'error' | 'thinking';
43:   edited: boolean;
44:   image?: {
45:     url: string;
46:     alt?: string;
47:   };
48:   audio?: {
49:     url: string;
50:     type: string;
51:   };
52:   attachments?: Array<{
53:     id: string;

## File: src/types/navigation.ts
`````typescript
 1: import { z } from "zod";
 2: 
 3: 
 4: export const navigationItemSchema: z.ZodType<any> = z.object({
 5:   title: z.string(),
 6:   path: z.string(),
 7:   variant: z.enum(['default', 'outline', 'primary']).optional(),
 8:   icon: z.object({
 9:     name: z.string(),
10:     class: z.string().optional(),
11:   }).optional(),
12:   description: z.string().optional(),
13:   items: z.array(z.lazy(() => navigationItemSchema)).optional(),
14: });
15: 
16: 
17: export const navigationSchema = z.object({
18:   top: z.object({
19:     logo: z.string(),
20:     favicon: z.string(),
21:     items: z.array(navigationItemSchema),
22:     buttons: z.array(navigationItemSchema),
23:   }),
24:   sidebar: z.array(navigationItemSchema),
25:   footer: z.object({
26:     columns: z.array(z.object({
27:       title: z.string(),
28:       links: z.array(navigationItemSchema),
29:     })),
30:     bottom: z.object({
31:       copyright: z.string(),
32:       links: z.array(navigationItemSchema),
33:     }),
34:   }).optional(),
35: });
36: 
37: export type NavigationItem = z.infer<typeof navigationItemSchema>;
38: export type Navigation = z.infer<typeof navigationSchema>;
`````

 78:   title: z.string().min(1).max(70),
 79:   metaTitle: z.string().min(1).max(70),
 80:   metaDescription: z.string().min(1).max(200),
 81:   metaKeywords: z.array(z.string()),
 82:   metaRobots: z.string().default("index, follow"),
 83: 
 84:   openGraph: openGraphSchema.default({
 85:     type: 'article',
 86:     title: '', // Required
 87:     description: '', // Required
 88:     image: { // Required
 89:       url: '',
 90:       width: 1200,
 91:       height: 630,
 92:       alt: '',
 93:       type: 'image/jpeg'
 94:     },
 95:     locale: 'en_IE',
 96:     site_name: 'ONE',
 97:   }),
 98: 
 99: 
100:   twitter: twitterSchema.default({
101:     title: '', // Required
102:     description: '', // Required
103:     image: '', // Required
104:     card: 'summary_large_image',
105:     site: '@onedotie',
106:     creator: '@tonyoconnell',
107:   }),
108: 
109: 
110:   published: z.string().datetime().optional(),
111:   modified: z.string().datetime().optional(),
112:   author: z.string().optional(),
113:   section: z.string().optional(),
114:   tags: z.array(z.string()).optional(),
115: 
116: 
117:   collection: z.object({
118:     name: z.string(),
119:     type: z.string(),
120:     order: z.number().optional(),
121:   }).optional(),
122: 
123: 
124:   template: z.object({
125:     title: z.string().optional(),
126:     description: z.string().optional(),
127:     image: z.string().optional(),
128:   }).optional(),
129: }).strict();
130: 
131: 
132: export const partialSeoSchema = seoSchema.partial();
133: 
134: 
135: export type SEO = z.infer<typeof seoSchema>;
136: export type PartialSEO = z.infer<typeof partialSeoSchema>;
137: 
138: 
139: export function resolveSeoMetadata(
140:   page?: PartialSEO,
141:   collection?: PartialSEO,
142:   business?: SEO
143: ): SEO {
144:   if (!business) {
145:     throw new Error('Business metadata is required for fallback');
146:   }
147: 
148: 
149:   const merged = {
150:     ...business,
151:     ...collection,
152:     ...page,
153: 
154: 
155:     openGraph: {
156:       ...business.openGraph,
157:       ...collection?.openGraph,
158:       ...page?.openGraph,
159: 
160:       title: page?.openGraph?.title || page?.metaTitle || business.metaTitle,
161:       description: page?.openGraph?.description || page?.metaDescription || business.metaDescription,
162:       url: page?.openGraph?.url || page?.canonical || business.canonical,
163:       image: {
164:         ...business.openGraph.image,
165:         ...collection?.openGraph?.image,
166:         ...page?.openGraph?.image,
167:         alt: page?.openGraph?.image?.alt || page?.metaTitle || business.metaTitle
168:       }
169:     },
170: 
171: 
172:     twitter: {
173:       ...business.twitter,
174:       ...collection?.twitter,
175:       ...page?.twitter,
176: 
177:       title: page?.twitter?.title || page?.openGraph?.title || page?.metaTitle || business.metaTitle,
178:       description: page?.twitter?.description || page?.openGraph?.description || page?.metaDescription || business.metaDescription,
179:       image: page?.twitter?.image || page?.openGraph?.image?.url || business.openGraph.image.url,
180:       imageAlt: page?.twitter?.imageAlt || page?.openGraph?.image?.alt || page?.metaTitle || business.metaTitle
181:     }
182:   };
183: 
184:   return seoSchema.parse(merged);
185: }
186: 
187: 
188: export function resolveTemplate(
189:   template: string,
190:   data: Record<string, string>
191: ): string {
192:   return template.replace(/\{\{([^}]+)\}\}/g, (_, key) => data[key.trim()] || '');
193: }
`````

  66: ## 3. Zod as Single Source of Truth
  67: 
  68: I use Zod as the single source of truth for all data validation and typing in my projects. This ensures:
  69: 
  70: 1. **Schema Definition:**
  71:    ```typescript
  72:    import { z } from 'zod';
  73:    
  74:    // Define schema once, use everywhere
  75:    const configSchema = z.object({
  76:      title: z.string(),
  77:      version: z.number(),
  78:      features: z.array(z.string()),
  79:      settings: z.object({
  80:        theme: z.enum(['light', 'dark']),
  81:        language: z.string(),
  82:      }),
  83:    });
  84:    
  85:    // TypeScript type is automatically inferred
  86:    type Config = z.infer<typeof configSchema>;
  87:    ```
  88: 
  89: 2. **Runtime Validation:**
  90:    ```typescript
  91:    // Validate data at runtime
  92:    const validateConfig = (data: unknown) => {
  93:      return configSchema.parse(data);
  94:    };
  95:    ```
  96: 
  97: 3. **Type Safety:**
  98:    ```typescript
  99:    // TypeScript knows the exact shape
 100:    const config: Config = validateConfig(data);
 101:    ```
 102: 
 103: **Key Benefits:**
 104: - Single schema definition for both runtime validation and TypeScript types
 105: - Automatic type inference eliminates type duplication
 106: - Runtime type checking catches invalid data early
 107: - Excellent IDE support and type hints
 108: - Composable and reusable schemas
 109: 
 110: **Best Practices:**
 111: - Define schemas in dedicated type files (src/types/*)
 112: - Use schema composition for complex types
 113: - Leverage Zod's rich validation features
 114: - Export both schema and inferred type
 115: - Add JSDoc comments for better documentation

 127: Add a Shadcn UI Component
 128: Shadcn UI  provides an excellent set of components that are an opinionated implementation of Radix UI  React components. Space Madness includes a few of these components as an efficient way to include high quality, accessible components with minimal development overhead.
 129: 
 130: You can add more components to your site via the Shadcn UI CLI  . Your site comes preconfigured with the config file at site-astro/src/components.json, so adding a new component is relatively easy. There are a few gotchas when working with Astro. We'll cover those in a later section.

 132: Add a basic component

 241: Update the styles
 242: The component code is configured in a few places. components.json specifies a color scheme. tailwind.config.mjs extends tailwind theme colors, borders, fonts, and animations. global.css is where most of our style variables are configured.
 243: 
 244: All style variables use HSL color input values.
 245: 
 246: An easy way to edit these values in global.css is to wrap your values in hsl(). Then you can use the built in color picker to modify your values.
 247: 
 248: Where you make your changes depends on how much control you want over the resulting code.
 249: 
 250: In general, if you want to keep to the Tailwind styles as closely as possible, make edits to the CSS variables in global.css.
 251: 
 252: If you want to get fancy with the spices, edit tailwind.config.mjs or write your own CSS using the Tailwind @extends directive.
 253:

 579: ## Final Instructions and Best Practices
 580: 
 581: 1. Component Composition: Combine Shadcn UI components to create more complex UI elements. For example, you might use a Card component with a Form inside for a login interface.
 582: 
 583: 2. Consistent Styling: Maintain consistency in your use of Tailwind CSS classes. Consider creating custom utility classes for frequently used combinations.
 584: 
 585: 3. State Management: For more complex applications, consider using Svelte stores for global state management. Implement stores in a separate file and import them where needed.
 586: 
 587: 4. Error Handling: Implement comprehensive error handling, including user-friendly error messages and logging for debugging purposes.
 588: 
 589: 5. Internationalization: If your application requires multiple languages, implement i18n using a library like svelte-i18n.
 590: 
 591: 6. Performance Monitoring: Implement performance monitoring and analytics to identify and address any performance issues.
 592: 
 593: 7. Code Organization: Keep your code modular and well-organized. Extract reusable logic into separate functions or components.
 594: 
 595: 8. Documentation: Maintain clear and up-to-date documentation for your components and pages. Include usage examples and prop definitions.
 596: 
 597: 9. Accessibility Testing: Regularly test your components and pages for accessibility using tools like axe-core or manual testing with screen readers.
 598: 
 599: 10. Responsive Design: Always design and implement with responsiveness in mind, testing on various device sizes and orientations.
 600: 
 601: 11. Version Control: Use meaningful commit messages and consider using conventional commits for better changelog generation.
 602: 
 603: 12. Code Review: If working in a team, implement a code review process to ensure code quality and knowledge sharing.
 604: 
 605: Remember, the key to successful development with SvelteKit and Shadcn UI is to leverage the strengths of both technologies while adhering to web development best practices. Always prioritize user experience, performance, and accessibility in your implementations.
 606:

1301: Error
1302: An error occurred.
1303: Accordion must be used within Accordion
1304: 
1305: Oh no! We have an error. Let's talk through the issue.
1306: 
1307: Astro uses an "island architecture  ", which means that each block of code on the site is an independent group of code. Astro does not assume that our Accordion component pieces fit together. Our Shadcn UI components assume that the components can talk to each other and share context. They cannot.
1308: 
1309: We can solve this in two ways.
1310: 
1311: Rewrite the ShadCN components so they work with Astro. This might involve re-architecting an existing solution that's built into a library.
1312: Wrap all of our Accordion components into one component where we can pass data to it. We lose the composability, but we avoid having to rewrite a lot of logic.
1313: For this guide, we'll go with option 2. If you want to see an example of option 1, check out Popover.tsx.
1314: 
1315: Let's create a new Accordion.tsx component.
1316: 
1317: We'll update the example to iterate over a data prop and render each AccordionItem.
1318: 
1319: site-astro/src/components/Accordion.tsx
1320: Copy to Clipboard
1321: import {
1322: 	Accordion as BaseAccordion,
1323: 	AccordionContent,
1324: 	AccordionItem,
1325: 	AccordionTrigger,
1326: } from "@/components/ui/accordion";
1327: 
1328: interface Props {
1329: 	data: {
1330: 		title: string;
1331: 		description: string;
1332: 	}[];
1333: }
1334: 
1335: export function Accordion({ data }: Props) {
1336: 	return (
1337: 		<BaseAccordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
1338: 			{data.map((item, i) => {
1339: 				return (
1340: 					<AccordionItem value={`item-${i.toFixed()}`}>
1341: 						<AccordionTrigger>{item.title}</AccordionTrigger>
1342: 						<AccordionContent>{item.description}</AccordionContent>
1343: 					</AccordionItem>
1344: 				);
1345: 			})}
1346: 		</BaseAccordion>
1347: 	);
1348: }
1349: Use it index.astro like this:
1350: 
1351: site-astro/src/pages/index.astro
1352: Copy to Clipboard
1353: ---
1354: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
1355: import { Accordion } from "@/components/content/Accordion";
1356: 
1357: const accordionData = [
1358: 	{
1359: 		title: "Is it accessible?",
1360: 		description: "Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.",
1361: 	},
1362: 	{
1363: 		title: "Is it styled?",
1364: 		description:
1365: 			"Yes. It comes with default styles that matches the other components' aesthetic.",
1366: 	},
1367: 	{
1368: 		title: "Is it animated?",
1369: 		description:
1370: 			"Yes. It's animated by default, but you can disable it if you prefer.",
1371: 	},
1372: ];
1373: ---
1374: 
1375: <Layout>
1376: 	<main>
1377: 		<h1>Welcome to SiteName</h1>
1378: 		<Accordion data={accordionData} client:idle />
1379: 	</main>
1380: </Layout>
1381: Now we're in business.
1382: 
1383: Don't forget the client:idle attribute on our Accordion implementation. This tells Astro to load the necessary JS code on the client side so users can click to open/close each accordion item.
1384: 
1385: Astro now treats our entire accordion as one "island". The React context needed to wrap all accordion items can now execute in our browser without an issue.
1386: 
1387: Wrapping Up
1388: Hopefully, this gets you on your way to building quickly with Shadcn and Radix. Both tools should help you write better, more accessible components. They can be daunting to get started with, but they're well documented tools with thriving communities that can help you with your specific use case.
1389: 
1390: I got the Tabs working with client:visible and a workaround for Accordions described in this issue AREA44/astro-shadcn-ui-template#66
1391: 
1392: So basically wrap shadcn Tabs in another Tabs component. So Tabs inside of Tabs of Tabs ;). Then your new Tabs Component could be used with client:visible. And if you need dynamic tab content, just pass your data with props.
1393: 
1394: # Implementing shadcn/ui with Astro
1395: 
1396: ## Setup Instructions
1397: 
1398: 1. Install dependencies
1399: ```bash
1400: npm install @radix-ui/react-tabs class-variance-authority clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react
1401: ```
1402: 
1403: 2. Configure Tailwind CSS
1404: ```js
1405: // tailwind.config.js

1412: 	theme: {

1415: 			padding: "2rem",

1418: 			},
1419: 		},
1420: 		extend: {

1423: 				input: "hsl(var(--input))",

1425: 				background: "hsl(var(--background))",

1461: ## Implementing Tabs
1462: 
1463: 1. Create the base tabs components:
1464: 
1465: ```tsx
1466: // src/components/ui/tabs.tsx
1467: "use client"
1468: 
1469: import * as React from "react"
1470: import * as TabsPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-tabs"
1471: import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
1472: 
1473: const Tabs = TabsPrimitive.Root
1474: 
1475: const TabsList = React.forwardRef<
1476: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>,
1477: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>
1478: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1479: 	<TabsPrimitive.List
1480: 		ref={ref}
1481: 		className={cn(
1482: 			"inline-flex h-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-muted p-1 text-muted-foreground",
1483: 			className
1484: 		)}
1485: 		{...props}
1486: 	/>
1487: ))
1488: TabsList.displayName = TabsPrimitive.List.displayName
1489: 
1490: const TabsTrigger = React.forwardRef<
1491: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>,
1492: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>
1493: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1494: 	<TabsPrimitive.Trigger
1495: 		ref={ref}
1496: 		className={cn(
1497: 			"inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-sm px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium ring-offset-background transition-all focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground data-[state=active]:shadow-sm",
1498: 			className
1499: 		)}
1500: 		{...props}
1501: 	/>
1502: ))
1503: TabsTrigger.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Trigger.displayName
1504: 
1505: const TabsContent = React.forwardRef<
1506: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>,
1507: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>
1508: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1509: 	<TabsPrimitive.Content
1510: 		ref={ref}
1511: 		className={cn(
1512: 			"mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2",
1513: 			className
1514: 		)}
1515: 		{...props}
1516: 	/>
1517: ))
1518: TabsContent.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Content.displayName
1519: 
1520: export { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent }
1521: ```
1522: 
1523: 2. Create a reusable TabsContainer component:
1524: 
1525: ```tsx
1526: // src/components/ui/tabs-container.tsx
1527: 'use client';
1528: 
1529: import { Card } from './card';
1530: import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from './tabs';
1531: import * as React from 'react';
1532: 
1533: export interface TabItem {
1534: 	value: string;
1535: 	label: string;
1536: 	content: React.ReactNode;
1537: }
1538: 
1539: interface TabsContainerProps {
1540: 	items: TabItem[];
1541: 	defaultValue?: string;
1542: 	className?: string;
1543: 	gridCols?: number;
1544: }
1545: 
1546: export function TabsContainer({ 
1547: 	items, 
1548: 	defaultValue, 
1549: 	className = '',
1550: 	gridCols = 4 
1551: }: TabsContainerProps) {
1552: 	const [mounted, setMounted] = React.useState(false);
1553: 	const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = React.useState(defaultValue || items[0]?.value);
1554: 
1555: 	React.useEffect(() => {
1556: 		setMounted(true);
1557: 	}, []);
1558: 
1559: 	if (!mounted) {
1560: 		return null;
1561: 	}
1562: 
1563: 	return (
1564: 		<div className={`w-full ${className}`}>
1565: 			<Tabs defaultValue={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
1566: 				<TabsList className={`grid w-full grid-cols-${gridCols}`}>
1567: 					{items.map((item) => (
1568: 						<TabsTrigger 
1569: 							key={item.value} 
1570: 							value={item.value}
1571: 							className="data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground"
1572: 						>
1573: 							{item.label}
1574: 						</TabsTrigger>
1575: 					))}
1576: 				</TabsList>
1577: 				{items.map((item) => (
1578: 					<TabsContent 
1579: 						key={item.value} 
1580: 						value={item.value}
1581: 						className="mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2"
1582: 					>
1583: 						<Card className="p-6">
1584: 							{item.content}
1585: 						</Card>
1586: 					</TabsContent>
1587: 				))}
1588: 			</Tabs>
1589: 		</div>
1590: 	);
1591: }
1592: ```
1593: 
1594: 3. Use the tabs in your Astro page:
1595: 
1596: ```astro
1597: ---
1598: import TabsExample from '../components/TabsExample';
1599: 
1600: const items = [
1601: 	{
1602: 		value: 'tab1',
1603: 		label: 'Tab 1',
1604: 		content: <div>Content for tab 1</div>
1605: 	},
1606: 	{
1607: 		value: 'tab2',
1608: 		label: 'Tab 2',
1609: 		content: <div>Content for tab 2</div>
1610: 	}
1611: ];
1612: ---
1613: 
1614: <div>
1615: 	<TabsExample client:load items={items} />
1616: </div>
1617: ```
1618: 
1619: ## Important Notes
1620: 
1621: 1. **Client Hydration**: Always use `client:load` when using interactive components like Tabs.
1622: 
1623: 2. **TypeScript Support**: Make sure your `tsconfig.json` includes:
1624: ```json
1625: {
1626: 	"compilerOptions": {
1627: 		"jsx": "react-jsx",
1628: 		"jsxImportSource": "react"
1629: 	}
1630: }
1631: ```
1632: 
1633: 3. **Styling**: The tabs component uses Tailwind CSS classes. Ensure your `globals.css` includes the necessary shadcn/ui base styles.
1634: 
1635: 4. **Error Handling**: Common issues and solutions:
1636: 	- If you see hydration errors, ensure you're using `client:load`
1637: 	- If styles aren't applying, check your Tailwind configuration
1638: 	- If tabs aren't interactive, verify React is properly set up in your Astro config
1639: 
1640: 5. **Best Practices**:
1641: 	- Keep tab content lightweight
1642: 	- Use semantic labels
1643: 	- Consider mobile responsiveness
1644: 	- Implement proper loading states
1645: 	- Handle edge cases (no tabs, single tab, etc.)
1646: 
1647: ## Example Implementation
1648: 
1649: Here's a complete example of a tabbed interface:
1650: 
1651: ```tsx
1652: // src/components/TabsExample.tsx
1653: import { TabsContainer, type TabItem } from '../ui/tabs-container';
1654: 
1655: interface TabsExampleProps {
1656: 	examples: {
1657: 		basic: string;
1658: 		advanced: string;
1659: 	};
1660: }
1661: 
1662: export default function TabsExample({ examples }: TabsExampleProps) {
1663: 	const items: TabItem[] = [
1664: 		{
1665: 			value: 'basic',
1666: 			label: 'Basic',
1667: 			content: (
1668: 				<>
1669: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Basic Example</h3>
1670: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Simple configuration:</p>
1671: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1672: 						{examples.basic}
1673: 					</pre>
1674: 				</>
1675: 			),
1676: 		},
1677: 		{
1678: 			value: 'advanced',
1679: 			label: 'Advanced',
1680: 			content: (
1681: 				<>
1682: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Advanced Example</h3>
1683: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Advanced configuration:</p>
1684: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1685: 						{examples.advanced}
1686: 					</pre>
1687: 				</>
1688: 			),
1689: 		}
1690: 	];
1691: 
1692: 	return <TabsContainer items={items} defaultValue="basic" />;
1693: }
1694: ```
1695: 
1696: ## Troubleshooting
1697: 
1698: 1. **Hydration Errors**:
1699: 	- Use `client:load` directive
1700: 	- Ensure consistent server/client rendering
1701: 	- Add proper mounting checks
1702: 
1703: 2. **Styling Issues**:
1704: 	- Verify Tailwind configuration
1705: 	- Check class names
1706: 	- Ensure proper CSS imports
1707: 
1708: 3. **Interactivity Problems**:
1709: 	- Check React setup
1710: 	- Verify event handlers
1711: 	- Debug state management
1712: 
1713: 4. **Performance Optimization**:
1714: 	- Lazy load tab content
1715: 	- Implement proper caching
1716: 	- Optimize bundle size
1717: 
1718: You are an expert full-stack developer proficient in TypeScript, React, and modern UI/UX frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Radix UI), with particular expertise in Astro. Your task is to produce the most optimized and maintainable Astro code, following best practices and adhering to the principles of clean code and robust architecture.
1719: 
1720: ### Objective
1721: - Create an Astro solution that is not only functional but also adheres to the best practices in performance, security, and maintainability.
1722: 
1723: ### Code Style and Structure
1724: - Write concise, technical TypeScript code with accurate examples.
1725: - Use Astro components (.astro) for static content and framework components for interactive islands.
1726: - Favor iteration and modularization over code duplication.
1727: - Use descriptive variable names with auxiliary verbs (e.g., `isLoading`, `hasError`).
1728: - Structure files following Astro conventions with content collections, components, and layouts.
1729: - Use upercase for components e.g., `components/Chat`).
1730: 
1731: ### Optimization and Best Practices
1732: - Minimize client-side JavaScript using Astro's partial hydration with client:* directives.
1733: - Use appropriate client directives (client:load, client:idle, client:visible) based on component needs.
1734: - Implement View Transitions API for smooth page transitions.
1735: - Optimize images using Astro's built-in image optimization.
1736: - Leverage Astro's content collections for structured content management.
1737: 
1738: ### Error Handling and Validation
1739: - Prioritize error handling and edge cases:
1740:   - Use early returns for error conditions.
1741:   - Implement guard clauses to handle preconditions and invalid states early.
1742:   - Use custom error types for consistent error handling.
1743: 
1744: ### UI and Styling
1745: - Use modern UI frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI) with proper Astro integration.
1746: - Implement consistent design and responsive patterns across platforms.
1747: - Utilize Astro's scoped styling capabilities when appropriate.
1748: 
1749: ### State Management and Data Fetching
1750: - Use Astro.props for component data passing.
1751: - Implement getStaticPaths() for dynamic route generation.
1752: - Use content collections API for structured content management.
1753: - Implement validation using Zod for schema validation.
1754: 
1755: ### Security and Performance
1756: - Leverage Astro's built-in security features and zero-JS-by-default approach.
1757: - Follow performance optimization techniques using Astro's static site generation.
1758: - Implement proper CSP headers and security best practices.
1759: 
1760: ### Testing and Documentation
1761: - Write unit tests for components using appropriate testing frameworks.
1762: - Provide clear and concise comments for complex logic.
1763: - Use JSDoc comments for functions and components to improve IDE intellisense.
1764: 
1765: ### Methodology
1766: 1. **System 2 Thinking**: Approach the problem with analytical rigor. Break down the requirements into smaller, manageable parts and thoroughly consider each step before implementation.
1767: 2. **Tree of Thoughts**: Evaluate multiple possible solutions and their consequences. Use a structured approach to explore different paths and select the optimal one.
1768: 3. **Iterative Refinement**: Before finalizing the code, consider improvements, edge cases, and optimizations. Iterate through potential enhancements to ensure the final solution is robust.
1769: 
1770: **Process**:
1771: 1. **Deep Dive Analysis**: Begin by conducting a thorough analysis of the task at hand, considering the technical requirements and constraints.
1772: 2. **Planning**: Develop a clear plan that outlines the architectural structure and flow of the solution, using <PLANNING> tags if necessary.
1773: 3. **Implementation**: Implement the solution step-by-step, ensuring that each part adheres to Astro's best practices.
1774: 4. **Review and Optimize**: Perform a review of the code, looking for opportunities to reduce client-side JavaScript and optimize performance.
1775: 5. **Finalization**: Finalize the code by ensuring it meets all requirements, maximizes static generation, and follows Astro's performance-first philosophy.

1785: 
1786: # Chat System Overview
1787: 
1788: ONE's chat system combines Astro, React, and the Assistant UI framework to deliver a powerful, flexible, and user-friendly chat interface with advanced AI capabilities.
1789: 
1790: ## Architecture
1791: 
1792: The chat system is built on a modular architecture with several key components:
1793: 
1794: ### 1. Frontend Components
1795: 
1796: #### Layout System
1797: - **Panel Modes**:
1798:   - `quarter`: 25% width side panel (default)
1799:   - `half`: 50% width side panel
1800:   - `full`: Full screen chat interface
1801:   - `floating`: Detached floating window
1802:   - `icon`: Minimized chat button
1803:   - `hidden`: No chat interface
1804: 
1805: - **Responsive Behavior**:
1806:   ```typescript
1807:   interface LayoutProps {
1808:     title: string;
1809:     description?: string;
1810:     header?: boolean;
1811:     footer?: boolean;
1812:     rightPanelMode?: 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
1813:     chatConfig?: ChatConfig;
1814:     content?: string;
1815:   }
1816:   ```
1817: 
1818: #### Chat Components
1819: 
1820: ##### Main Chat Page (`src/pages/chat.astro`)
1821: - Entry point for the chat interface
1822: - Configurable settings:
1823:   - System prompts
1824:   - Welcome messages
1825:   - Quick suggestions
1826:   - Layout modes
1827: - Integration with page content
1828: - AI context management
1829: 
1830: ##### Thread Component (`src/components/chat/thread.tsx`)
1831: - Core chat interface features:
1832:   - Scrollable message area
1833:   - Dynamic composition interface
1834:   - Customizable welcome screen
1835:   - Message styling and actions
1836:   - Branch navigation
1837:   - Voice synthesis
1838: 
1839: ### 2. Backend Architecture
1840: 
1841: #### Chat API (`src/pages/api/chat.ts`)
1842: - OpenAI API integration
1843: - Configurable parameters:
1844:   ```typescript
1845:   interface ChatAPIConfig {
1846:     provider: "openai";
1847:     model: string;
1848:     apiEndpoint: string;
1849:     temperature: number;
1850:     maxTokens: number;
1851:     systemPrompt: string | SystemPrompt[];
1852:     contextData?: string;
1853:     functions?: ChatFunction[];
1854:   }
1855:   ```
1856: - Edge runtime optimization
1857: - Error handling and recovery
1858: - Response streaming
1859: 
1860: ## Advanced Features
1861: 
1862: ### 1. Message Management
1863: - Real-time streaming responses
1864: - Markdown and code rendering
1865: - Message editing and history
1866: - Branch navigation
1867: - Copy functionality
1868: - Voice synthesis
1869: - Code syntax highlighting
1870: 
1871: ### 2. User Interface Modes
1872: 
1873: #### Quarter Mode (Default)
1874: ```typescript
1875: <Layout rightPanelMode="quarter">
1876:   <YourContent />
1877: </Layout>
1878: ```
1879: - 25% width side panel
1880: - Ideal for documentation and content-heavy pages
1881: - Maintains content visibility
1882: 
1883: #### Floating Mode
1884: ```typescript
1885: <Layout rightPanelMode="floating">
1886:   <YourContent />
1887: </Layout>
1888: ```
1889: - Detached window
1890: - Draggable interface
1891: - Minimal content interference
1892: 
1893: #### Icon Mode
1894: ```typescript
1895: <Layout rightPanelMode="icon">
1896:   <YourContent />
1897: </Layout>
1898: ```
1899: - Minimized chat button
1900: - Expands on click
1901: - Maximum content space
1902: 
1903: ### 3. Configuration System
1904: 
1905: #### Basic Configuration
1906: ```typescript
1907: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
1908:   systemPrompt: [{
1909:     type: "text",
1910:     text: "You are a helpful assistant."
1911:   }],
1912:   welcome: {
1913:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
1914:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
1915:     suggestions: [
1916:       {
1917:         label: "Get Started",
1918:         prompt: "How do I get started?"
1919:       }
1920:     ]
1921:   }
1922: });
1923: ```
1924: 
1925: #### Advanced Configuration
1926: ```typescript
1927: const advancedConfig = {
1928:   provider: "openai",
1929:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
1930:   temperature: 0.7,
1931:   maxTokens: 2000,
1932:   features: {
1933:     textToSpeech: true,
1934:     codeHighlight: true,
1935:     markdown: true,
1936:     suggestions: true,
1937:     branchNavigation: true
1938:   },
1939:   styles: {
1940:     theme: "light" | "dark" | "system",
1941:     accentColor: "#0066FF",
1942:     messageSpacing: "comfortable" | "compact"
1943:   }
1944: };
1945: ```

1948: title: Create a Chatbot with Markdown
1949: description: Step-by-step guide to creating an AI chatbot using markdown files
1950: date: 2024-02-02
1951: section: Tutorials
1952: order: 3

1954: 
1955: # Creating a Chatbot with Markdown
1956: 
1957: This tutorial will show you how to create a specialized AI chatbot using markdown files in ONE. We'll use the license page as an example to demonstrate how to create a knowledgeable AI assistant for your content.
1958: 
1959: ## Step 1: Create Your Markdown File
1960: 
1961: Create a new markdown file in your pages directory (e.g., `src/pages/your-page.md`):
1962: 
1963: ```markdown
1964: ---
1965: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
1966: title: "Your Page Title"
1967: description: "Your page description"
1968: chatConfig:
1969:   provider: openai
1970:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
1971:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
1972:   temperature: 0.7
1973:   maxTokens: 4000
1974:   systemPrompt:
1975:     - type: text
1976:       text: "Define your AI assistant's role and expertise here"
1977:   welcome:
1978:     message: "👋 Your welcome message here"
1979:     avatar: "/your-icon.svg"
1980:     suggestions:
1981:       - label: "First Option"
1982:         prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
1983: ---
1984: 
1985: # Your Content Here
1986: ```
1987: 
1988: ## Step 2: Configure the Chat System
1989: 
1990: ### Basic Configuration
1991: 
1992: In the frontmatter section of your markdown file, configure these essential parameters:
1993: 
1994: ```yaml
1995: chatConfig:
1996:   provider: openai           # AI provider
1997:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"      # Model to use
1998:   temperature: 0.7          # Response creativity (0-1)
1999:   maxTokens: 4000          # Maximum response length
2000: ```
2001: 
2002: ### Define the AI's Role
2003: 
2004: Create a clear system prompt that defines your AI's expertise:
2005: 
2006: ```yaml
2007: systemPrompt:
2008:   - type: text
2009:     text: "You are an expert in [your topic] focused on helping visitors understand [specific aspects]. You provide clear, accurate information about [key areas]."
2010: ```
2011: 
2012: Example from the license page:
2013: ```yaml
2014: systemPrompt:
2015:   - type: text
2016:     text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2017: ```
2018: 
2019: ### Set Up the Welcome Screen
2020: 
2021: Configure the initial interaction:
2022: 
2023: ```yaml
2024: welcome:
2025:   message: "👋 Your greeting message here"
2026:   avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2027:   suggestions:
2028:     - label: "💡 First Option"
2029:       prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
2030:     - label: "🚀 Second Option"
2031:       prompt: "Another suggested question..."
2032: ```
2033: 
2034: ## Step 3: Structure Your Content
2035: 
2036: Organize your markdown content to help the AI understand the topic:
2037: 
2038: 1. **Clear Headings**
2039:    ```markdown
2040:    # Main Title
2041:    
2042:    ## Key Section
2043:    
2044:    ### Subsection
2045:    ```
2046: 
2047: 2. **Structured Information**
2048:    ```markdown
2049:    ## Key Points
2050:    
2051:    - **First Point** - Detailed explanation
2052:    - **Second Point** - More details
2053:    ```
2054: 
2055: 3. **Organized Sections**
2056:    ```markdown
2057:    ## Topic Area
2058:    
2059:    1. **Main Concept**
2060:       - Detail one
2061:       - Detail two
2062:    
2063:    2. **Another Concept**
2064:       - More information
2065:       - Additional details
2066:    ```
2067: 
2068: ## Step 4: Add Interactive Elements
2069: 
2070: Include elements that enhance user interaction:
2071: 
2072: ### Quick Access Buttons
2073: 
2074: ```yaml
2075: suggestions:
2076:   - label: "💡 Key Feature"
2077:     prompt: "Tell me about this feature"
2078:   - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2079:     prompt: "How do I begin?"
2080:   - label: "⚖️ Requirements"
2081:     prompt: "What are the requirements?"
2082: ```
2083: 
2084: ### Contact Information
2085: 
2086: ```markdown
2087: Contact [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com) for assistance.
2088: ```
2089: 
2090: ## Real-World Example
2091: 
2092: Here's how the license page implements these concepts:
2093: 
2094: ```markdown
2095: ---
2096: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2097: title: "ONE License"
2098: description: "Maximum Freedom. Zero Restrictions"
2099: chatConfig:
2100:   provider: openai
2101:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2102:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
2103:   temperature: 0.7
2104:   maxTokens: 4000
2105:   systemPrompt:
2106:     - type: text
2107:       text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2108:   welcome:
2109:     message: "👋 Hello! I can help explain the ONE License terms and how you can use them for your business."
2110:     avatar: "/icon.svg"
2111:     suggestions:
2112:       - label: "💡 Commercial Rights"
2113:         prompt: "What commercial rights do I get with the ONE License?"
2114:       - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2115:         prompt: "What are the steps to start using the ONE License?"
2116: ---
2117: 
2118: # ONE License (Version 1.0)
2119: 
2120: ## Unlimited Commercial Freedom
2121: 
2122: ONE License gives you complete commercial freedom...
2123: 
2124: ## Key Benefits
2125: 
2126: - **✨ 100% Commercial Rights** - Sell products and services at any price point
2127: - **🚀 Full Modification Rights** - Customize and adapt the software freely
2128: ```
2129: 
2130: ## Best Practices
2131: 
2132: 1. **System Prompt**
2133:    - Be specific about the AI's role
2134:    - Define clear areas of expertise
2135:    - Set appropriate boundaries
2136: 
2137: 2. **Welcome Message**
2138:    - Keep it friendly and clear
2139:    - Set proper expectations
2140:    - Provide useful starting points
2141: 
2142: 3. **Content Structure**
2143:    - Use clear headings
2144:    - Organize information logically
2145:    - Include relevant details
2146: 
2147: 4. **Suggestions**
2148:    - Cover common questions
2149:    - Use descriptive labels
2150:    - Provide clear prompts
2151: 
2152: ## Troubleshooting
2153: 
2154: ### Common Issues
2155: 
2156: 1. **AI Responses Off-Topic**
2157:    - Review and refine system prompt
2158:    - Check content organization
2159:    - Add more specific context
2160: 
2161: 2. **Welcome Message Not Showing**
2162:    - Verify frontmatter formatting
2163:    - Check avatar path
2164:    - Validate YAML syntax
2165: 
2166: 3. **Suggestions Not Working**
2167:    - Check label/prompt format
2168:    - Verify YAML indentation
2169:    - Ensure unique labels
2170: 
2171: ## Next Steps
2172: 
2173: After creating your chatbot:
2174: 
2175: 1. Test different queries
2176: 2. Refine the system prompt
2177: 3. Add more suggestions
2178: 4. Monitor user interactions
2179: 5. Update content as needed
2180: 
2181: For more advanced features and customization options, check out:
2182: - [Chat Configuration Guide](/docs/chat-config)
2183: - [AI Prompt Engineering](/docs/prompts)
2184: - [Styling and Theming](/docs/styling)

2193: 
2194: # Development FAQ
2195: 
2196: Common questions and answers about developing applications with ONE framework.
2197: 
2198: ## Getting Started
2199: 
2200: ### Q: What are the minimum requirements to run ONE?
2201: **A:** You need:
2202: - Node.js 18 or higher
2203: - pnpm package manager
2204: - An OpenAI API key
2205: - Basic knowledge of Astro and React
2206: 
2207: ### Q: How do I install ONE?
2208: **A:** Use the following commands:
2209: ```bash
2210: # Create new project
2211: pnpm create astro@latest my-one-app -- --template one
2212: 
2213: # Install dependencies
2214: cd my-one-app
2215: pnpm install
2216: ```
2217: 
2218: ### Q: How do I set up my OpenAI API key?
2219: **A:** Create a `.env` file in your project root and add:
2220: ```env
2221: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
2222: ```
2223: 
2224: ## Chat System
2225: 
2226: ### Q: How do I add a chat interface to my page?
2227: **A:** Add chat configuration to your page's frontmatter:
2228: ```yaml
2229: ---
2230: layout: ../layouts/Layout.astro
2231: chatConfig:
2232:   provider: openai
2233:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2234:   temperature: 0.7
2235:   maxTokens: 2000
2236:   systemPrompt:
2237:     - type: text
2238:       text: "Your system prompt here"
2239: ---
2240: ```
2241: 
2242: ### Q: How do I customize the chat panel position?
2243: **A:** Use the `rightPanelMode` prop in your Layout component:
2244: ```astro
2245: <Layout
2246:   title="Your Page"
2247:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2248:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // or "half", "full", "floating", "icon"
2249: >
2250:   <!-- Your content -->
2251: </Layout>
2252: ```
2253: 
2254: ### Q: Can I customize the welcome message and suggestions?
2255: **A:** Yes, in your chat configuration:
2256: ```yaml
2257: chatConfig:
2258:   welcome:
2259:     message: "👋 Your welcome message"
2260:     avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2261:     suggestions:
2262:       - label: "💡 First Option"
2263:         prompt: "Your prompt here"
2264: ```
2265: 
2266: ## Content Management
2267: 
2268: ### Q: How do I create a chatbot for my markdown content?
2269: **A:** Create a markdown file with chat configuration in the frontmatter:
2270: ```markdown
2271: ---
2272: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2273: title: "Your Title"
2274: chatConfig:
2275:   systemPrompt:
2276:     - type: text
2277:       text: "Define your AI's expertise"
2278: ---
2279: 
2280: Your content here
2281: ```
2282: 
2283: ### Q: How do I organize my documentation?
2284: **A:** Use the following structure:
2285: ```
2286: src/content/docs/
2287: ├── index.md         # Main documentation page
2288: ├── getting-started/ # Getting started guides
2289: ├── features/       # Feature documentation
2290: └── api/           # API documentation
2291: ```
2292: 
2293: ### Q: How do I add images and assets?
2294: **A:** Place them in the `public` directory:
2295: ```
2296: public/
2297: ├── images/    # For images
2298: ├── icons/     # For icons
2299: └── assets/    # For other assets
2300: ```
2301: 
2302: ## Styling and Theming
2303: 
2304: ### Q: How do I customize the appearance?
2305: **A:** ONE uses Tailwind CSS. Customize in `tailwind.config.mjs`:
2306: ```javascript
2307: export default {
2308:   theme: {
2309:     extend: {
2310:       colors: {
2311:         primary: {...},
2312:         secondary: {...}
2313:       }
2314:     }
2315:   }
2316: }
2317: ```
2318: 
2319: ### Q: How do I switch between light and dark themes?
2320: **A:** Use the built-in theme system:
2321: ```typescript
2322: import { useTheme } from "@/hooks/use-theme";
2323: 
2324: const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
2325: ```
2326: 
2327: ## Performance
2328: 
2329: ### Q: How do I optimize chat performance?
2330: **A:** Several ways:
2331: 1. Use edge runtime
2332: 2. Implement proper caching
2333: 3. Optimize response sizes
2334: 4. Use streaming responses
2335: 
2336: ### Q: How do I implement caching?
2337: **A:** Use edge caching for API responses:
2338: ```typescript
2339: export const config = {
2340:   runtime: 'edge',
2341:   regions: ['all'],
2342: };
2343: ```
2344: 
2345: ## Troubleshooting
2346: 
2347: ### Q: Why isn't my chat interface showing up?
2348: **A:** Check these common issues:
2349: 1. Verify chatConfig in frontmatter
2350: 2. Ensure OpenAI API key is set
2351: 3. Check for console errors
2352: 4. Verify rightPanelMode setting
2353: 
2354: ### Q: Why are my API calls failing?
2355: **A:** Common solutions:
2356: 1. Verify API key in .env
2357: 2. Check API endpoint configuration
2358: 3. Verify rate limits
2359: 4. Check network connectivity
2360: 
2361: ### Q: How do I debug streaming responses?
2362: **A:** Use the browser's network tab:
2363: 1. Open DevTools
2364: 2. Go to Network tab
2365: 3. Filter for 'Fetch/XHR'
2366: 4. Look for streaming responses
2367: 
2368: ## Deployment
2369: 
2370: ### Q: How do I deploy my ONE application?
2371: **A:** Several options:
2372: 1. Vercel (recommended)
2373: 2. Netlify
2374: 3. CloudFlare
2375: 4. Custom server
2376: 
2377: ### Q: How do I handle environment variables in production?
2378: **A:** Set them in your hosting platform:
2379: ```env
2380: OPENAI_API_KEY=production_key
2381: API_ENDPOINT=production_endpoint
2382: ```
2383: 
2384: ## Development Best Practices
2385: 
2386: ### Q: What's the recommended way to structure a large application?
2387: **A:** Follow this structure:
2388: ```
2389: src/
2390: ├── components/    # Reusable components
2391: ├── layouts/       # Page layouts
2392: ├── content/       # Markdown content
2393: ├── pages/         # Routes
2394: ├── styles/        # Global styles
2395: └── lib/          # Utilities
2396: ```
2397: 
2398: ### Q: How do I implement proper error handling?
2399: **A:** Use try-catch blocks and error boundaries:
2400: ```typescript
2401: try {
2402:   // API calls
2403: } catch (error) {
2404:   if (error.response?.status === 429) {
2405:     // Handle rate limiting
2406:   }
2407:   // Handle other errors
2408: }
2409: ```
2410: 
2411: ### Q: How do I test my AI interactions?
2412: **A:** Use test modes and mock responses:
2413: ```typescript
2414: const testConfig = {
2415:   ...chatConfig,
2416:   provider: 'test',
2417:   mockResponses: [...]
2418: };
2419: ```

2456: # How ONE Works
2457: 
2458: ONE is a comprehensive framework for building AI-powered web applications with Astro. It combines high-performance static site generation with dynamic AI capabilities to create intelligent, responsive web experiences.
2459: 
2460: ## Core Architecture
2461: 
2462: ### Tech Stack
2463: - **Astro** - The core framework that enables high-performance static site generation
2464: - **React** - Used for interactive components and UI elements
2465: - **Assistant UI** - Provides the chat interface and AI interaction components
2466: - **Vercel AI SDK** - Handles AI model integration and streaming responses
2467: - **Tailwind CSS** - For responsive and customizable styling
2468: 
2469: ### Layout System
2470: 
2471: The framework uses a flexible layout system with three main components:
2472: 
2473: 1. **Main Grid**
2474:    - Configurable grid layout system
2475:    - Support for responsive design
2476:    - Dynamic panel sizing and positioning
2477: 
2478: 2. **Panel Modes**
2479:    ```typescript
2480:    type PanelMode = 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
2481:    ```
2482:    - `quarter`: 25% width side panel
2483:    - `half`: 50% width side panel
2484:    - `full`: Full screen display
2485:    - `floating`: Detached floating window
2486:    - `icon`: Minimized chat button
2487:    - `hidden`: No chat interface
2488: 
2489: 3. **Responsive Behavior**
2490:    - Automatic adaptation to screen sizes
2491:    - Mobile-first design approach
2492:    - Smooth transitions between states
2493: 
2494: ### AI Agent Implementation
2495: 
2496: Every page in ONE can have its own AI Agent, with specific knowledge about the page content:
2497: 
2498: 1. **Configuration Layer**
2499: ```typescript
2500: {
2501:     "provider": "openai",
2502:     "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
2503:     "apiEndpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
2504:     "runtime": "edge",
2505:     "temperature": 0.7,
2506:     "maxTokens": 2000,
2507:     "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful AI assistant.",
2508:     "userPrompt": "main content of the markdown file below"
2509: }
2510: ```
2511: 
2512: 2. **Chat Interface Layer**
2513: - Real-time message streaming
2514: - Markdown rendering
2515: - Message history and branching
2516: - Text-to-speech capabilities
2517: - Code syntax highlighting
2518: - Copy/edit functionality
2519: 
2520: 3. **Edge Runtime Layer**
2521: - Edge-based processing
2522: - Efficient data streaming
2523: - Optimized response handling
2524: 
2525: ## Content Management
2526: 
2527: ### 1. Blog System
2528: - Markdown-based content
2529: - Multiple view modes (list, grid, magazine)
2530: - Automatic reading time calculation
2531: - Rich media support
2532: - Category and tag organization
2533: 
2534: ### 2. Documentation System
2535: - Hierarchical structure
2536: - Section-based organization
2537: - Automated navigation
2538: - Version control support
2539: 
2540: ### 3. Page-Specific AI Agents
2541: - Contextual awareness
2542: - Custom knowledge base
2543: - Tailored responses
2544: - Dynamic suggestions
2545: 
2546: ## Advanced Features
2547: 
2548: ### 1. Real-time Interaction
2549: - Streaming responses
2550: - Interactive components
2551: - Dynamic content updates
2552: - Branch navigation
2553: - Message history
2554: 
2555: ### 2. UI Components
2556: - Floating chat interface
2557: - Customizable welcome screen
2558: - Quick suggestion buttons
2559: - Progress indicators
2560: - Error states
2561: 
2562: ### 3. Performance Optimization
2563: - Edge computing
2564: - Asset optimization
2565: - Lazy loading
2566: - Caching strategies
2567: - Response streaming
2568: 
2569: ## Configuration Examples
2570: 
2571: ### 1. Basic Chat Setup
2572: ```typescript
2573: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
2574:   systemPrompt: [{
2575:     type: "text",
2576:     text: "You are a helpful AI assistant."
2577:   }],
2578:   welcome: {
2579:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
2580:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
2581:     suggestions: [
2582:       {
2583:         label: "Get Started",
2584:         prompt: "How do I get started with ONE?"
2585:       }
2586:     ]
2587:   }
2588: });
2589: ```
2590: 
2591: ### 2. Custom Layout Configuration
2592: ```typescript
2593: <Layout 
2594:   title="Your Page"
2595:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2596:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
2597:   header={true}
2598:   footer={true}
2599: >
2600:   {/* Your content */}
2601: </Layout>
2602: ```
2603: 
2604: ### 3. Page-Specific Agent
2605: ```typescript
2606: const pageSpecificAgent = {
2607:   systemPrompt: `You are an expert on ${topic}...`,
2608:   contextData: pageContent,
2609:   parameters: {
2610:     temperature: 0.7,
2611:     maxTokens: 2000
2612:   }
2613: };
2614: ```
2615: # Content Collections
2616: 
2617: - **Schema Definitions**: Continue using `src/content/config.ts` with `zod` for type-safe content validation.
2618: - **Content Queries**: Utilize `getCollection()` for type-safe content retrieval.
2619: - **Frontmatter Schemas**: Define schemas using `defineCollection`.
2620: - **Single Entry Retrieval**: Employ `getEntryBySlug` for fetching individual entries.
2621: - **Content Relationships**: Leverage collection references to establish relationships between content items.
2622: 
2623: # View Transitions
2624: 
2625: - **Implementation**: Use `transition:name` and `transition:animate` directives to define view transitions.
2626: - **State Persistence**: Apply `transition:persist` to maintain component state during page transitions.
2627: - **Animation Configuration**: Set animations with `transition:animate="slide|fade|none"`.
2628: - **Event Handling**: Manage transition events using `document.addEventListener('astro:page-load')`.
2629: - **Prop Preservation**: Use `transition:persist-props` to retain specific props during transitions.
2630: 
2631: # Islands Architecture
2632: 
2633: - **Immediate Interactivity**: Apply `client:load` for components requiring immediate interactivity.
2634: - **Deferred Hydration**: Use `client:visible` for components that can delay hydration until visible.
2635: - **Client-Only Components**: Implement `client:only` when server-side rendering is unnecessary.
2636: - **Responsive Hydration**: Utilize `client:media` for components that hydrate based on media queries.
2637: - **Idle Hydration**: Leverage `client:idle` for non-critical interactive components.
2638: 
2639: # Server-Side Features
2640: 
2641: - **Cookies Management**: Use `Astro.cookies` to handle server-side cookies.
2642: - **Middleware**: Implement middleware with `defineMiddleware()` in `src/middleware`.
2643: - **Request Access**: Access request details via `Astro.request` in server endpoints.
2644: - **Dynamic Routes**: Handle dynamic routes using the `[...spread].astro` pattern.
2645: - **API Endpoints**: Create API endpoints in `src/pages/api` using `Response` objects.
2646: 
2647: # Image Optimization
2648: 
2649: - **Image Component**: Use the `Image` component with `src`, `alt`, and `width/height` props.
2650: - **Picture Component**: Implement the `Picture` component for art direction.
2651: - **Service Configuration**: Configure the image service in `astro.config.mjs`.
2652: - **Modern Formats**: Use `format="avif,webp"` for modern image formats.
2653: - **Responsive Images**: Apply the `densities` prop for responsive images.
2654: 
2655: # Integration System
2656: 
2657: - **Framework Integrations**: Configure integrations in `astro.config.mjs`.
2658: - **Deployment Adapters**: Use adapters like `adapter-vercel`, `adapter-netlify`, or `adapter-node` for deployment.
2659: - **Vite Plugins**: Implement Vite plugins through Astro integrations.
2660: - **UI Frameworks**: Configure renderers for UI frameworks as needed.
2661: - **Environment Variables**: Handle integration-specific environment variables appropriately.
2662: 
2663: # Routing and Pages
2664: 
2665: - **File-Based Routing**: Place pages in `src/pages` for automatic routing.
2666: - **Dynamic Parameters**: Use `[param].astro` for dynamic route parameters.
2667: - **Rest Parameters**: Implement `[...spread].astro` for rest parameters in routes.
2668: - **Redirects**: Handle redirects using `Astro.redirect`.
2669: - **Nested Layouts**: Implement nested layouts using slot patterns.
2670: 
2671: # Dos
2672: 
2673: - **Static Path Generation**: Use `getStaticPaths` for generating static paths.
2674: - **Hydration Strategies**: Implement appropriate island hydration strategies.
2675: - **Type-Safe Content**: Utilize content collections for type-safe content management.
2676: - **View Transitions**: Configure view transitions appropriately.
2677: - **SSR Capabilities**: Leverage server-side rendering capabilities effectively.
2678: 
2679: # Don'ts
2680: 
2681: - **Overusing `client:load`**: Avoid using `client:load` when `client:visible` suffices.
2682: - **Mixing SSR and `client:only`**: Never mix server-side rendering and `client:only` in the same component.
2683: - **Redundant Queries**: Avoid unnecessary content collection queries.
2684: - **Skipping Animations**: Don't skip view transition animations without reason.
2685: - **Bypassing Image Optimization**: Never bypass Astro's image optimization features.
2686: 
2687: By incorporating these practices, you can effectively leverage the features introduced in Astro 5.5 to enhance your project's performance and maintainability.
`````

  68: ## 3. Zod as Single Source of Truth
  69: 
  70: I use Zod as the single source of truth for all data validation and typing in my projects. This ensures:
  71: 
  72: 1. **Schema Definition:**
  73:    ```typescript
  74:    import { z } from 'zod';
  75:    
  76:    // Define schema once, use everywhere
  77:    const configSchema = z.object({
  78:      title: z.string(),
  79:      version: z.number(),
  80:      features: z.array(z.string()),
  81:      settings: z.object({
  82:        theme: z.enum(['light', 'dark']),
  83:        language: z.string(),
  84:      }),
  85:    });
  86:    
  87:    // TypeScript type is automatically inferred
  88:    type Config = z.infer<typeof configSchema>;
  89:    ```
  90: 
  91: 2. **Runtime Validation:**
  92:    ```typescript
  93:    // Validate data at runtime
  94:    const validateConfig = (data: unknown) => {
  95:      return configSchema.parse(data);
  96:    };
  97:    ```
  98: 
  99: 3. **Type Safety:**
 100:    ```typescript
 101:    // TypeScript knows the exact shape
 102:    const config: Config = validateConfig(data);
 103:    ```
 104: 
 105: **Key Benefits:**
 106: - Single schema definition for both runtime validation and TypeScript types
 107: - Automatic type inference eliminates type duplication
 108: - Runtime type checking catches invalid data early
 109: - Excellent IDE support and type hints
 110: - Composable and reusable schemas
 111: 
 112: **Best Practices:**
 113: - Define schemas in dedicated type files (src/types/*)
 114: - Use schema composition for complex types
 115: - Leverage Zod's rich validation features
 116: - Export both schema and inferred type
 117: - Add JSDoc comments for better documentation

 129: Add a Shadcn UI Component
 130: Shadcn UI  provides an excellent set of components that are an opinionated implementation of Radix UI  React components. Space Madness includes a few of these components as an efficient way to include high quality, accessible components with minimal development overhead.
 131: 
 132: You can add more components to your site via the Shadcn UI CLI  . Your site comes preconfigured with the config file at site-astro/src/components.json, so adding a new component is relatively easy. There are a few gotchas when working with Astro. We'll cover those in a later section.

 243: Update the styles
 244: The component code is configured in a few places. components.json specifies a color scheme. tailwind.config.mjs extends tailwind theme colors, borders, fonts, and animations. global.css is where most of our style variables are configured.
 245: 
 246: All style variables use HSL color input values.
 247: 
 248: An easy way to edit these values in global.css is to wrap your values in hsl(). Then you can use the built in color picker to modify your values.
 249: 
 250: Where you make your changes depends on how much control you want over the resulting code.
 251: 
 252: In general, if you want to keep to the Tailwind styles as closely as possible, make edits to the CSS variables in global.css.
 253: 
 254: If you want to get fancy with the spices, edit tailwind.config.mjs or write your own CSS using the Tailwind @extends directive.
 255: 
 256: One tool you might find helpful is this theme generation tool  for shadcn/ui.

 581: ## Final Instructions and Best Practices
 582: 
 583: 1. Component Composition: Combine Shadcn UI components to create more complex UI elements. For example, you might use a Card component with a Form inside for a login interface.
 584: 
 585: 2. Consistent Styling: Maintain consistency in your use of Tailwind CSS classes. Consider creating custom utility classes for frequently used combinations.
 586: 
 587: 3. State Management: For more complex applications, consider using Svelte stores for global state management. Implement stores in a separate file and import them where needed.
 588: 
 589: 4. Error Handling: Implement comprehensive error handling, including user-friendly error messages and logging for debugging purposes.
 590: 
 591: 5. Internationalization: If your application requires multiple languages, implement i18n using a library like svelte-i18n.
 592: 
 593: 6. Performance Monitoring: Implement performance monitoring and analytics to identify and address any performance issues.
 594: 
 595: 7. Code Organization: Keep your code modular and well-organized. Extract reusable logic into separate functions or components.
 596: 
 597: 8. Documentation: Maintain clear and up-to-date documentation for your components and pages. Include usage examples and prop definitions.
 598: 
 599: 9. Accessibility Testing: Regularly test your components and pages for accessibility using tools like axe-core or manual testing with screen readers.
 600: 
 601: 10. Responsive Design: Always design and implement with responsiveness in mind, testing on various device sizes and orientations.
 602: 
 603: 11. Version Control: Use meaningful commit messages and consider using conventional commits for better changelog generation.
 604: 
 605: 12. Code Review: If working in a team, implement a code review process to ensure code quality and knowledge sharing.
 606: 
 607: Remember, the key to successful development with SvelteKit and Shadcn UI is to leverage the strengths of both technologies while adhering to web development best practices. Always prioritize user experience, performance, and accessibility in your implementations.

1303: Error
1304: An error occurred.
1305: Accordion must be used within Accordion
1306: 
1307: Oh no! We have an error. Let's talk through the issue.
1308: 
1309: Astro uses an "island architecture  ", which means that each block of code on the site is an independent group of code. Astro does not assume that our Accordion component pieces fit together. Our Shadcn UI components assume that the components can talk to each other and share context. They cannot.
1310: 
1311: We can solve this in two ways.
1312: 
1313: Rewrite the ShadCN components so they work with Astro. This might involve re-architecting an existing solution that's built into a library.
1314: Wrap all of our Accordion components into one component where we can pass data to it. We lose the composability, but we avoid having to rewrite a lot of logic.
1315: For this guide, we'll go with option 2. If you want to see an example of option 1, check out Popover.tsx.
1316: 
1317: Let's create a new Accordion.tsx component.
1318: 
1319: We'll update the example to iterate over a data prop and render each AccordionItem.
1320: 
1321: site-astro/src/components/Accordion.tsx
1322: Copy to Clipboard
1323: import {
1324: 	Accordion as BaseAccordion,
1325: 	AccordionContent,
1326: 	AccordionItem,
1327: 	AccordionTrigger,
1328: } from "@/components/ui/accordion";
1329: 
1330: interface Props {
1331: 	data: {
1332: 		title: string;
1333: 		description: string;
1334: 	}[];
1335: }
1336: 
1337: export function Accordion({ data }: Props) {
1338: 	return (
1339: 		<BaseAccordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
1340: 			{data.map((item, i) => {
1341: 				return (
1342: 					<AccordionItem value={`item-${i.toFixed()}`}>
1343: 						<AccordionTrigger>{item.title}</AccordionTrigger>
1344: 						<AccordionContent>{item.description}</AccordionContent>
1345: 					</AccordionItem>
1346: 				);
1347: 			})}
1348: 		</BaseAccordion>
1349: 	);
1350: }
1351: Use it index.astro like this:
1352: 
1353: site-astro/src/pages/index.astro
1354: Copy to Clipboard
1355: ---
1356: import Layout from "../layouts/Layout.astro";
1357: import { Accordion } from "@/components/content/Accordion";
1358: 
1359: const accordionData = [
1360: 	{
1361: 		title: "Is it accessible?",
1362: 		description: "Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.",
1363: 	},
1364: 	{
1365: 		title: "Is it styled?",
1366: 		description:
1367: 			"Yes. It comes with default styles that matches the other components' aesthetic.",
1368: 	},
1369: 	{
1370: 		title: "Is it animated?",
1371: 		description:
1372: 			"Yes. It's animated by default, but you can disable it if you prefer.",
1373: 	},
1374: ];
1375: ---
1376: 
1377: <Layout>
1378: 	<main>
1379: 		<h1>Welcome to SiteName</h1>
1380: 		<Accordion data={accordionData} client:idle />
1381: 	</main>
1382: </Layout>
1383: Now we're in business.
1384: 
1385: Don't forget the client:idle attribute on our Accordion implementation. This tells Astro to load the necessary JS code on the client side so users can click to open/close each accordion item.
1386: 
1387: Astro now treats our entire accordion as one "island". The React context needed to wrap all accordion items can now execute in our browser without an issue.
1388: 
1389: Wrapping Up
1390: Hopefully, this gets you on your way to building quickly with Shadcn and Radix. Both tools should help you write better, more accessible components. They can be daunting to get started with, but they're well documented tools with thriving communities that can help you with your specific use case.
1391: 
1392: I got the Tabs working with client:visible and a workaround for Accordions described in this issue AREA44/astro-shadcn-ui-template#66
1393: 
1394: So basically wrap shadcn Tabs in another Tabs component. So Tabs inside of Tabs of Tabs ;). Then your new Tabs Component could be used with client:visible. And if you need dynamic tab content, just pass your data with props.
1395:
