1463: ## Implementing Tabs
1464: 
1465: 1. Create the base tabs components:
1466: 
1467: ```tsx
1468: // src/components/ui/tabs.tsx
1469: "use client"
1470: 
1471: import * as React from "react"
1472: import * as TabsPrimitive from "@radix-ui/react-tabs"
1473: import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
1474: 
1475: const Tabs = TabsPrimitive.Root
1476: 
1477: const TabsList = React.forwardRef<
1478: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>,
1479: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.List>
1480: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1481: 	<TabsPrimitive.List
1482: 		ref={ref}
1483: 		className={cn(
1484: 			"inline-flex h-10 items-center justify-center rounded-md bg-muted p-1 text-muted-foreground",
1485: 			className
1486: 		)}
1487: 		{...props}
1488: 	/>
1489: ))
1490: TabsList.displayName = TabsPrimitive.List.displayName
1491: 
1492: const TabsTrigger = React.forwardRef<
1493: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>,
1494: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Trigger>
1495: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1496: 	<TabsPrimitive.Trigger
1497: 		ref={ref}
1498: 		className={cn(
1499: 			"inline-flex items-center justify-center whitespace-nowrap rounded-sm px-3 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium ring-offset-background transition-all focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50 data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground data-[state=active]:shadow-sm",
1500: 			className
1501: 		)}
1502: 		{...props}
1503: 	/>
1504: ))
1505: TabsTrigger.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Trigger.displayName
1506: 
1507: const TabsContent = React.forwardRef<
1508: 	React.ElementRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>,
1509: 	React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof TabsPrimitive.Content>
1510: >(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
1511: 	<TabsPrimitive.Content
1512: 		ref={ref}
1513: 		className={cn(
1514: 			"mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2",
1515: 			className
1516: 		)}
1517: 		{...props}
1518: 	/>
1519: ))
1520: TabsContent.displayName = TabsPrimitive.Content.displayName
1521: 
1522: export { Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger, TabsContent }
1523: ```
1524: 
1525: 2. Create a reusable TabsContainer component:
1526: 
1527: ```tsx
1528: // src/components/ui/tabs-container.tsx
1529: 'use client';
1530: 
1531: import { Card } from './card';
1532: import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from './tabs';
1533: import * as React from 'react';
1534: 
1535: export interface TabItem {
1536: 	value: string;
1537: 	label: string;
1538: 	content: React.ReactNode;
1539: }
1540: 
1541: interface TabsContainerProps {
1542: 	items: TabItem[];
1543: 	defaultValue?: string;
1544: 	className?: string;
1545: 	gridCols?: number;
1546: }
1547: 
1548: export function TabsContainer({ 
1549: 	items, 
1550: 	defaultValue, 
1551: 	className = '',
1552: 	gridCols = 4 
1553: }: TabsContainerProps) {
1554: 	const [mounted, setMounted] = React.useState(false);
1555: 	const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = React.useState(defaultValue || items[0]?.value);
1556: 
1557: 	React.useEffect(() => {
1558: 		setMounted(true);
1559: 	}, []);
1560: 
1561: 	if (!mounted) {
1562: 		return null;
1563: 	}
1564: 
1565: 	return (
1566: 		<div className={`w-full ${className}`}>
1567: 			<Tabs defaultValue={activeTab} onValueChange={setActiveTab}>
1568: 				<TabsList className={`grid w-full grid-cols-${gridCols}`}>
1569: 					{items.map((item) => (
1570: 						<TabsTrigger 
1571: 							key={item.value} 
1572: 							value={item.value}
1573: 							className="data-[state=active]:bg-background data-[state=active]:text-foreground"
1574: 						>
1575: 							{item.label}
1576: 						</TabsTrigger>
1577: 					))}
1578: 				</TabsList>
1579: 				{items.map((item) => (
1580: 					<TabsContent 
1581: 						key={item.value} 
1582: 						value={item.value}
1583: 						className="mt-2 ring-offset-background focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-2"
1584: 					>
1585: 						<Card className="p-6">
1586: 							{item.content}
1587: 						</Card>
1588: 					</TabsContent>
1589: 				))}
1590: 			</Tabs>
1591: 		</div>
1592: 	);
1593: }
1594: ```
1595: 
1596: 3. Use the tabs in your Astro page:
1597: 
1598: ```astro
1599: ---
1600: import TabsExample from '../components/TabsExample';
1601: 
1602: const items = [
1603: 	{
1604: 		value: 'tab1',
1605: 		label: 'Tab 1',
1606: 		content: <div>Content for tab 1</div>
1607: 	},
1608: 	{
1609: 		value: 'tab2',
1610: 		label: 'Tab 2',
1611: 		content: <div>Content for tab 2</div>
1612: 	}
1613: ];
1614: ---
1615: 
1616: <div>
1617: 	<TabsExample client:load items={items} />
1618: </div>
1619: ```
1620: 
1621: ## Important Notes
1622: 
1623: 1. **Client Hydration**: Always use `client:load` when using interactive components like Tabs.
1624: 
1625: 2. **TypeScript Support**: Make sure your `tsconfig.json` includes:
1626: ```json
1627: {
1628: 	"compilerOptions": {
1629: 		"jsx": "react-jsx",
1630: 		"jsxImportSource": "react"
1631: 	}
1632: }
1633: ```
1634: 
1635: 3. **Styling**: The tabs component uses Tailwind CSS classes. Ensure your `globals.css` includes the necessary shadcn/ui base styles.
1636: 
1637: 4. **Error Handling**: Common issues and solutions:
1638: 	- If you see hydration errors, ensure you're using `client:load`
1639: 	- If styles aren't applying, check your Tailwind configuration
1640: 	- If tabs aren't interactive, verify React is properly set up in your Astro config
1641: 
1642: 5. **Best Practices**:
1643: 	- Keep tab content lightweight
1644: 	- Use semantic labels
1645: 	- Consider mobile responsiveness
1646: 	- Implement proper loading states
1647: 	- Handle edge cases (no tabs, single tab, etc.)
1648: 
1649: ## Example Implementation
1650: 
1651: Here's a complete example of a tabbed interface:
1652: 
1653: ```tsx
1654: // src/components/TabsExample.tsx
1655: import { TabsContainer, type TabItem } from '../ui/tabs-container';
1656: 
1657: interface TabsExampleProps {
1658: 	examples: {
1659: 		basic: string;
1660: 		advanced: string;
1661: 	};
1662: }
1663: 
1664: export default function TabsExample({ examples }: TabsExampleProps) {
1665: 	const items: TabItem[] = [
1666: 		{
1667: 			value: 'basic',
1668: 			label: 'Basic',
1669: 			content: (
1670: 				<>
1671: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Basic Example</h3>
1672: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Simple configuration:</p>
1673: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1674: 						{examples.basic}
1675: 					</pre>
1676: 				</>
1677: 			),
1678: 		},
1679: 		{
1680: 			value: 'advanced',
1681: 			label: 'Advanced',
1682: 			content: (
1683: 				<>
1684: 					<h3 className="text-xl font-medium mb-4">Advanced Example</h3>
1685: 					<p className="text-muted-foreground mb-4">Advanced configuration:</p>
1686: 					<pre className="text-sm overflow-auto p-4 bg-muted rounded-lg">
1687: 						{examples.advanced}
1688: 					</pre>
1689: 				</>
1690: 			),
1691: 		}
1692: 	];
1693: 
1694: 	return <TabsContainer items={items} defaultValue="basic" />;
1695: }
1696: ```
1697: 
1698: ## Troubleshooting
1699: 
1700: 1. **Hydration Errors**:
1701: 	- Use `client:load` directive
1702: 	- Ensure consistent server/client rendering
1703: 	- Add proper mounting checks
1704: 
1705: 2. **Styling Issues**:
1706: 	- Verify Tailwind configuration
1707: 	- Check class names
1708: 	- Ensure proper CSS imports
1709: 
1710: 3. **Interactivity Problems**:
1711: 	- Check React setup
1712: 	- Verify event handlers
1713: 	- Debug state management
1714: 
1715: 4. **Performance Optimization**:
1716: 	- Lazy load tab content
1717: 	- Implement proper caching
1718: 	- Optimize bundle size
1719: 
1720: You are an expert full-stack developer proficient in TypeScript, React, and modern UI/UX frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Radix UI), with particular expertise in Astro. Your task is to produce the most optimized and maintainable Astro code, following best practices and adhering to the principles of clean code and robust architecture.
1721: 
1722: ### Objective
1723: - Create an Astro solution that is not only functional but also adheres to the best practices in performance, security, and maintainability.
1724: 
1725: ### Code Style and Structure
1726: - Write concise, technical TypeScript code with accurate examples.
1727: - Use Astro components (.astro) for static content and framework components for interactive islands.
1728: - Favor iteration and modularization over code duplication.
1729: - Use descriptive variable names with auxiliary verbs (e.g., `isLoading`, `hasError`).
1730: - Structure files following Astro conventions with content collections, components, and layouts.
1731: - Use upercase for components e.g., `components/Chat`).
1732: 
1733: ### Optimization and Best Practices
1734: - Minimize client-side JavaScript using Astro's partial hydration with client:* directives.
1735: - Use appropriate client directives (client:load, client:idle, client:visible) based on component needs.
1736: - Implement View Transitions API for smooth page transitions.
1737: - Optimize images using Astro's built-in image optimization.
1738: - Leverage Astro's content collections for structured content management.
1739: 
1740: ### Error Handling and Validation
1741: - Prioritize error handling and edge cases:
1742:   - Use early returns for error conditions.
1743:   - Implement guard clauses to handle preconditions and invalid states early.
1744:   - Use custom error types for consistent error handling.
1745: 
1746: ### UI and Styling
1747: - Use modern UI frameworks (e.g., Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI) with proper Astro integration.
1748: - Implement consistent design and responsive patterns across platforms.
1749: - Utilize Astro's scoped styling capabilities when appropriate.
1750: 
1751: ### State Management and Data Fetching
1752: - Use Astro.props for component data passing.
1753: - Implement getStaticPaths() for dynamic route generation.
1754: - Use content collections API for structured content management.
1755: - Implement validation using Zod for schema validation.
1756: 
1757: ### Security and Performance
1758: - Leverage Astro's built-in security features and zero-JS-by-default approach.
1759: - Follow performance optimization techniques using Astro's static site generation.
1760: - Implement proper CSP headers and security best practices.
1761: 
1762: ### Testing and Documentation
1763: - Write unit tests for components using appropriate testing frameworks.
1764: - Provide clear and concise comments for complex logic.
1765: - Use JSDoc comments for functions and components to improve IDE intellisense.
1766: 
1767: ### Methodology
1768: 1. **System 2 Thinking**: Approach the problem with analytical rigor. Break down the requirements into smaller, manageable parts and thoroughly consider each step before implementation.
1769: 2. **Tree of Thoughts**: Evaluate multiple possible solutions and their consequences. Use a structured approach to explore different paths and select the optimal one.
1770: 3. **Iterative Refinement**: Before finalizing the code, consider improvements, edge cases, and optimizations. Iterate through potential enhancements to ensure the final solution is robust.
1771: 
1772: **Process**:
1773: 1. **Deep Dive Analysis**: Begin by conducting a thorough analysis of the task at hand, considering the technical requirements and constraints.
1774: 2. **Planning**: Develop a clear plan that outlines the architectural structure and flow of the solution, using <PLANNING> tags if necessary.
1775: 3. **Implementation**: Implement the solution step-by-step, ensuring that each part adheres to Astro's best practices.
1776: 4. **Review and Optimize**: Perform a review of the code, looking for opportunities to reduce client-side JavaScript and optimize performance.
1777: 5. **Finalization**: Finalize the code by ensuring it meets all requirements, maximizes static generation, and follows Astro's performance-first philosophy.

1787: 
1788: # Chat System Overview
1789: 
1790: ONE's chat system combines Astro, React, and the Assistant UI framework to deliver a powerful, flexible, and user-friendly chat interface with advanced AI capabilities.
1791: 
1792: ## Architecture
1793: 
1794: The chat system is built on a modular architecture with several key components:
1795: 
1796: ### 1. Frontend Components
1797: 
1798: #### Layout System
1799: - **Panel Modes**:
1800:   - `quarter`: 25% width side panel (default)
1801:   - `half`: 50% width side panel
1802:   - `full`: Full screen chat interface
1803:   - `floating`: Detached floating window
1804:   - `icon`: Minimized chat button
1805:   - `hidden`: No chat interface
1806: 
1807: - **Responsive Behavior**:
1808:   ```typescript
1809:   interface LayoutProps {
1810:     title: string;
1811:     description?: string;
1812:     header?: boolean;
1813:     footer?: boolean;
1814:     rightPanelMode?: 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
1815:     chatConfig?: ChatConfig;
1816:     content?: string;
1817:   }
1818:   ```
1819: 
1820: #### Chat Components
1821: 
1822: ##### Main Chat Page (`src/pages/chat.astro`)
1823: - Entry point for the chat interface
1824: - Configurable settings:
1825:   - System prompts
1826:   - Welcome messages
1827:   - Quick suggestions
1828:   - Layout modes
1829: - Integration with page content
1830: - AI context management
1831: 
1832: ##### Thread Component (`src/components/chat/thread.tsx`)
1833: - Core chat interface features:
1834:   - Scrollable message area
1835:   - Dynamic composition interface
1836:   - Customizable welcome screen
1837:   - Message styling and actions
1838:   - Branch navigation
1839:   - Voice synthesis
1840: 
1841: ### 2. Backend Architecture
1842: 
1843: #### Chat API (`src/pages/api/chat.ts`)
1844: - OpenAI API integration
1845: - Configurable parameters:
1846:   ```typescript
1847:   interface ChatAPIConfig {
1848:     provider: "openai";
1849:     model: string;
1850:     apiEndpoint: string;
1851:     temperature: number;
1852:     maxTokens: number;
1853:     systemPrompt: string | SystemPrompt[];
1854:     contextData?: string;
1855:     functions?: ChatFunction[];
1856:   }
1857:   ```
1858: - Edge runtime optimization
1859: - Error handling and recovery
1860: - Response streaming
1861: 
1862: ## Advanced Features
1863: 
1864: ### 1. Message Management
1865: - Real-time streaming responses
1866: - Markdown and code rendering
1867: - Message editing and history
1868: - Branch navigation
1869: - Copy functionality
1870: - Voice synthesis
1871: - Code syntax highlighting
1872: 
1873: ### 2. User Interface Modes
1874: 
1875: #### Quarter Mode (Default)
1876: ```typescript
1877: <Layout rightPanelMode="quarter">
1878:   <YourContent />
1879: </Layout>
1880: ```
1881: - 25% width side panel
1882: - Ideal for documentation and content-heavy pages
1883: - Maintains content visibility
1884: 
1885: #### Floating Mode
1886: ```typescript
1887: <Layout rightPanelMode="floating">
1888:   <YourContent />
1889: </Layout>
1890: ```
1891: - Detached window
1892: - Draggable interface
1893: - Minimal content interference
1894: 
1895: #### Icon Mode
1896: ```typescript
1897: <Layout rightPanelMode="icon">
1898:   <YourContent />
1899: </Layout>
1900: ```
1901: - Minimized chat button
1902: - Expands on click
1903: - Maximum content space
1904: 
1905: ### 3. Configuration System
1906: 
1907: #### Basic Configuration
1908: ```typescript
1909: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
1910:   systemPrompt: [{
1911:     type: "text",
1912:     text: "You are a helpful assistant."
1913:   }],
1914:   welcome: {
1915:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
1916:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
1917:     suggestions: [
1918:       {
1919:         label: "Get Started",
1920:         prompt: "How do I get started?"
1921:       }
1922:     ]
1923:   }
1924: });
1925: ```
1926: 
1927: #### Advanced Configuration
1928: ```typescript
1929: const advancedConfig = {
1930:   provider: "openai",
1931:   model: "gpt-4o-mini",
1932:   temperature: 0.7,
1933:   maxTokens: 2000,
1934:   features: {
1935:     textToSpeech: true,
1936:     codeHighlight: true,
1937:     markdown: true,
1938:     suggestions: true,
1939:     branchNavigation: true
1940:   },
1941:   styles: {
1942:     theme: "light" | "dark" | "system",
1943:     accentColor: "#0066FF",
1944:     messageSpacing: "comfortable" | "compact"
1945:   }
1946: };
1947: ```

1952: date: 2024-02-02

1956: 
1957: # Creating a Chatbot with Markdown
1958: 
1959: This tutorial will show you how to create a specialized AI chatbot using markdown files in ONE. We'll use the license page as an example to demonstrate how to create a knowledgeable AI assistant for your content.
1960: 
1961: ## Step 1: Create Your Markdown File
1962: 
1963: Create a new markdown file in your pages directory (e.g., `src/pages/your-page.md`):
1964: 
1965: ```markdown
1966: ---
1967: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
1968: title: "Your Page Title"
1969: description: "Your page description"
1970: chatConfig:
1971:   provider: openai
1972:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
1973:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
1974:   temperature: 0.7
1975:   maxTokens: 4000
1976:   systemPrompt:
1977:     - type: text
1978:       text: "Define your AI assistant's role and expertise here"
1979:   welcome:
1980:     message: "👋 Your welcome message here"
1981:     avatar: "/your-icon.svg"
1982:     suggestions:
1983:       - label: "First Option"
1984:         prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
1985: ---
1986: 
1987: # Your Content Here
1988: ```
1989: 
1990: ## Step 2: Configure the Chat System
1991: 
1992: ### Basic Configuration
1993: 
1994: In the frontmatter section of your markdown file, configure these essential parameters:
1995: 
1996: ```yaml
1997: chatConfig:
1998:   provider: openai           # AI provider
1999:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"      # Model to use
2000:   temperature: 0.7          # Response creativity (0-1)
2001:   maxTokens: 4000          # Maximum response length
2002: ```
2003: 
2004: ### Define the AI's Role
2005: 
2006: Create a clear system prompt that defines your AI's expertise:
2007: 
2008: ```yaml
2009: systemPrompt:
2010:   - type: text
2011:     text: "You are an expert in [your topic] focused on helping visitors understand [specific aspects]. You provide clear, accurate information about [key areas]."
2012: ```
2013: 
2014: Example from the license page:
2015: ```yaml
2016: systemPrompt:
2017:   - type: text
2018:     text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2019: ```
2020: 
2021: ### Set Up the Welcome Screen
2022: 
2023: Configure the initial interaction:
2024: 
2025: ```yaml
2026: welcome:
2027:   message: "👋 Your greeting message here"
2028:   avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2029:   suggestions:
2030:     - label: "💡 First Option"
2031:       prompt: "What would you like to know about...?"
2032:     - label: "🚀 Second Option"
2033:       prompt: "Another suggested question..."
2034: ```
2035: 
2036: ## Step 3: Structure Your Content
2037: 
2038: Organize your markdown content to help the AI understand the topic:
2039: 
2040: 1. **Clear Headings**
2041:    ```markdown
2042:    # Main Title
2043:    
2044:    ## Key Section
2045:    
2046:    ### Subsection
2047:    ```
2048: 
2049: 2. **Structured Information**
2050:    ```markdown
2051:    ## Key Points
2052:    
2053:    - **First Point** - Detailed explanation
2054:    - **Second Point** - More details
2055:    ```
2056: 
2057: 3. **Organized Sections**
2058:    ```markdown
2059:    ## Topic Area
2060:    
2061:    1. **Main Concept**
2062:       - Detail one
2063:       - Detail two
2064:    
2065:    2. **Another Concept**
2066:       - More information
2067:       - Additional details
2068:    ```
2069: 
2070: ## Step 4: Add Interactive Elements
2071: 
2072: Include elements that enhance user interaction:
2073: 
2074: ### Quick Access Buttons
2075: 
2076: ```yaml
2077: suggestions:
2078:   - label: "💡 Key Feature"
2079:     prompt: "Tell me about this feature"
2080:   - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2081:     prompt: "How do I begin?"
2082:   - label: "⚖️ Requirements"
2083:     prompt: "What are the requirements?"
2084: ```
2085: 
2086: ### Contact Information
2087: 
2088: ```markdown
2089: Contact [support@example.com](mailto:support@example.com) for assistance.
2090: ```
2091: 
2092: ## Real-World Example
2093: 
2094: Here's how the license page implements these concepts:
2095: 
2096: ```markdown
2097: ---
2098: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2099: title: "ONE License"
2100: description: "Maximum Freedom. Zero Restrictions"
2101: chatConfig:
2102:   provider: openai
2103:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2104:   apiEndpoint: "https://api.openai.com/v1"
2105:   temperature: 0.7
2106:   maxTokens: 4000
2107:   systemPrompt:
2108:     - type: text
2109:       text: "You are a licensing expert focused on helping visitors understand the ONE License terms and benefits. You provide clear, accurate information about licensing terms, commercial rights, and usage requirements."
2110:   welcome:
2111:     message: "👋 Hello! I can help explain the ONE License terms and how you can use them for your business."
2112:     avatar: "/icon.svg"
2113:     suggestions:
2114:       - label: "💡 Commercial Rights"
2115:         prompt: "What commercial rights do I get with the ONE License?"
2116:       - label: "🚀 Getting Started"
2117:         prompt: "What are the steps to start using the ONE License?"
2118: ---
2119: 
2120: # ONE License (Version 1.0)
2121: 
2122: ## Unlimited Commercial Freedom
2123: 
2124: ONE License gives you complete commercial freedom...
2125: 
2126: ## Key Benefits
2127: 
2128: - **✨ 100% Commercial Rights** - Sell products and services at any price point
2129: - **🚀 Full Modification Rights** - Customize and adapt the software freely
2130: ```
2131: 
2132: ## Best Practices
2133: 
2134: 1. **System Prompt**
2135:    - Be specific about the AI's role
2136:    - Define clear areas of expertise
2137:    - Set appropriate boundaries
2138: 
2139: 2. **Welcome Message**
2140:    - Keep it friendly and clear
2141:    - Set proper expectations
2142:    - Provide useful starting points
2143: 
2144: 3. **Content Structure**
2145:    - Use clear headings
2146:    - Organize information logically
2147:    - Include relevant details
2148: 
2149: 4. **Suggestions**
2150:    - Cover common questions
2151:    - Use descriptive labels
2152:    - Provide clear prompts
2153: 
2154: ## Troubleshooting
2155: 
2156: ### Common Issues
2157: 
2158: 1. **AI Responses Off-Topic**
2159:    - Review and refine system prompt
2160:    - Check content organization
2161:    - Add more specific context
2162: 
2163: 2. **Welcome Message Not Showing**
2164:    - Verify frontmatter formatting
2165:    - Check avatar path
2166:    - Validate YAML syntax
2167: 
2168: 3. **Suggestions Not Working**
2169:    - Check label/prompt format
2170:    - Verify YAML indentation
2171:    - Ensure unique labels
2172: 
2173: ## Next Steps
2174: 
2175: After creating your chatbot:
2176: 
2177: 1. Test different queries
2178: 2. Refine the system prompt
2179: 3. Add more suggestions
2180: 4. Monitor user interactions
2181: 5. Update content as needed

2195: 
2196: # Development FAQ
2197: 
2198: Common questions and answers about developing applications with ONE framework.
2199: 
2200: ## Getting Started
2201: 
2202: ### Q: What are the minimum requirements to run ONE?
2203: **A:** You need:
2204: - Node.js 18 or higher
2205: - pnpm package manager
2206: - An OpenAI API key
2207: - Basic knowledge of Astro and React
2208: 
2209: ### Q: How do I install ONE?
2210: **A:** Use the following commands:
2211: ```bash
2212: # Create new project
2213: pnpm create astro@latest my-one-app -- --template one
2214: 
2215: # Install dependencies
2216: cd my-one-app
2217: pnpm install
2218: ```
2219: 
2220: ### Q: How do I set up my OpenAI API key?
2221: **A:** Create a `.env` file in your project root and add:
2222: ```env
2223: OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
2224: ```
2225: 
2226: ## Chat System
2227: 
2228: ### Q: How do I add a chat interface to my page?
2229: **A:** Add chat configuration to your page's frontmatter:
2230: ```yaml
2231: ---
2232: layout: ../layouts/Layout.astro
2233: chatConfig:
2234:   provider: openai
2235:   model: "gpt-4o-mini"
2236:   temperature: 0.7
2237:   maxTokens: 2000
2238:   systemPrompt:
2239:     - type: text
2240:       text: "Your system prompt here"
2241: ---
2242: ```
2243: 
2244: ### Q: How do I customize the chat panel position?
2245: **A:** Use the `rightPanelMode` prop in your Layout component:
2246: ```astro
2247: <Layout
2248:   title="Your Page"
2249:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2250:   rightPanelMode="quarter" // or "half", "full", "floating", "icon"
2251: >
2252:   <!-- Your content -->
2253: </Layout>
2254: ```
2255: 
2256: ### Q: Can I customize the welcome message and suggestions?
2257: **A:** Yes, in your chat configuration:
2258: ```yaml
2259: chatConfig:
2260:   welcome:
2261:     message: "👋 Your welcome message"
2262:     avatar: "/path/to/icon.svg"
2263:     suggestions:
2264:       - label: "💡 First Option"
2265:         prompt: "Your prompt here"
2266: ```
2267: 
2268: ## Content Management
2269: 
2270: ### Q: How do I create a chatbot for my markdown content?
2271: **A:** Create a markdown file with chat configuration in the frontmatter:
2272: ```markdown
2273: ---
2274: layout: ../layouts/Text.astro
2275: title: "Your Title"
2276: chatConfig:
2277:   systemPrompt:
2278:     - type: text
2279:       text: "Define your AI's expertise"
2280: ---
2281: 
2282: Your content here
2283: ```
2284: 
2285: ### Q: How do I organize my documentation?
2286: **A:** Use the following structure:
2287: ```
2288: src/content/docs/
2289: ├── index.md         # Main documentation page
2290: ├── getting-started/ # Getting started guides
2291: ├── features/       # Feature documentation
2292: └── api/           # API documentation
2293: ```
2294: 
2295: ### Q: How do I add images and assets?
2296: **A:** Place them in the `public` directory:
2297: ```
2298: public/
2299: ├── images/    # For images
2300: ├── icons/     # For icons
2301: └── assets/    # For other assets
2302: ```
2303: 
2304: ## Styling and Theming
2305: 
2306: ### Q: How do I customize the appearance?
2307: **A:** ONE uses Tailwind CSS. Customize in `tailwind.config.mjs`:
2308: ```javascript
2309: export default {
2310:   theme: {
2311:     extend: {
2312:       colors: {
2313:         primary: {...},
2314:         secondary: {...}
2315:       }
2316:     }
2317:   }
2318: }
2319: ```
2320: 
2321: ### Q: How do I switch between light and dark themes?
2322: **A:** Use the built-in theme system:
2323: ```typescript
2324: import { useTheme } from "@/hooks/use-theme";
2325: 
2326: const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
2327: ```
2328: 
2329: ## Performance
2330: 
2331: ### Q: How do I optimize chat performance?
2332: **A:** Several ways:
2333: 1. Use edge runtime
2334: 2. Implement proper caching
2335: 3. Optimize response sizes
2336: 4. Use streaming responses
2337: 
2338: ### Q: How do I implement caching?
2339: **A:** Use edge caching for API responses:
2340: ```typescript
2341: export const config = {
2342:   runtime: 'edge',
2343:   regions: ['all'],
2344: };
2345: ```
2346: 
2347: ## Troubleshooting
2348: 
2349: ### Q: Why isn't my chat interface showing up?
2350: **A:** Check these common issues:
2351: 1. Verify chatConfig in frontmatter
2352: 2. Ensure OpenAI API key is set
2353: 3. Check for console errors
2354: 4. Verify rightPanelMode setting
2355: 
2356: ### Q: Why are my API calls failing?
2357: **A:** Common solutions:
2358: 1. Verify API key in .env
2359: 2. Check API endpoint configuration
2360: 3. Verify rate limits
2361: 4. Check network connectivity
2362: 
2363: ### Q: How do I debug streaming responses?
2364: **A:** Use the browser's network tab:
2365: 1. Open DevTools
2366: 2. Go to Network tab
2367: 3. Filter for 'Fetch/XHR'
2368: 4. Look for streaming responses
2369: 
2370: ## Deployment
2371: 
2372: ### Q: How do I deploy my ONE application?
2373: **A:** Several options:
2374: 1. Vercel (recommended)
2375: 2. Netlify
2376: 3. CloudFlare
2377: 4. Custom server
2378: 
2379: ### Q: How do I handle environment variables in production?
2380: **A:** Set them in your hosting platform:
2381: ```env
2382: OPENAI_API_KEY=production_key
2383: API_ENDPOINT=production_endpoint
2384: ```
2385: 
2386: ## Development Best Practices
2387: 
2388: ### Q: What's the recommended way to structure a large application?
2389: **A:** Follow this structure:
2390: ```
2391: src/
2392: ├── components/    # Reusable components
2393: ├── layouts/       # Page layouts
2394: ├── content/       # Markdown content
2395: ├── pages/         # Routes
2396: ├── styles/        # Global styles
2397: └── lib/          # Utilities
2398: ```
2399: 
2400: ### Q: How do I implement proper error handling?
2401: **A:** Use try-catch blocks and error boundaries:
2402: ```typescript
2403: try {
2404:   // API calls
2405: } catch (error) {
2406:   if (error.response?.status === 429) {
2407:     // Handle rate limiting
2408:   }
2409:   // Handle other errors
2410: }
2411: ```
2412: 
2413: ### Q: How do I test my AI interactions?
2414: **A:** Use test modes and mock responses:
2415: ```typescript
2416: const testConfig = {
2417:   ...chatConfig,
2418:   provider: 'test',
2419:   mockResponses: [...]
2420: };
2421: ```
2422: 
2423: ## Commercial Usage
2424: 
2425: ### Q: Can I use ONE in a commercial project?
2426: **A:** Yes, ONE License provides:
2427: - Full commercial rights
2428: - White-label options
2429: - No royalty fees
2430: - Enterprise support
2431: 
2432: ### Q: How do I remove ONE branding?
2433: **A:** Contact [agent@one.ie](mailto:agent@one.ie) for white-label rights.
2434: 
2435: ## Support and Resources
2436: 
2437: ### Q: Where can I get help?
2438: **A:** Several options:
2439: 1. [Documentation](/docs)
2440: 3. [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/one-ie/one/issues)
2441: 4. Email support@one.ie
2442: 
2443: ### Q: How do I report bugs?
2444: **A:** Open an issue on GitHub with:
2445: - Description of the problem
2446: - Steps to reproduce
2447: - Expected vs actual behavior
2448: - Environment details

2457: 
2458: # How ONE Works
2459: 
2460: ONE is a comprehensive framework for building AI-powered web applications with Astro. It combines high-performance static site generation with dynamic AI capabilities to create intelligent, responsive web experiences.
2461: 
2462: ## Core Architecture
2463: 
2464: ### Tech Stack
2465: - **Astro** - The core framework that enables high-performance static site generation
2466: - **React** - Used for interactive components and UI elements
2467: - **Assistant UI** - Provides the chat interface and AI interaction components
2468: - **Vercel AI SDK** - Handles AI model integration and streaming responses
2469: - **Tailwind CSS** - For responsive and customizable styling
2470: 
2471: ### Layout System
2472: 
2473: The framework uses a flexible layout system with three main components:
2474: 
2475: 1. **Main Grid**
2476:    - Configurable grid layout system
2477:    - Support for responsive design
2478:    - Dynamic panel sizing and positioning
2479: 
2480: 2. **Panel Modes**
2481:    ```typescript
2482:    type PanelMode = 'hidden' | 'full' | 'half' | 'quarter' | 'floating' | 'icon';
2483:    ```
2484:    - `quarter`: 25% width side panel
2485:    - `half`: 50% width side panel
2486:    - `full`: Full screen display
2487:    - `floating`: Detached floating window
2488:    - `icon`: Minimized chat button
2489:    - `hidden`: No chat interface
2490: 
2491: 3. **Responsive Behavior**
2492:    - Automatic adaptation to screen sizes
2493:    - Mobile-first design approach
2494:    - Smooth transitions between states
2495: 
2496: ### AI Agent Implementation
2497: 
2498: Every page in ONE can have its own AI Agent, with specific knowledge about the page content:
2499: 
2500: 1. **Configuration Layer**
2501: ```typescript
2502: {
2503:     "provider": "openai",
2504:     "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
2505:     "apiEndpoint": "https://api.openai.com/v1",
2506:     "runtime": "edge",
2507:     "temperature": 0.7,
2508:     "maxTokens": 2000,
2509:     "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful AI assistant.",
2510:     "userPrompt": "main content of the markdown file below"
2511: }
2512: ```
2513: 
2514: 2. **Chat Interface Layer**
2515: - Real-time message streaming
2516: - Markdown rendering
2517: - Message history and branching
2518: - Text-to-speech capabilities
2519: - Code syntax highlighting
2520: - Copy/edit functionality
2521: 
2522: 3. **Edge Runtime Layer**
2523: - Edge-based processing
2524: - Efficient data streaming
2525: - Optimized response handling
2526: 
2527: ## Content Management
2528: 
2529: ### 1. Blog System
2530: - Markdown-based content
2531: - Multiple view modes (list, grid, magazine)
2532: - Automatic reading time calculation
2533: - Rich media support
2534: - Category and tag organization
2535: 
2536: ### 2. Documentation System
2537: - Hierarchical structure
2538: - Section-based organization
2539: - Automated navigation
2540: - Version control support
2541: 
2542: ### 3. Page-Specific AI Agents
2543: - Contextual awareness
2544: - Custom knowledge base
2545: - Tailored responses
2546: - Dynamic suggestions
2547: 
2548: ## Advanced Features
2549: 
2550: ### 1. Real-time Interaction
2551: - Streaming responses
2552: - Interactive components
2553: - Dynamic content updates
2554: - Branch navigation
2555: - Message history
2556: 
2557: ### 2. UI Components
2558: - Floating chat interface
2559: - Customizable welcome screen
2560: - Quick suggestion buttons
2561: - Progress indicators
2562: - Error states
2563: 
2564: ### 3. Performance Optimization
2565: - Edge computing
2566: - Asset optimization
2567: - Lazy loading
2568: - Caching strategies
2569: - Response streaming
2570: 
2571: ## Configuration Examples
2572: 
2573: ### 1. Basic Chat Setup
2574: ```typescript
2575: const chatConfig = ChatConfigSchema.parse({
2576:   systemPrompt: [{
2577:     type: "text",
2578:     text: "You are a helpful AI assistant."
2579:   }],
2580:   welcome: {
2581:     message: "👋 How can I help you today?",
2582:     avatar: "/icon.svg",
2583:     suggestions: [
2584:       {
2585:         label: "Get Started",
2586:         prompt: "How do I get started with ONE?"
2587:       }
2588:     ]
2589:   }
2590: });
2591: ```
2592: 
2593: ### 2. Custom Layout Configuration
2594: ```typescript
2595: <Layout 
2596:   title="Your Page"
2597:   chatConfig={chatConfig}
2598:   rightPanelMode="quarter"
2599:   header={true}
2600:   footer={true}
2601: >
2602:   {/* Your content */}
2603: </Layout>
2604: ```
2605: 
2606: ### 3. Page-Specific Agent
2607: ```typescript
2608: const pageSpecificAgent = {
2609:   systemPrompt: `You are an expert on ${topic}...`,
2610:   contextData: pageContent,
2611:   parameters: {
2612:     temperature: 0.7,
2613:     maxTokens: 2000
2614:   }
2615: };
2616: ```
`````

 20:   const deleteAgent = useMutation(api.agents.mutations.removeMine);
 21:   const shuffleAvatar = useMutation(api.agents.mutations.shuffleAvatar);
 22:   const updateAgent = useMutation(api.agents.mutations.updateMine);

 25:   const [editedName, setEditedName] = React.useState("");
 26:   const [isShufflingAvatar, setIsShufflingAvatar] = React.useState(false);
 27:   const onApiError = useApiErrorHandler();
 28: 
 29:   React.useEffect(() => {
 30:     if (agent?.name) setEditedName(agent.name);
 31:   }, [agent?.name]);
 32: 
 33:   const handleNameSubmit = async () => {
 34:     if (!editedName.trim() || editedName === agent?.name) {
 35:       setIsEditingName(false);
 36:       return;
 37:     }
 38: 
 39:     if (!agent) return;
 40: 
 41:     await updateAgent({
 42:       agentId,
 43:       name: editedName,
 44:       description: agent.description,
 45:       personality: agent.personality,
 46:       tools: agent.tools,
 47:     })
 48:       .catch(onApiError)
 49:       .finally(() => setIsEditingName(false));
 50:   };
 51: 
 52:   const handleKeyDown = (e: React.KeyboardEvent) => {
 53:     if (e.key === "Enter") {
 54:       e.preventDefault();
 55:       handleNameSubmit();
 56:     } else if (e.key === "Escape") {
 57:       setIsEditingName(false);
 58:       setEditedName(agent?.name ?? "");
 59:     }
 60:   };
 61: 
 62:   if (!agent)
 63:     return (
 64:       <div className="flex-1 p-8">
 65:         <div className="max-w-2xl mx-auto space-y-6">
 66:           <Skeleton className="h-48 w-48 rounded-full mx-auto" />
 67:           <Skeleton className="h-8 w-48 mx-auto" />
 68:           <Skeleton className="h-24 w-full" />
 69:           <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-4">
 70:             <Skeleton className="h-32" />
 71:             <Skeleton className="h-32" />
 72:           </div>
 73:         </div>
 74:       </div>
 75:     );
 76: 
 77:   return (
 78:     <div className="flex-1 p-8">
 79:       <div className="max-w-2xl mx-auto space-y-8">
 80:         <div className="text-center">
 81:           <div className="relative inline-block">
 82:             <AgentAvatar
 83:               avatarUrl={agent.avatarUrl}
 84:               name={agent.name}
 85:               size="lg"
 86:             />
 87:             <Button
 88:               variant="secondary"
 89:               size="icon"
 90:               className="absolute bottom-6 -right-2"
 91:               disabled={isShufflingAvatar}
 92:               onClick={async () => {
 93:                 setIsShufflingAvatar(true);
 94:                 await shuffleAvatar({
 95:                   agentId,
 96:                 })
 97:                   .catch(onApiError)
 98:                   .finally(() => setIsShufflingAvatar(false));
 99:               }}
100:             >
101:               {isShufflingAvatar ? (
102:                 <Loader2 className="h-4 w-4 animate-spin" />
103:               ) : (
104:                 <Shuffle className="h-4 w-4" />
105:               )}
106:             </Button>
107:           </div>
108:           <div className="flex items-center justify-center gap-2 mb-2">
109:             {isEditingName ? (
110:               <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
111:                 <Input
112:                   value={editedName}
113:                   onChange={(e) => setEditedName(e.target.value)}
114:                   onKeyDown={handleKeyDown}
115:                   className="text-2xl font-bold text-center w-64"
116:                   autoFocus
117:                 />
118:                 <Button variant="ghost" size="icon" onClick={handleNameSubmit}>
119:                   <Check className="h-4 w-4" />
120:                 </Button>
121:               </div>
122:             ) : (
123:               <>
124:                 <h1 className="text-3xl font-bold">{agent.name}</h1>
125:                 <Button
126:                   variant="ghost"
127:                   size="icon"
128:                   onClick={() => setIsEditingName(true)}
129:                 >
130:                   <Pencil className="h-4 w-4" />
131:                 </Button>
132:               </>
133:             )}
134:           </div>
135:         </div>
136:         <AgentDescription
137:           agentId={agent._id}
138:           name={agent.name}
139:           description={agent.description}
140:           personality={agent.personality}
141:           tools={agent.tools}
142:         />
143:         <div className="grid grid-cols-2 gap-6">
144:           <AgentPersonality
145:             agentId={agent._id}
146:             name={agent.name}
147:             description={agent.description}
148:             personality={agent.personality}
149:             tools={agent.tools}
150:           />
151:           <AgentTools
152:             agentId={agent._id}
153:             name={agent.name}
154:             description={agent.description}
155:             personality={agent.personality}
156:             tools={agent.tools as AgentToolName[]}
157:           />
158:         </div>

161:         </div>

163:           <Button
164:             variant="destructive"
165:             onClick={() => setShowDeleteConfirm(true)}
166:           >
167:             Delete Agent
168:           </Button>
169:         </div>
170: 
171:         <Confirm
172:           open={showDeleteConfirm}
173:           onOpenChange={setShowDeleteConfirm}
174:           title="Delete Agent"
175:           description={`Are you sure you want to delete ${agent.name}? This action cannot be undone.`}
176:           confirmText="Delete"
177:           cancelText="Cancel"
178:           onConfirm={() =>

181:               .catch(onApiError)

183:           variant="destructive"
184:         />
185:       </div>
186:     </div>
187:   );
188: };

`````typescript
  1: import * as React from "react";

  9: import {
 10:   DropdownMenu,
 11:   DropdownMenuContent,
 12:   DropdownMenuItem,
 13:   DropdownMenuTrigger,
 14: } from "@/components/ui/dropdown-menu";
 15: import {
 16:   UserChoosableToolName,
 17:   userChoosableToolDefinitions,
 18:   toolDefinitions,
 19:   AgentToolName,
 20: } from "../../../../shared/tools";
 21: 
 22: interface AgentToolsProps {
 23:   agentId: Id<"agents">;
 24:   name: string;
 25:   description: string;
 26:   personality: string;
 27:   tools: AgentToolName[];
 28: }
 29: 
 30: export const AgentTools: React.FC<AgentToolsProps> = ({
 31:   agentId,
 32:   name,
 33:   description,
 34:   personality,
 35:   tools,
 36: }) => {
 37:   const updateAgent = useMutation(api.agents.mutations.updateMine);
 38:   const [isEditing, setIsEditing] = React.useState(false);
 39: 
 40:   const handleRemoveTool = async (toolToRemove: AgentToolName) => {
 41:     await updateAgent({
 42:       agentId,
 43:       name,
 44:       description,
 45:       personality,
 46:       tools: tools.filter((tool) => tool !== toolToRemove),
 47:     });
 48:   };
 49: 
 50:   const handleAddTool = async (toolToAdd: UserChoosableToolName) => {
 51:     if (tools.includes(toolToAdd)) return;
 52:     await updateAgent({
 53:       agentId,
 54:       name,
 55:       description,
 56:       personality,
 57:       tools: [...tools, toolToAdd],
 58:     });
 59:   };
 60: 
 61: 
 62:   const availableTools: Array<
 63:     [UserChoosableToolName, (typeof toolDefinitions)[UserChoosableToolName]]
 64:   > = [];
 65: 
 66: 
 67:   Object.keys(userChoosableToolDefinitions).forEach((key) => {
 68:     const toolKey = key as UserChoosableToolName;
 69:     if (!tools.includes(toolKey)) {
 70:       availableTools.push([toolKey, toolDefinitions[toolKey]]);
 71:     }
 72:   });
 73: 
 74:   return (
 75:     <Card className="p-6">
 76:       <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-4">
 77:         <h2 className="text-lg font-semibold">Tools</h2>
 78:         <Button
 79:           variant="ghost"
 80:           size="sm"
 81:           className="h-8 w-8 p-0"
 82:           onClick={() => setIsEditing(!isEditing)}
 83:         >
 84:           <Pencil className="h-4 w-4" />
 85:         </Button>
 86:       </div>
 87:       <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
 88:         {tools.map((tool) => (
 89:           <Badge
 90:             key={tool}
 91:             variant="secondary"
 92:             className="flex items-center gap-1"
 93:           >
 94:             {tool}
 95:             {isEditing && (
 96:               <button
 97:                 onClick={() => handleRemoveTool(tool)}
 98:                 className="ml-1 hover:text-destructive"
 99:               >
100:                 <X className="h-3 w-3" />
101:               </button>
102:             )}
103:           </Badge>
104:         ))}
105:         {isEditing && availableTools.length > 0 && (
106:           <DropdownMenu>
107:             <DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>
108:               <Button variant="outline" size="sm" className="h-6">
109:                 <Plus className="h-3 w-3 mr-1" />
110:                 Add Tool
111:               </Button>
112:             </DropdownMenuTrigger>
113:             <DropdownMenuContent>
114:               {availableTools.map(([key, tool]) => (
115:                 <DropdownMenuItem key={key} onClick={() => handleAddTool(key)}>
116:                   <div>
117:                     <div className="font-medium">{tool.name}</div>
118:                     <div className="text-xs text-muted-foreground">
119:                       {tool.description}
120:                     </div>
121:                   </div>
122:                 </DropdownMenuItem>
123:               ))}
124:             </DropdownMenuContent>
125:           </DropdownMenu>
126:         )}
127:       </div>
128:     </Card>
129:   );
130: };
`````

 1: import React, { createContext, useContext, useState, ReactNode } from "react";
 2: 
 3: interface ChatContextType {
 4:   replyToMention: string | null;
 5:   setReplyToMention: (mention: string | null) => void;
 6:   shouldFocusInput: boolean;
 7:   setShouldFocusInput: (focus: boolean) => void;
 8: }
 9: 
10: const ChatContext = createContext<ChatContextType | undefined>(undefined);
11: 
12: export function useChatContext() {
13:   const context = useContext(ChatContext);
14:   if (context === undefined) {
15:     throw new Error("useChatContext must be used within a ChatProvider");
16:   }

18: }
19: 
20: interface ChatProviderProps {
21:   children: ReactNode;
22: }
23: 
24: export function ChatProvider({ children }: ChatProviderProps) {

26:   const [shouldFocusInput, setShouldFocusInput] = useState(false);
27: 
28:   return (
29:     <ChatContext.Provider
30:       value={{
31:         replyToMention,
32:         setReplyToMention,
33:         shouldFocusInput,
34:         setShouldFocusInput,
35:       }}
36:     >
37:       {children}
38:     </ChatContext.Provider>

 50: 
 51:   const timeAgo = useTimeAgo(message._creationTime);
 52: 
 53:   const handleReply = () => {
 54:     if (participant?.kind === "agent" && matchingAgent) {
 55:       const mentionText = createMentionString({
 56:         kind: "agent",

 58:         name: participant.name ?? "Agent",
 59:       });
 60:       setReplyToMention(mentionText + " ");
 61:       setShouldFocusInput(true);
 62:     }
 63:   };
 64: 
 65:   const renderMessageContent = (content: string) => {
 66:     const parts = splitMessageContent(content);
 67: 
 68:     return parts.map((part, index) => {
 69:       if (part.type === "text") {

 74:             components={{
 75: 
 76:               a: (props) => (

 78:                   {...props}
 79:                   target="_blank"
 80:                   rel="noopener noreferrer"
 81:                   className={`${
 82:                     participant?.kind === "user"
 83:                       ? "text-primary-foreground  decoration-primary-foreground/70 hover:decoration-primary-foreground hover:text-orange-200"
 84:                       : "text-blue-600 dark:text-blue-400 font-medium  decoration-blue-600/70 dark:decoration-blue-400/70 hover:text-orange-500 dark:hover:text-orange-400"
 85:                   } transition-all`}
 86:                 />
 87:               ),
 88: 
 89:               p: (props) => <span {...props} />,
 90:             }}
 91:           >
 92:             {part.content}
 93:           </ReactMarkdown>
 94:         );
 95:       } else {

100:               key={`mention-${index}`}
101:               display={reference.display}

106:         } else {

110:               display={reference.display}

112:               isInUserMessage={participant?.kind === "user"}

114:           );
115:         }
116:       }
117:     });
118:   };
119: 
120:   return (

122:       className={`flex items-start gap-3 ${
123:         participant?.kind === "user" ? "flex-row-reverse" : "flex-row"
124:       }`}

## File: components/misc/hooks.ts
`````typescript
 1: import * as React from "react";
 2: import {
 3:   formatDistanceToNow,
 4:   differenceInSeconds,
 5:   differenceInMinutes,
 6:   differenceInHours,
 7: } from "date-fns";
 8: 
 9: 
10: 
11: 
12: 
13: export const useTimeAgo = (timestamp: number) => {
14:   const [timeAgo, setTimeAgo] = React.useState(() =>
15:     formatDistanceToNow(new Date(timestamp), { addSuffix: true }),
16:   );
17: 
18:   React.useEffect(() => {
19:     const date = new Date(timestamp);
20: 
21:     const getUpdateInterval = () => {
22:       const secondsOld = differenceInSeconds(new Date(), date);
23:       const minutesOld = differenceInMinutes(new Date(), date);
24:       const hoursOld = differenceInHours(new Date(), date);
25: 
26:       if (secondsOld < 60) return 1000;
27:       if (minutesOld < 60) return 60000;
28:       if (hoursOld < 24) return 300000;
29:       return 3600000;
30:     };
31: 
32:     const updateTimeAgo = () => {
33:       setTimeAgo(formatDistanceToNow(date, { addSuffix: true }));
34:     };
35: 
36:     const interval = setInterval(() => {
37:       updateTimeAgo();
38: 
39:       clearInterval(interval);
40:       const newInterval = setInterval(updateTimeAgo, getUpdateInterval());
41:       return () => clearInterval(newInterval);
42:     }, getUpdateInterval());
43: 
44:     return () => clearInterval(interval);
45:   }, [timestamp]);
46: 
47:   return timeAgo;
48: };
`````

`````typescript
  1: import * as React from "react";
  2: import { Button } from "./button";
  3: import { Textarea } from "./textarea";
  4: import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";
  5: import { useApiErrorHandler } from "@/components/misc/errors";
  6: 
  7: export interface EditableTextHandle {
  8:   startEditing: () => void;
  9: }
 10: 
 11: interface EditableTextProps {
 12:   value: string;
 13:   onSave: (value: string) => Promise<void>;
 14:   className?: string;
 15:   textClassName?: string;
 16:   editRef?: React.RefObject<EditableTextHandle | null>;
 17: }
 18: 
 19: export const EditableText: React.FC<EditableTextProps> = ({
 20:   value,
 21:   onSave,
 22:   className,
 23:   textClassName,
 24:   editRef,
 25: }) => {
 26:   const [isEditing, setIsEditing] = React.useState(false);
 27:   const [editValue, setEditValue] = React.useState(value);
 28:   const [isSaving, setIsSaving] = React.useState(false);
 29:   const onApiError = useApiErrorHandler();
 30: 
 31:   React.useEffect(() => {
 32:     setEditValue(value);
 33:   }, [value]);
 34: 
 35:   React.useImperativeHandle(
 36:     editRef,
 37:     () => ({
 38:       startEditing: () => setIsEditing(true),
 39:     }),
 40:     [],
 41:   );
 42: 
 43:   if (isEditing)
 44:     return (
 45:       <div className={cn("space-y-2", className)}>
 46:         <Textarea
 47:           value={editValue}
 48:           onChange={(e) => setEditValue(e.target.value)}
 49:           className="min-h-[100px]"
 50:           disabled={isSaving}
 51:         />
 52:         <div className="flex gap-2 justify-end">
 53:           <Button
 54:             variant="outline"
 55:             size="sm"
 56:             onClick={() => {
 57:               setEditValue(value);
 58:               setIsEditing(false);
 59:             }}
 60:             disabled={isSaving}
 61:           >
 62:             Cancel
 63:           </Button>
 64:           <Button
 65:             size="sm"
 66:             onClick={async () => {
 67:               if (editValue === value) {
 68:                 setIsEditing(false);
 69:                 return;
 70:               }
 71: 
 72:               setIsSaving(true);
 73:               try {
 74:                 await onSave(editValue);
 75:                 setIsEditing(false);
 76:               } catch (error) {
 77:                 console.error("Failed to save");
 78:                 onApiError(error);
 79:               } finally {
 80:                 setIsSaving(false);
 81:               }
 82:             }}
 83:             disabled={isSaving}
 84:           >
 85:             {isSaving ? "Saving..." : "Save"}
 86:           </Button>
 87:         </div>
 88:       </div>
 89:     );
 90: 
 91:   return (
 92:     <div
 93:       className={cn(
 94:         "group cursor-pointer hover:opacity-80 transition-opacity",
 95:         className,
 96:       )}
 97:       onClick={() => setIsEditing(true)}
 98:     >
 99:       <p className={cn("text-muted-foreground", textClassName)}>{value}</p>
100:     </div>
101:   );
102: };
`````

 1: import { useState } from "react";

 5: export function SignInWithPassword({
 6:   onModeChange,
 7: }: {
 8:   onModeChange?: (mode: "signIn" | "signUp") => void;
 9: }) {
10:   const { signIn } = useAuthActions();
11:   const [step, setStep] = useState<"signUp" | "signIn">("signIn");
12: 
13:   const toggleStep = (newStep: "signUp" | "signIn") => {

17:

22:         className="flex flex-col gap-4"
23:         onSubmit={async (e) => {
24:           e.preventDefault();
25:           const formData = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
26:           await signIn("password", formData);
27:         }}
28:       >
29:         <input
30:           name="email"
31:           type="email"
32:           placeholder="Email"
33:           required
34:           className="p-2 border rounded bg-background"
35:         />
36:         <input
37:           name="password"
38:           type="password"
39:           placeholder="Password"
40:           required
41:           className="p-2 border rounded bg-background"
42:         />
43:         <input name="flow" type="hidden" value={step} />
44:         <div className="flex flex-col gap-2">
45:           <Button type="submit" className="w-full">
46:             {step === "signIn" ? "Sign in" : "Sign up"}
47:           </Button>
48:           <Button
49:             type="button"
50:             variant="ghost"
51:             className="text-sm"
52:             onClick={() => toggleStep(step === "signIn" ? "signUp" : "signIn")}
53:           >
54:             {step === "signIn"
55:               ? "Don't have an account? Sign up"
56:               : "Already have an account? Sign in"}
57:           </Button>
58:         </div>
59:       </form>
60:     </div>
61:   );
62: }

 91: <script>
 92:   function initializeQuizzes() {
 93:     document.querySelectorAll('.quiz-block').forEach(quizBlock => {
 94:       const quizData = JSON.parse(quizBlock.getAttribute('data-quiz') || '{}');
 95:       const checkButton = quizBlock.querySelector('.quiz-check');
 96:       const resetButton = quizBlock.querySelector('.quiz-reset');
 97:       let selectedAnswers = new Array(quizData.questions.length).fill(-1);
 98:       let showingResults = false;
 99: 
100:       // Handle option selection
101:       quizBlock.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(option => {
102:         option.addEventListener('click', () => {
103:           if (showingResults) return;
104:           
105:           const questionIndex = (option.closest('.quiz-question') as HTMLElement)?.dataset.index;
106:           const optionIndex = (option as HTMLElement).dataset.index;
107:           
108:           if (questionIndex !== undefined && optionIndex !== undefined) {
109:             selectedAnswers[parseInt(questionIndex)] = parseInt(optionIndex);
110:             
111:             // Update UI
112:             const questionDiv = option.closest('.quiz-question');
113:             questionDiv?.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(opt => {
114:               opt.classList.remove('bg-primary', 'text-primary-foreground');
115:             });
116:             option.classList.add('bg-primary', 'text-primary-foreground');
117:           }
118:         });
119:       });
120: 
121:       // Handle check answers
122:       checkButton?.addEventListener('click', () => {
123:         if (selectedAnswers.includes(-1)) return;
124:         showingResults = true;
125:         
126:         quizBlock.querySelectorAll('.quiz-question').forEach((question, qIndex) => {
127:           const selected = selectedAnswers[qIndex];
128:           const correct = quizData.questions[qIndex].correctAnswer;
129:           
130:           question.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach((option, oIndex) => {
131:             if (oIndex === correct) {
132:               option.classList.add('bg-green-500', 'text-white');
133:             } else if (oIndex === selected) {
134:               option.classList.add('bg-red-500', 'text-white');
135:             }
136:           });
137:           
138:           question.querySelector('.quiz-explanation')?.classList.remove('hidden');
139:         });
140:         
141:         checkButton.classList.add('hidden');
142:         resetButton?.classList.remove('hidden');
143:       });
144: 
145:       // Handle reset
146:       resetButton?.addEventListener('click', () => {
147:         showingResults = false;
148:         selectedAnswers = new Array(quizData.questions.length).fill(-1);
149:         
150:         quizBlock.querySelectorAll('.quiz-option').forEach(option => {
151:           option.classList.remove(
152:             'bg-primary', 'text-primary-foreground',
153:             'bg-green-500', 'bg-red-500', 'text-white'
154:           );
155:         });
156:         
157:         quizBlock.querySelectorAll('.quiz-explanation').forEach(exp => {
158:           exp.classList.add('hidden');
159:         });
160:         
161:         checkButton?.classList.remove('hidden');
162:         resetButton?.classList.add('hidden');
163:       });
164:     });
165:   }
166: 
167:   // Initialize quizzes when the page loads
168:   document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initializeQuizzes);
169: </script>
`````

  1: import { type LessonContent } from '@/schema/lesson';
  2: import { VideoEmbed } from './VideoEmbed';

  4: import {
  5:   Accordion,

  7:   AccordionItem,
  8:   AccordionTrigger,
  9: } from "@/components/ui/accordion";

 11: import { useState } from 'react';
 12: 
 13: interface LessonContentProps {
 14:   content: LessonContent;
 15: }
 16: 
 17: export function LessonContent({ content }: LessonContentProps) {
 18:   return (
 19:     <div className="space-y-8">
 20:       {content.map((block, index) => {
 21:         switch (block.type) {
 22:           case 'video':
 23:             return (
 24:               <VideoEmbed
 25:                 key={index}
 26:                 id={block.id}
 27:                 title={block.title}
 28:                 description={block.description}
 29:                 timestamp={block.timestamp}
 30:                 params={block.params}
 31:               />
 32:             );
 33: 
 34:           case 'text':
 35:             return (
 36:               <Card key={index} className="p-6">
 37:                 {block.title && (
 38:                   <h3 className="text-xl font-semibold mb-4">{block.title}</h3>
 39:                 )}
 40:                 <div className="prose dark:prose-invert max-w-none">
 41:                   {block.content}
 42:                 </div>
 43:               </Card>
 44:             );
 45: 
 46:           case 'quiz':
 47:             return <QuizBlock key={index} quiz={block} />;
 48:         }
 49:       })}
 50:     </div>
 51:   );
 52: }
 53: 
 54: function QuizBlock({ quiz }: { quiz: Extract<LessonContent[number], { type: 'quiz' }> }) {
 55:   const [selectedAnswers, setSelectedAnswers] = useState<number[]>(
 56:     new Array(quiz.questions.length).fill(-1)
 57:   );
 58:   const [showResults, setShowResults] = useState(false);
 59: 
 60:   const handleAnswerSelect = (questionIndex: number, answerIndex: number) => {
 61:     const newAnswers = [...selectedAnswers];
 62:     newAnswers[questionIndex] = answerIndex;
 63:     setSelectedAnswers(newAnswers);
 64:   };
 65: 
 66:   const checkAnswers = () => {
 67:     setShowResults(true);
 68:   };
 69: 
 70:   const resetQuiz = () => {
 71:     setSelectedAnswers(new Array(quiz.questions.length).fill(-1));
 72:     setShowResults(false);
 73:   };
 74: 
 75:   return (
 76:     <Card className="p-6">
 77:       <h3 className="text-xl font-semibold mb-2">{quiz.title}</h3>
 78:       {quiz.description && (
 79:         <p className="text-muted-foreground mb-6">{quiz.description}</p>
 80:       )}
 81: 
 82:       <Accordion type="single" collapsible className="w-full">
 83:         {quiz.questions.map((question, qIndex) => (
 84:           <AccordionItem key={qIndex} value={`q-${qIndex}`}>
 85:             <AccordionTrigger className="text-left">
 86:               <span className="font-medium">
 87:                 Question {qIndex + 1}: {question.question}
 88:               </span>
 89:             </AccordionTrigger>
 90:             <AccordionContent>
 91:               <div className="space-y-4 pt-4">
 92:                 {question.options.map((option, oIndex) => (
 93:                   <Button
 94:                     key={oIndex}
 95:                     variant={
 96:                       showResults
 97:                         ? oIndex === question.correctAnswer
 98:                           ? 'default'
 99:                           : selectedAnswers[qIndex] === oIndex
100:                           ? 'destructive'
101:                           : 'outline'
102:                         : selectedAnswers[qIndex] === oIndex
103:                         ? 'default'
104:                         : 'outline'
105:                     }
106:                     className="w-full justify-start"
107:                     onClick={() => !showResults && handleAnswerSelect(qIndex, oIndex)}
108:                   >
109:                     {option}
110:                   </Button>
111:                 ))}
112:                 {showResults && question.explanation && (
113:                   <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground mt-4">
114:                     {question.explanation}
115:                   </p>
116:                 )}
117:               </div>
118:             </AccordionContent>
119:           </AccordionItem>
120:         ))}
121:       </Accordion>
122: 
123:       <div className="mt-6 flex gap-4">
124:         <Button
125:           onClick={checkAnswers}
126:           disabled={selectedAnswers.includes(-1) || showResults}
127:         >
128:           Check Answers
129:         </Button>
130:         {showResults && (
131:           <Button variant="outline" onClick={resetQuiz}>
132:             Try Again
133:           </Button>
134:         )}
135:       </div>
136:     </Card>
137:   );
138: }
`````

## File: src/components/CountdownTimer.tsx
`````typescript
 1: 'use client';
 2: 
 3: import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
 4: 
 5: interface CountdownTimerProps {
 6:   targetDate: Date | string | number;
 7:   className?: string;
 8:   onComplete?: () => void;
 9: }
10: 
11: export function CountdownTimer({ targetDate, className = '', onComplete }: CountdownTimerProps) {
12:   const [timeLeft, setTimeLeft] = useState({ days: 0, hours: 0, minutes: 0, seconds: 0 });
13: 
14:   useEffect(() => {
15:     const updateCountdown = () => {
16:       try {
17:         const endDate = new Date(targetDate);
18:         const now = new Date();
19: 
20:         // Add debug logging
21:         console.log('Target date:', endDate, 'Now:', now);
22: 
23:         // Calculate the difference in milliseconds
24:         let difference = endDate.getTime() - now.getTime();
25:         console.log('Time difference (ms):', difference);
26: 
27:         // If countdown is finished
28:         if (difference <= 0) {
29:           setTimeLeft({ days: 0, hours: 0, minutes: 0, seconds: 0 });
30:           if (onComplete) onComplete();
31:           return;
32:         }
33: 
34:         // Calculate all units
35:         const days = Math.floor(difference / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24));
36:         difference -= days * (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
37: 
38:         const hours = Math.floor(difference / (1000 * 60 * 60));
39:         difference -= hours * (1000 * 60 * 60);
40: 
41:         const minutes = Math.floor(difference / (1000 * 60));
42:         difference -= minutes * (1000 * 60);
43: 
44:         const seconds = Math.floor(difference / 1000);
45: 
46:         setTimeLeft({ days, hours, minutes, seconds });
47:       } catch (error) {
48:         console.error('Error updating countdown:', error);
49:       }
50:     };
51: 
52:     // Update immediately and then every second
53:     updateCountdown();
54:     const interval = setInterval(updateCountdown, 1000);
55: 
56:     // Cleanup on unmount
57:     return () => clearInterval(interval);
58:   }, [targetDate, onComplete]);
59: 
60:   const timeUnits = [
61:     { value: timeLeft.days, label: 'Days' },
62:     { value: timeLeft.hours, label: 'Hours' },
63:     { value: timeLeft.minutes, label: 'Minutes' },
64:     { value: timeLeft.seconds, label: 'Seconds' }
65:   ];
66: 
67:   return (
68:     <div className={`inline-flex items-center justify-center gap-2 ${className}`}>
69:       {timeUnits.map((unit, index) => (
70:         <div key={unit.label} className="flex items-center">
71:           <div className="bg-[#1a1a1a] px-6 py-4 rounded-lg text-center min-w-[120px]">
72:             <div className="text-3xl font-bold text-white">{unit.value.toString().padStart(2, '0')}</div>
73:             <div className="text-sm text-[#aaaaaa] uppercase tracking-wide">{unit.label}</div>
74:           </div>
75:           {index < timeUnits.length - 1 && (
76:             <div className="text-3xl font-bold text-white mx-3">:</div>
77:           )}
78:         </div>
79:       ))}
80:     </div>
81:   );
82: }
`````

174:                     </a>

180:         </section>
181:       </div>
182:     )
183:   },
184: )
185: HeroSection.displayName = "HeroSection"
186: 
187: export { HeroSection }
`````

169:                 </button>
170:               </div>
171:             </div>
172:           </header>
173:           <main
174:             className="flex-1 overflow-hidden mx-auto w-full max-w-[850px] right-panel-bg"
175:           >
176:             {hydratedChatConfig && (
177:               <Chat
178:                 className="right-panel-bg"

180:                 key={JSON.stringify(hydratedChatConfig.welcome)}
181:               />
182:             )}
183:           </main>
184:         </div>
185:       )}
186:     </div>
187:   );
188: };

190: Right.displayName = "Right";

## File: src/components/SmoothScroll.tsx
`````typescript
 1: import { useEffect } from 'react';
 2: 
 3: export function SmoothScroll() {
 4:   useEffect(() => {
 5:     const handleSmoothScroll = (e: Event) => {
 6:       if (!(e instanceof MouseEvent)) return;
 7:       const target = e.target;
 8:       if (!(target instanceof HTMLAnchorElement) || !target.hash) return;
 9: 
10:       e.preventDefault();
11:       const targetElement = document.querySelector(target.hash);
12:       if (!targetElement) return;
13: 
14:       const targetPosition = targetElement.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY;
15:       const startPosition = window.scrollY;
16:       const distance = targetPosition - startPosition;
17:       const duration = 1500;
18:       let start: number | null = null;
19: 
20:       function animation(currentTime: number): void {
21:         if (start === null) start = currentTime;
22:         const timeElapsed = currentTime - start;
23:         const progress = Math.min(timeElapsed / duration, 1);
24: 
25: 
26:         const ease = (t: number): number =>
27:           t < .5 ? 4 * t * t * t : (t - 1) * (2 * t - 2) * (2 * t - 2) + 1;
28: 
29:         window.scrollTo(0, startPosition + distance * ease(progress));
30: 
31:         if (timeElapsed < duration) {
32:           requestAnimationFrame(animation);
33:         }
34:       }
35: 
36:       requestAnimationFrame(animation);
37:     };
38: 
39:     document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]').forEach(anchor => {
40:       anchor.addEventListener('click', handleSmoothScroll);
41:     });
42: 
43:     return () => {
44:       document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="#"]').forEach(anchor => {
45:         anchor.removeEventListener('click', handleSmoothScroll);
46:       });
47:     };
48:   }, []);
49: 
50:   return null;
51: }
`````

## File: src/content/docs/adapters/langchain.mdx
`````
 1: ---
 2: title: LangChain
 3: description: Learn how to use LangChain with the AI SDK.
 4: status: public
 5: tags: ['langchain', 'adapter', 'integration', 'llm', 'rag']
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: # LangChain
 9: 
10: [LangChain](https://js.langchain.com/docs/) is your Swiss Army knife for building AI-powered apps. It's packed with features for working with language models, creating agents, managing vector stores, and implementing retrieval augmented generation (RAG). But here's the catch - it doesn't handle UI stuff or streaming data to the client out of the box. That's where we come in! 
11: 
12: ## Quick Example: Completion
13: 
14: ```ts
15: // api/completion/route.ts
16: import { ChatOpenAI } from '@langchain/openai';
17: import { LangChainAdapter } from 'ai';
18: 
19: export const maxDuration = 60;
20: 
21: export async function POST(req: Request) {
22:   const { prompt } = await req.json();
23: 
24:   const model = new ChatOpenAI({
25:     model: 'gpt-3.5-turbo-0125',
26:     temperature: 0,
27:   });
28: 
29:   const stream = await model.stream(prompt);
30: 
31:   return LangChainAdapter.toDataStreamResponse(stream);
32: }
33: ```
34: 
35: For the frontend, you'll want to hook this up to your UI using our handy `useCompletion` hook.
`````

## File: src/content/docs/adapters/llamaindex.mdx
`````
 1: ---
 2: title: LlamaIndex
 3: description: Learn how to use LlamaIndex with the AI SDK.
 4: status: public
 5: tags: ['llamaindex', 'adapter', 'integration', 'data-indexing', 'rag']
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: # LlamaIndex
 9: 
10: 🦙 Meet your new best friend in data wrangling! [LlamaIndex](https://ts.llamaindex.ai/) is like a super-smart librarian for your LLM applications. It helps you organize, structure, and access your private or domain-specific data with style. And guess what? LlamaIndex.TS brings all that Python goodness to JavaScript land!
11: 
12: ## Supported Environments
13: - Node.js (Rock-solid official support) ✨
14: - Vercel Edge Functions (Experimental but exciting!) 🚀
15: - Deno (Also experimental, but living on the edge is fun!) 🦕
16: 
17: ## Quick Example: Completion
18: 
19: Let's see this llama in action! Here's how to combine the AI SDK and LlamaIndex.
20: 
21: 
22: ```ts
23: // api/completion/route.ts
24: import { OpenAI, SimpleChatEngine } from 'llamaindex';
25: import { LlamaIndexAdapter } from 'ai';
26: 
27: export const maxDuration = 60;
28: 
29: export async function POST(req: Request) {
30:   const { prompt } = await req.json();
31: 
32:   const llm = new OpenAI({ model: 'gpt-4o' });
33:   const chatEngine = new SimpleChatEngine({ llm });
34: 
35:   const stream = await chatEngine.chat({
36:     message: prompt,
37:     stream: true,
38:   });
39: 
40:   return LlamaIndexAdapter.toDataStreamResponse(stream);
41: }
42: ```
43: 
44: For the frontend piece, you'll want to use our completion hook.
`````

## File: src/content/docs/ai-sdk/01-overview.mdx
`````
 1: ---
 2: title: Overview
 3: description: An overview of foundational concepts critical to understanding the AI SDK
 4: status: public
 5: tags: ["AI", "LLM", "embeddings", "generative-ai", "concepts"]
 6: ---
 7: 
 8: # Overview
 9: 
10: The AI SDK standardizes integrating artificial intelligence (AI) models across supported providers. This enables developers to focus on building great AI applications, not waste time on technical details.
11: 
12: For example, here's how you can generate text with various models using the AI SDK:
13: 
14: To effectively leverage the AI SDK, it helps to familiarize yourself with the following concepts:
15: 
16: ## Generative Artificial Intelligence
17: 
18: **Generative artificial intelligence** refers to models that predict and generate various types of outputs (such as text, images, or audio) based on what's statistically likely, pulling from patterns they've learned from their training data. For example:
19: 
20: - Given a photo, a generative model can generate a caption.
21: - Given an audio file, a generative model can generate a transcription.
22: - Given a text description, a generative model can generate an image.
23: 
24: ## Large Language Models
25: 
26: A **large language model (LLM)** is a subset of generative models focused primarily on **text**. An LLM takes a sequence of words as input and aims to predict the most likely sequence to follow. It assigns probabilities to potential next sequences and then selects one. The model continues to generate sequences until it meets a specified stopping criterion.
27: 
28: LLMs learn by training on massive collections of written text, which means they will be better suited to some use cases than others. For example, a model trained on GitHub data would understand the probabilities of sequences in source code particularly well.
29: 
30: However, it's crucial to understand LLMs' limitations. When asked about less known or absent information, like the birthday of a personal relative, LLMs might "hallucinate" or make up information. It's essential to consider how well-represented the information you need is in the model.
31: 
32: ## Embedding Models
33: 
34: An **embedding model** is used to convert complex data (like words or images) into a dense vector (a list of numbers) representation, known as an embedding. Unlike generative models, embedding models do not generate new text or data. Instead, they provide representations of semantic and syntactic relationships between entities that can be used as input for other models or other natural language processing tasks.
35: 
36: In the next section, you will learn about the difference between models providers and models, and which ones are available in the AI SDK.
`````

  7: 
  8: # Providers and Models
  9: 
 10: Companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic (providers) offer access to a range of large language models (LLMs) with differing strengths and capabilities through their own APIs.
 11: 
 12: Each provider typically has its own unique method for interfacing with their models, complicating the process of switching providers and increasing the risk of vendor lock-in.
 13: 
 14: To solve these challenges, AI SDK Core offers a standardized approach to interacting with LLMs through a language model specification that abstracts differences between providers. This unified interface allows you to switch between providers with ease while using the same API for all providers.
 15: 
 16: Here is an overview of the AI SDK Providers:
 17: 
 18: ## AI SDK Providers
 19: 
 20: The AI SDK comes with a wide range of providers that you can use to interact with different language models:
 21: 
 22: - OpenAI Provider (`@ai-sdk/openai`)
 23: - Azure OpenAI Provider (`@ai-sdk/azure`)
 24: - Anthropic Provider (`@ai-sdk/anthropic`)
 25: - Amazon Bedrock Provider (`@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock`)
 26: - Google Generative AI Provider (`@ai-sdk/google`)
 27: - Google Vertex Provider (`@ai-sdk/google-vertex`)
 28: - Mistral Provider (`@ai-sdk/mistral`)
 29: - xAI Grok Provider (`@ai-sdk/xai`)
 30: - Together.ai Provider (`@ai-sdk/togetherai`)
 31: - Cohere Provider (`@ai-sdk/cohere`)
 32: - Fireworks Provider (`@ai-sdk/fireworks`)
 33: - DeepInfra Provider (`@ai-sdk/deepinfra`)
 34: - DeepSeek Provider (`@ai-sdk/deepseek`)
 35: - Cerebras Provider (`@ai-sdk/cerebras`)
 36: - Groq Provider (`@ai-sdk/groq`)
 37: - Perplexity Provider (`@ai-sdk/perplexity`)
 38: 
 39: You can also use the OpenAI Compatible provider with OpenAI-compatible APIs:
 40: 
 41: - LM Studio
 42: - Baseten
 43: 
 44: Our language model specification is published as an open-source package, which you can use to create custom providers.
 45: 
 46: The open-source community has created the following providers:

 61:
